author: zkochan
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `packageManager` delegation failure that broke the [Update Lockfile run 29134436655](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/actions/runs/29134436655/job/86495886559): any delegation from an installed v12 binary to a *different* v12 version aborted with `the native pnpm binary at … resolves outside …`.

The global virtual store lays engine slots out as `links/<scope>/<name>/<version>/<hash>`, with a literal `@` placeholder as the scope segment of unscoped packages (see `format_global_virtual_store_path`). `global_virtual_store_root_from_slot` walked the slot path upward without knowing about that placeholder, so for the unscoped `pnpm` wrapper it landed on `@` where it expected `links` and returned `None`; `native_source_trust_root` then fell back to the wrapper's own slot as the trust root. Since the wrapper's `@pnpm/exe.<target>` platform package is a symlink into a *sibling* slot under `links`, `validate_native_binary_source` rejected a perfectly healthy install. Scoped wrappers (`@pnpm/exe`) happened to walk correctly, which is why only the unscoped `pnpm` wrapper — i.e. exactly the v12 delegation path — was affected.

The fix re-derives the slot's `links`-relative path with `format_global_virtual_store_path` — the same formatter that laid the slot out — so the reader and writer of the layout can't drift again. The symlink-escape guard is unchanged: a platform package resolving outside `links` is still rejected (covered by a new test).

Note for maintainers: released alpha.6/alpha.7 binaries still carry the bug and the *old* binary performs the delegation, so CI jobs remain broken until the `packageManager` pin and the installed setup version match again (and permanently once a fixed release is the installed binary).

## Squash Commit Body

```text
The global virtual store lays slots out as
links/<scope>/<name>/<version>/<hash>, with a literal @ placeholder as the
scope segment of unscoped packages (see format_global_virtual_store_path).
global_virtual_store_root_from_slot walked the slot path upward without
that placeholder, so for the unscoped pnpm wrapper it landed on @ where it
expected links, gave up, and native_source_trust_root fell back to the
wrapper's own slot. The wrapper's @pnpm/exe.<target> platform package is a
symlink to a sibling slot under links, so linking the native binary then
failed with "the native pnpm binary ... resolves outside ...". This is
exactly the packageManager-delegation path: any delegation to a different
v12 version aborted, which broke the Update Lockfile workflow after its
updater bumped the pin mid-job.

Derive the slot's links-relative path with format_global_virtual_store_path
- the formatter that laid the slot out - instead of a hand-rolled walk, so
the reader and writer of the layout cannot drift again. Scoped wrappers
resolved to the links root before and still do, and a platform-package
symlink escaping links entirely is still rejected.
```

## Checklist

- [x] The change is implemented in both the TypeScript CLI and the Rust
  `pnpm/` port, or the description notes what still needs porting. *(Rust-only: the trust-root containment check is pacquet-only hardening; the TypeScript `linkExePlatformBinary` has no such check, so there is nothing to mirror.)*
- [x] Added or updated tests. *(Regression test verified to fail against the previous walk; plus a scoped-wrapper test and a symlink-escape test guarding the security check.)*

author: jpsoaresxy
body:
## Status

**READY**

## Summary

Implements issue #46: removes the last mock data from the dashboard and adds the "loading/error states" polish pass.

Stacked on `45-demo-scenario-buttons` (PR #111, open) since both touch `page.tsx`.

**Wired to real endpoints (1st criterion):**
- `useLiveSession` now hydrates idle-state data from `GET /status` (current activity/immobility/decision) and `GET /alerts` (recent alert history) on mount — previously-unconsumed endpoints. Before this, the hero card fell back to `dashboard/src/lib/scenarios.ts`'s canned mock object (`scenarios.idle`, fabricated timestamps and copy) whenever no live session was running.
- Clicking a demo button no longer flips the card to a fabricated "fall"/"false_positive" preview. The button's own "Running…" label was already real (driven by `isRunning`), so removing the card's fake preview loses no genuine feedback — the card now only ever shows real data or an honest empty state, arriving within a few seconds via the same SSE pipeline built in #42–#45. This let `scenario`/`mockState`/the `?scenario=` deep-link be deleted outright.
- The header's `SignalStatusBadge` is repurposed from 100%-fabricated sensor-quality copy ("Signal: Strong", "3 sensors reporting" — no backend concept for this exists at all) to the real `EventSource` connection status ("Connect" while connecting, "Connected" once open), via the stream's own `onopen`/`onerror`.

**Polish (2nd criterion):** the empty states above (no fabricated demo copy while nothing has happened yet) double as the loading-state treatment — the fetches are fast and the empty state is itself an honest rendering, not a placeholder to hide. Errors from the initial `/status` fetch are logged via `console.error` (matching the pattern already established in #45), consistent with the rest of the app's minimal-chrome error handling.

**Not actionable (3rd criterion):** "verified against the public demo deploy" — `README.md`'s own Demo section says "Live public demo: coming soon," no deployed URL exists yet. Verified instead against the same throwaway fixture SSE server used throughout #42–#45.

**Found and fixed during self-review:** reusing the existing `hasSeenSessionEventRef` guard (from #45) to re-arm a post-session REST refresh — added so the decision log picks up an alert the session may have just persisted, instead of going stale until reload — reintroduced the exact stale-fetch race that guard was built to prevent. A single boolean can't distinguish *which* hydration call is stale across repeated session start/end cycles. Replaced with a generation counter: bumped on every session-boundary SSE event, captured by each hydration call at invocation, checked at resolution — any response from an invalidated generation is discarded.

Also cleaned up during review: removed a redundant `isStarting` state in `page.tsx` (`pendingScenario` alone already covers the click-to-resolution window — simpler and actually closes a small gap the old two-state version had), deduplicated the `/status`+`/alerts` fetch/parse skeleton into a small `fetchJson` helper, shared the alert→`Notification` mapping between the REST-hydration and SSE-live paths, and exported `ConnectionStatus` from one place instead of declaring it twice.

## Type of change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️  Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️  Chore

## Changes

- `dashboard/src/lib/scenarios.ts` — deleted `scenarios`, `ScenarioKey`, `ScenarioState`, `baseNotifications`; kept `activityLabel`, `DEMO_ELDERLY_PROFILE`, and the plain types still used elsewhere.
- `dashboard/src/lib/use-live-session.ts` — added `hydrateFromRest()` (GET /status + GET /alerts), a generation-counter guard replacing the old sticky boolean, `connectionStatus` tracked via `EventSource.onopen`/`onerror`, a shared `fetchJson`/`alertToNotification` helper.
- `dashboard/src/components/signal-status-badge.tsx` — `quality` prop (fake) → `connectionStatus` (real), imported from `use-live-session.ts` instead of redeclared.
- `dashboard/src/app/page.tsx` — removed the mock preview and deep-link entirely; added honest empty states for null activity/decision/timeline; simplified the demo-button state machine (dropped the redundant `isStarting`).

## Testing

### Steps

1. Extended the same throwaway fixture SSE server used for #42–#45 with `GET /alerts` (canned alert list) and a richer `GET /status` (real `current_activity`/`immobility_duration_seconds`/`last_decision` fields, previously only `stream_active`).
2. `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:<fixture-port> npm run dev`, verified in a real browser (Playwright): fresh idle load shows real alert history + "Connect"→"Connected" badge + honest empty activity/timeline; clicking a button shows no fake preview, just "Running…" immediately followed by real data within seconds; the clicked button's specific label persists for the whole run; after `done`, buttons re-enable and the decision log re-hydrates with real data instead of staying stuck on the empty-state copy.
3. `npm run build && npm run lint`.

### Results

- All flows above verified visually, zero console errors across repeated runs (including the specific race-condition regression found and fixed before this commit).
- `npm run build` / `npm run lint` — clean.

### Regressions

- None; Motion (#42) and the underlying SSE event handling (#43/#44) are untouched — this PR only changes what happens before/after a live session and how the demo buttons kick one off. Full self/code-review pass (8 finder angles) surfaced 3 findings, all fixed before this commit.

## Checklist

- [x] **Scope**: The referenced issue (#46) is addressed; the public-deploy criterion is explicitly called out as not yet actionable rather than silently skipped.
- [x] **Compatibility**: Builds on #45's real `/stream/start` wiring; no other consumer depends on the removed mock exports.
- [x] **Documentation**: N/A — no new env vars or config.
- [x] **Testing**: Build, lint, and manual browser verification against a real event-shaped fixture stream, including the specific race that caused the regression found during review.
- [x] **Commits**: Single commit, conventional message, no fixup commits.

body:
Follow-up to the 2026-07-10 14-agent parallel verification ([DEEP-INSIGHT-2026-07-10](docs/insight/DEEP-INSIGHT-2026-07-10-parallel-verified.md)). Four atomic commits, each TDD (RED → GREEN) and adversarially reviewed (4-dimension workflow — the review caught that the breaker fix's first cut was incomplete and it was extended in a second pass).

## What lands

- **`fix(breaker)` (02d2253)** — under `SCRAPY_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED`, MQ per-message ack tokens were silently lost: `_pop_with_ack` inspected the proxy CLASS (which resolved `pop_with_ack` to the ABC default via MRO) → called `backend.pop()` → `token=None`. Two-part fix: `pop_with_ack` added to `_HOT_PATH` + `queue.py` unwraps the proxy. **Fixes #27.**
- **`feat(scheduler)` (74a76a3)** — `_warn_strategy_mq_ack_bypass` logs a WARNING at `from_settings` when a non-passthrough strategy pairs with a `requires_ack` backend (7 strategies × 5 MQ = 35 misconfig combinations). Parametrized over 9 cases. **References #28** (warning landed; the deeper token-aware-strategies fix remains a follow-up).
- **`fix(spider_mixin)` (1cf46d0)** — `setup_backend` now acquires via `ConnectionManager.get_manager` (the singleton registry) instead of constructing directly. Sharing test proves two spiders co-locate on one manager. **References #29** (get_manager landed; `from_settings` routing for the getters deferred — needs a crawler-less fallback design).
- **`docs` (c61516b)** — §3.2/§3.4 ack model collapsed 3→2 buckets (SQS/Pulsar are per-message-ack, not single-slot); metrics synced; new verified risk register; `QueueBackend` ABC docstring corrected. **References #26** (docstring done; `scheduler.py:408` error message still stale).

## Issue triage
- Fixes #27 (clean full fix)
- References #26, #28, #29 (partial — each has a checked + unchecked item)
- See #30 (ES `StorageError`/`ttl()`), #31 (undocumented failure modes umbrella) — related, not addressed here

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest -q` → **1989 passed / 37 skipped** (+17 vs the 1972 baseline)
- [x] `uv run pytest --cov=scrapy_extension` → **99.42%** (95% floor)
- [x] `uv run ruff check src/ tests/` → `All checks passed!`
- [x] `uv run mypy src/scrapy_extension` → `Success: no issues found in 71 source files` (--strict)
- [x] Each new test proven RED before its fix, GREEN after (verified via git-stash revert during the adversarial review)
- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] Real-broker round-trip with breaker ON (mock-only in unit suite; integration deselected) — follow-up

## Out of scope (tracked)
- #29 `from_settings` routing for `get_queue/get_dupefilter/get_scheduler` (design decision)
- #30 ES `StorageError` wrap + `ttl()` contract unification
- #31 WorkStealing/DynamoDB/Memcached/RocketMQ failure-mode cluster

## Summary by Sourcery

强化 MQ 确认（ack）处理以及调度器/爬虫的集成路径，并更新文档，以反映修正后的双桶 ack 模型以及近期的验证结果。

Bug 修复：
- 确保被熔断器包装的队列后端仍然使用其 `pop_with_ack` 重写方法，从而保留逐消息的 ack token，并让熔断器状态能够反映 `pop_with_ack` 的失败。
- 调整 `BackendQueue._pop_with_ack`，在检测后端对 `pop_with_ack` 的重写时拆解熔断器代理，以便在启用 `SCRAPY_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED` 时 MQ ack token 得以保留。
- 更新 `BackendSpiderMixin.setup_backend`，通过单例注册表访问器获取 `ConnectionManager` 而不是直接构造它，从而恢复共享的、基于引用计数的连接管理。

增强功能：
- 当为需要确认（ack）的后端配置非直通队列策略时，添加调度器警告，以暴露由策略导致的 MQ ack 绕过风险。
- 扩展熔断器队列代理语义，将 `pop_with_ack` 视为热点路径操作，确保 MQ ack-pop 流量完全参与熔断器保护和可观测性。

文档：
- 修订深度洞察文档，将 ack 模型从三桶收敛为两桶，澄清所有捆绑的 MQ 后端均为逐消息确认且并发安全，记录策略×MQ ack 的注意事项，并刷新度量和覆盖率数据。
- 添加经过验证的风险登记文档，记录多智能体深度洞察调查、关键正确性发现及其解决状态。

测试：
- 为被熔断器包装的 MQ 后端以及 `BackendQueue._pop_with_ack` 添加定向测试，以固定 token 保留和熔断器行为，并为调度器警告以及通过 `ConnectionManager` 单例共享的爬虫后端添加测试。

<details>

## Summary by Sourcery

Harden MQ ack handling and scheduler/spider integration paths, and update documentation to reflect the corrected two-bucket ack model and recent verification results.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure queue backends wrapped by the circuit breaker still use their pop_with_ack overrides so per-message ack tokens are preserved and breaker state reflects pop_with_ack failures.
- Adjust BackendQueue._pop_with_ack to unwrap breaker proxies when detecting backend pop_with_ack overrides so MQ ack tokens survive under SCRAPY_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED.
- Update BackendSpiderMixin.setup_backend to acquire ConnectionManager via the singleton registry accessor instead of constructing it directly, restoring shared, refcounted connection management.

Enhancements:
- Add a scheduler warning when non-passthrough queue strategies are configured with backends that require acknowledgements, surfacing strategy-mediated MQ ack bypass risks.
- Extend circuit breaker queue proxy semantics to treat pop_with_ack as a hot-path operation, ensuring MQ ack-pop traffic participates fully in breaker protection and observability.

Documentation:

author: thaynes43
body:
Guards against a bad action my own PR #2018 (Flux-native attribution) could take. **haynesnetwork v0.40.1 was pushed unsigned by another agent; the enforce `verify-haynesnetwork-images` policy correctly blocked it; Flux rolled back (app fine on v0.40.0); the HR is `Stalled=True`** — so the next triage run would have summoned remediate and auto-reverted v0.40.1. That's wrong: a signature/admission block is a build-side fix (sign the image) or a human policy decision — reverting would undo the other agent's work and route around a security control.

`attribute()` now drops admission/policy-blocked HRs from **both** attribution paths up front (`hr_admission_blocked`), so triage never auto-reverts one. The gate still pages the Flux failure for a human. Genuine deploy failures stay auto-remediable. Verified against the live haynesnetwork HR (excluded) and a normal upgrade failure (still remediable).

author: kola0d246
body:
# refactor: restructure to feature-based architecture and implement barrel routing

### 📝 Summary
This PR transitions the frontend application to a highly scalable **feature-based architecture**. Alongside the structural move, the routing system has been completely refactored to utilize barrel files (`index.jsx`) for cleaner imports and implements lazy loading to optimize the public-facing bundle size. 

This sets a stable, clean foundation for our upcoming React Router v7 migration.

### 🛠️ Key Changes
* **Feature-Based Scaffolding:** Reorganized the `src/` directory into isolated feature modules (e.g., `features/events`, `features/gallery`, `features/home`).
* **Barrel Files (`index.jsx`):** Implemented barrel files across all public and admin feature directories to encapsulate components and provide clean import paths (e.g., `import Home from '@/features/home'`).
* **Router Extraction:** Extracted routing logic out of `App.jsx` into a dedicated `src/router.jsx` file. `App.jsx` now strictly acts as a clean top-level provider wrapper.
* **Lazy Loading & Code Splitting:** Implemented `React.lazy` and `<Suspense>` for all `/admin` routes. The build process now successfully splits admin components into separate chunks, ensuring the public site loads instantly without downloading admin-heavy JavaScript.
* **Isolated Admin Login:** Restructured the `/admin/login` route to sit outside the `AdminLayout`, ensuring unauthenticated users do not see the admin sidebar/header while trying to logging in.

### ✅ Pre-Merge Checklist
[x] Code builds successfully (`npm run build`) with no rendering errors.
[x] Verified there are no missing React `key` warnings in the browser console.

--- 
**Note to Reviewers:** 
This PR focuses strictly on structural organization and React component routing optimization. No visual UI or underlying business logic was altered during this refactor.

author: evanharmon1
body:
## Summary

Implements the **harmon-devkit side** of #53 (Tier 1 — manifest-driven pull sync): make this repo the single source of truth for reusable agent skills, and ship a pinned, pull-based vendoring toolkit that consumer repos adopt with `task sync:skills`. A drift check keeps vendored copies from silently rotting against the pinned ref.

Everything here is built, linted, and **tested end-to-end within this repo**. The cross-repo consumer rollout (Lawnomator's manifest, the `DEVKIT_READ_TOKEN` secret, cutting the release tag) can't happen from this repo and is listed as follow-up.

## What's in this PR

**Skill reorganization**
- `ai/skills/` is now grouped into category subdirs: `universal/`, `backend/`, `frontend/`, `infra/`, `mobile/`, `repo/`. The `design/` skills moved into `frontend/`; `repo/` kept as-is. (100% renames — history preserved.)

**Source-of-truth guard** — `scripts/verify-skills.sh` + `task validate:skills`
- Enforces the invariant consumers rely on: **skill directory names unique across categories** (categories are flattened on vendor), plus valid `SKILL.md` frontmatter (`name:` + `description:`, `name:` matching the dir). Drafts/placeholders (no `SKILL.md`) are skipped, not failed.
- yq-free, offline; wired into `task verify`, CI, and the pre-commit hook.

**Vendoring engine** — `scripts/sync-skills.sh` (the copy-paste artifact for consumers)
- `sync` — clones the pinned tag, flattens requested categories into `dest`, guards name collisions, stamps `.SKILLS_PROVENANCE` (source + ref + resolved SHA + do-not-edit marker).
- `verify` — authoritative drift check; re-vendors into a temp dir **outside the repo** and diffs (no working-tree side effects, so no `.gitignore` entry needed).
- `verify-offline` — fast, no-network check that the vendored provenance matches the manifest ref.

**Tests** — `scripts/test-skills.sh` + `task test:skills`
- 23 hermetic, offline assertions over throwaway git fixtures (cloned via `file://`, the same code path as a real remote): guard collision/frontmatter cases; engine sync/flatten/provenance/drift-detect/offline/collision/missing-category; nested `assets/`+`references/` survive vendoring.

**Consumer template** — `templates/skills-sync/`
- Example `.skills-sync.yaml`, `Taskfile.skills.yml` (`sync:skills` / `verify:skills` / `verify:skills:offline`), and an adoption README with the CI job + Lefthook snippets.

**Wiring & docs**
- `Taskfile.yml`: `validate:skills` (→ `validate`) and `test:skills` (→ `verify`).
- `.github/workflows/build.yml`: install `yq`; run `task validate` + `task test:skills`.
- `lefthook.yml`: run `validate:skills` on pre-commit when `ai/skills/**` changes.
- `ai/skills/README.md` (layout, unique-name rule, how to add a skill) + README template-index / AI-assets updates.

## Verification

- `task verify` green (lint + `validate:skills` + `test:skills` 23/23 + existing guards).
- `task security:secrets` — no leaks.
- **Real end-to-end**: vendored this branch's actual skills via `file://` clone — `design-handoff` + `standardize-repo` came across flattened with `assets/`+`references/` intact, drafts skipped, provenance stamped with the resolved SHA; `verify` and `verify-offline` both pass.

## Deliberate deviations from the issue

- **Categories**: kept the issue's `universal/backend/frontend/infra/mobile` **and** the existing `repo/`, moving `design/` skills into `frontend/` (per your steer). The illustrative example skills in the issue don't exist; the real ones are `design-handoff` + `standardize-repo`.
- **Path**: skills stay under `ai/skills/` (this repo's convention), not top-level `skills/`. The engine defaults `source.path` to `ai/skills` (overridable in the manifest).
- **Source-side task naming**: the issue's `verify:skills` means the consumer network drift check; the source-side guard here is `validate:skills` to avoid a name clash. Consumers still get `verify:skills` / `verify:skills:offline` (in the template).
- **No `.skills-sync.verify.tmp/`**: the engine uses `mktemp`, so consumers don't need that `.gitignore` entry.
- Left a stray **untracked** `ai/skills/design/design-handoff.zip` (a regenerable build artifact) in your working tree — not deleted, not committed. Safe to `rm` if unwanted.

## Follow-up (cross-repo, not doable from here)

- Cut a harmon-devkit release/tag that ships the category layout, then pin consumers to it.
- Roll out to consumers: add `.skills-sync.yaml`, run `task sync:skills`, commit vendored skills, add the `skills-drift` CI job + `DEVKIT_READ_TOKEN` secret, add the Lefthook pre-push offline check.
- Phase 2 (deferred by the issue): push-based auto-PR sync, frontmatter linting, package distribution.

Refs #53

author: magicwilliams
body:
## What changed

Takes Tempo from a mock-data shell to a working product running on real HealthKit/Garmin data, with Supabase as the corrected source of truth and Claude behind two Edge Functions (`coach`, `plan`).

### Data layer
- **HealthKit ingest** is insert-only with a second dedupe layer (±5-min start-time window) — Garmin re-exporting workouts under new UUIDs can no longer double-count mileage
- **Supabase `runs` is the read path**: user corrections made in chat survive every re-sync; originals snapshotted for audit
- **HR backfill**: Garmin doesn't associate HR samples with workouts, so new rows are enriched from the time window and a capped repair pass fills recent history
- **Load model** (`Engine/LoadModel.swift`): pace-relative training load → CTL/ATL/form → a real readiness score (check-in can cap it — the athlete's word outranks the math)

### Coach (Edge Function v11)
- Calm-expert persona with the athlete's real runs, plan, fitness, and settings as grounding
- **Write tools with confirm cards**: amend/add runs, plan settings (with full regenerate cascade), single-session adaptations, athlete facts, risk tolerance — the function never writes; the app executes under RLS after the athlete confirms
- Cached per-run takeaways (auto-generated when a run matches today's session), onboarding interview mode, tool-continuation + empty-reply guards

### Plan engine (Edge Function v2)
- Deterministic feature extraction → Claude proposes the plan *shape* in a forced tool schema (phases emerge from the data, no fixed template) → deterministic generator writes weeks/sessions with real paces
- **Create-then-retire**: a mid-flight failure can never destroy the active plan
- Strength prescription (opt-in), Sunday long runs, step-back weeks, taper

### App
- Today: real session card with pre-run check-in gate, coach's read of completed runs, tomorrow preview, tappable readiness → full breakdown screen
- Plan: 2 firm weeks + honest sketch beyond; Progress: live projection vs goal, phase bars; You: real stats/bests/settings, fully tappable
- Run Detail: pace-colored route map (when GPS exists), scrubbable pace+HR overlay, time-in-zone, elevation, splits
- Onboarding: hard-gated Welcome → Connect → coach-led interview, ends with a live plan
- Chat polish: animated typing indicator with busy labels, stateful confirm cards, context-aware quick replies, iMessage-style timestamp reveal

## Why

Beta-of-one build for the 2026 Chicago Marathon block (see `progress.md` for the full decision log and session history). Design principles locked with the user along the way: assessment-driven plans anchored on real volume, user agency over injury-safety paternalism, corrections via conversation, and no paywalled sense-making.

## Reviewer notes
- `supabase/migrations/0002–0005` have already been applied to the live project; Edge Functions `coach` v11 and `plan` v2 are deployed
- The Xcode project is XcodeGen-generated (`ios/project.yml`); `Tempo.xcodeproj` is gitignored — run `xcodegen generate` in `ios/`
- Secrets: `.env` (Anthropic key) is gitignored; the key lives only as a Supabase function secret
- Verified: full build (`BUILD SUCCEEDED`), live smoke tests of both functions, and on-device testing throughout

author: fuddlesworth
body:
## Summary

Implements the request from discussion #745 (reply thread): a window-layer option so floating windows can always stay above tiled windows, like Krohnkite's Window Layer setting.

Adds a new window-domain rule action **SetWindowLayer** carrying a closed `above` / `normal` / `below` enum token. Combined with the existing `IsFloating` / `IsTiled` match fields, the requested behavior is one rule:

> WHEN IsFloating THEN Set window layer: Above other windows

and the Krohnkite fork's default (push tiled windows down instead) is the inverse rule with `IsTiled` and Below.

## How it works

The action is consumed entirely effect-side. `reconcileRuleWindowLayer` resolves the new `window-layer` slot through the existing live rule query (which already carries the floating/tiled/snapped placement facts) and maps the token onto KWin's `keepAbove`/`keepBelow` pair. It rides the same triggers as the title-bar reconcile: window added, the placement-state flush on float/snap flips, and `updateAllDecorations` on rule edits and focus changes. No daemon change, no D-Bus change, and the action is purely additive (no schema migration, older builds drop the unknown action on load).

## Divergences from Krohnkite (deliberate)

Krohnkite's implementation has three lifecycle problems this avoids:

- **It never restores flags.** Disable the script or unmanage a window and the last-committed `keepBelow` sticks forever. Here the pre-rule flag pair is snapshotted on first application and restored when no rule owns the layer any more, with a destructor restore-all so an effect unload can't strand flags on live windows.
- **Stale opposite flag.** Its Above path sets `keepAbove` without clearing `keepBelow` (and vice versa), so an above-to-below transition leaves both set. Here the fully-specified pair is always written from the token.
- **It fights the user.** It re-asserts flags on every layout commit. Here re-asserts happen only on real triggers, and the snapshot is never re-captured under an active rule, so restore always returns the window to the user's own state.

## Scope note

`IsFloating` means explicitly floated (float toggle, Float rule, overflow float), which matches what Krohnkite's option covers. A window PlasmaZones has never managed is not "floating" and will not match.

## Settings UI

body:
## What

Out-of-scope areas (suburbs, Indiana, the lake) now get a subtle slate wash (`#3E4C59` @ 18%) so the app's coverage is visible before a wasted click. Everything outside the City of Chicago is tinted; the city (including the O'Hare corridor) reads clear, and the Norridge/Harwood Heights enclave correctly stays washed.

## How

New **`scope-mask` ENGINE block** (inventory 21 → 22) in the MAP section:

- One world-sized polygon whose even-odd holes are the coverage tiling's **dissolved outline**: ring segments traversed by two features are interior borders and dropped; the survivors are chained back into closed rings. Rendering the raw per-feature rings instead leaves antialiasing hairlines along coincident shared edges — faint gray lines tracing a district layer that isn't toggled on — so the dissolve is the honest rendering; the block falls back to raw rings only if a chain fails to close.
- Draws in its own pane (z 350, between tiles at 200 and overlays at 400) with `pointer-events: none` — every district overlay, highlight, and marker stays on top, and clicks fall through to the map (verified with a real click on a masked suburb).
- Fails silent: the wash is a hint, not data — a boundary-fetch failure skips it, and the owning layer's own error/Retry card surfaces the outage.
- **Fork seam:** `drawOutOfScopeMask(loadCoverageGeometry)` takes the metro's coverage loader as a parameter at the unfenced BOOT call site. Chicago passes `loadSchoolBoardDistricts` — the 20 ERSB districts tile the city exactly and are an offline anchor, so one same-origin fetch serves both the wash and the school-board card.

Honesty framing (in the block comment and playbook): regional layers (county / state / federal) may still resolve under the wash — it marks where *full* coverage ends, never "no data here."

## Docs

- `docs/ENGINE_SYNC.md`: block inventory 21 → 22; notes the loader-as-parameter seam pattern for engine code that needs a per-metro function (the geocoder reconciliation should reuse it).
- `docs/METRO_EXPANSION_PLAYBOOK.md`: §3 checklist step 6 (pick the metro-tiling anchor, hand its loader to `drawOutOfScopeMask`), a §4 bullet with the full fork contract (topology-preserved shared edges required — exact-coordinate cancellation is what the dissolve matches on), and the N.3 NYC worked example.

## Cross-fork status

Born in the NYC fork; this is the reference-tree landing per the ENGINE_SYNC "backport to Chicago first" rule. `check_engine_parity.py --against` the NYC tree (ThursdaysFamous/DistrictExplorer-NYC#15) reports the block byte-identical (1 identical, 0 drifted; the 21 "missing in sibling" are the pre-existing unfenced-NYC drift).

## Testing

- `python3 scripts/check_engine_parity.py index.html` — OK, 22 blocks well formed
- `python3 scripts/validate_index.py index.html` — OK
- Full `smoke_test.mjs` — all 12 checks pass
- Playwright visual pass: mask pane wiring (z-index/pointer-events/even-odd, 6 rings = world + 5 outline), citywide screenshot confirms no interior seams, suburb click still selects a point

author: c0dertang
body:
Closes #188

## What changed
- `src/lib/nav-routes.ts`:
  - Moved `MENU_ROUTES` (`/`, `/dashboard`) here from `nav.tsx` so there is one source of truth shared by `<Nav>` and `isKnownRoute`.
  - Added and exported `isKnownRoute(pathname)`: true for menu routes, back routes (`isBackRoute`), and auth pages (`/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, prefix-matched the same way as back routes to cover Clerk's catch-all steps like `/sign-in/factor-one`). Pure, dependency-free, matches the rest of the module.
  - `/admin` is deliberately in NO route set (documented in the module header): the admin surface is unadvertised and 404s for non-admins (404-not-403 design, issue #175), so the nav must be unable to distinguish `/admin` from a nonexistent path. `/admin` and `/admin/*` render the minimal menu-screen chrome for everyone, admins included (direct-URL ops page — no Back button, no route marker).
- `src/components/nav.tsx`:
  - Imports `MENU_ROUTES` and `isKnownRoute` from `nav-routes.ts` instead of declaring its own local `MENU_ROUTES` set.
  - The minimal-chrome branch condition became `MENU_ROUTES.has(pathname) || !isKnownRoute(pathname)` — unknown routes (404s) now render the exact same minimal chrome (wordmark + auth chip only) as menu screens: no `// ${pathname}` HUD marker, no link bar. Known routes are unaffected — same branch, same JSX, unchanged behavior.
- `src/components/nav/route-back.tsx`: no change. Verified `isBackRoute` already returns `false` for unknown top-level paths (including `/admin` now), so `RouteBack` returns `null` there — nothing to fix.
- `tests/nav-routes.test.ts` (new): covers `isBackRoute` (existing prefixes + subpaths; `/admin` and `/admin/reports` pinned false; `/racecar`/`/settingsX` lookalike-prefix negatives) and `isKnownRoute` (menu routes, back routes + subpaths, auth pages + subpaths, unknown paths, `/admin`/`/admin/reports`/`/admin/anything` pinned false, and `/settingsX`/`/sign-inX`/`/racecar` lookalike-prefix negatives).

## How verified
- `pnpm exec eslint .` — clean.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` — 58 test files, 630 tests, all passed (includes the new `tests/nav-routes.test.ts`).
- Manually traced the unknown-route path: `not-found.tsx` renders inside the root layout's `<Nav>`; for any pathname not in `MENU_ROUTES`/`isBackRoute`/auth prefixes, `isKnownRoute` is `false`, so `<Nav>` takes the same early-return branch as `/` and `/dashboard` — identical JSX, so the 404 chrome is byte-for-byte the menu-screen chrome (no restyling, no new branch).

## Notes for reviewers
- No visual/styling changes anywhere — the unknown-route case reuses the literal existing menu-screen JSX branch (same `if` block), per the issue's instruction to match it exactly.
- The `/admin` invariant: a non-admin requesting `/admin` sees chrome pixel-identical to any other 404 — no path echo, no Back button, no navigation surface — so the admin surface's existence cannot be inferred from the nav.

## Deviations
- The issue spec asked to ADD `/admin` to `BACK_ROUTE_PREFIXES`; review caught that this would make `isKnownRoute('/admin')` true and give a non-admin's 404 on `/admin` the full back-route chrome (HUD marker + RouteBack) — the exact leak this issue removes. Per master's correction, `/admin` is instead excluded from every route set; real admins get minimal menu-screen chrome on `/admin`, which is acceptable for a direct-URL ops page.

author: xfab-hari
body:
## Relevant issues

Fixes #32854
Related: #16584, #16596

## Linear ticket

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

To verify the fix, run a streaming request through a litellm proxy configured with a `bedrock_mantle/` model and observe the SSE chunks:

```bash
# Chat completions path (direct bedrock_mantle)
curl -sN http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"bedrock-mantle-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}],"stream":true}' \
  | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | sort -u

# Responses API bridge path (mode:"responses" models like openai.gpt-5.5 called via chat completions)
curl -sN http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}],"stream":true}' \
  | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | sort -u
```

Before the fix, every chunk has a different ID on both paths. After the fix, all chunks share the first chunk's ID.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

Two separate code paths produce inconsistent chunk IDs for `bedrock_mantle/` streaming, both breaking the openai-go SDK's `ChatCompletionAccumulator` which checks `cc.ID != chunk.ID` and silently drops every chunk after the first when IDs don't match.

**Path 1 — Direct chat completions (`BedrockMantleChatConfig`):**

Regular `bedrock_mantle/` models go through `llm_http_handler` → `BedrockMantleChatConfig.get_model_response_iterator()`. The upstream Bedrock Mantle API returns a unique ID per SSE chunk. Fix: added `BedrockMantleStreamingHandler` extending `OpenAIChatCompletionStreamingHandler` that captures the first chunk's raw `id` field and stamps it on all subsequent chunks before calling `super().chunk_parser()`.

**Path 2 — Responses API bridge (`OpenAiResponsesToChatCompletionStreamIterator`):**

Models with `mode: "responses"` (e.g. `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.5`) called via `/v1/chat/completions` route through the Responses API bridge in `completion_extras`. The bridge's `translate_responses_chunk_to_openai_stream()` creates a new `ModelResponseStream` per chunk, each getting a fresh UUID from the default constructor. Fix: capture the first converted chunk's ID in `self.response_id` and reuse it for all subsequent chunks.

**Path already OK — `bedrock/chat/mantle/` (Anthropic Messages API):**

This path uses its own `ModelResponseIterator` which generates a consistent `response_id` at init time. No fix needed.

PR #16596 (Nov 2025) fixed the same root cause for `bedrock/` (Converse API) but neither `bedrock_mantle/` path was patched.

4 regression tests total: 3 for the streaming handler (multi-chunk, single-chunk, config wiring) and 1 for the Responses→Chat bridge (ID consistency across event types).

## Summary

Adds bilingual support to the blog, since the team writes in Spanish:

- **Content model**: posts gain `lang` (`en`|`es`, default `en`) and `translationKey` (kebab-case, defaults to the slug). A Spanish/English pair shares a `translationKey`; each file keeps its own idiomatic slug and URL. Two files with the same key **and** the same lang fail the build.
- **Listings**: homepage, tag pages, and RSS feed collapse a pair to one entry, preferring English. The sitemap keeps both languages.

Same-repo PRs only; `GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes can't re-trigger the workflow (no loop). A failed translation never blocks merge.

After this merges, PRs #349 (QS-01) and #350 (QS-02) get `lang: es` frontmatter pushed to their branches, which triggers the new workflow to translate them — dogfooding the feature end-to-end.

author: skrimager
body:
## What was broken

The founder (`wadeskrimager@icloud.com`) still gets *\"you've used all three free sessions\"* on the public demo/trial flow, despite being told this was fixed.

## Root cause — why the earlier \"fix\" didn't take

The earlier fix **was written and merged** (PR #27, merged 2026-07-09). It adds an allowlist (`server/demo.ts`) — the founder's email is a hardcoded default plus an `UNLIMITED_DEMO_EMAILS` env var — and every enforcement call site (`/api/demo/request-code`, `/verify`, `/session`) already passes the email to `isSessionLimitReached`, which short-circuits for allowlisted emails. That code is correct and present on `master`. So this is **not a code regression**.

Two things kept the founder blocked anyway:

1. **Merged ≠ deployed.** There is no CI/CD or deploy config in the repo (no `.github/workflows`, no `render.yaml`); deploys are manual. If production is running a build from before PR #27, the exemption simply isn't in the running code. This is the same *\"merged but never applied to prod\"* gap as the Phoenix batch seed.
2. **The exemption is runtime-only and never healed the stored counter.** The founder's `demo_signups` row still has `sessionsUsed >= 3` from before he was allowlisted. The runtime check bypasses that count, but the stale value is misleading in the admin export and leaves the account brittle to any code path that reads the raw count.

## What this PR does

- Adds `healUnlimitedDemoUsage(store)` to `server/demo.ts`: resets `sessionsUsed` to 0 for every allowlisted email whose stored counter is > 0. Idempotent; only touches rows that need it.
- Calls it from `seed()` (runs on every boot, after migrations self-heal). **A redeploy alone now unblocks allowlisted emails with no manual production DB edit.**
- Adds unit tests for the heal (reset at/over cap, case/whitespace-insensitive match, non-exempt left untouched, idempotent no-op).

The allowlist itself (add more internal testers via `UNLIMITED_DEMO_EMAILS`) already exists from PR #27 and is unchanged here.

## Still required in production

Because deploys are manual, **this branch must actually be merged and deployed** for the founder to be unblocked — that is the real gap. Once deployed, boot heals his row automatically. If you want to unblock him *before* a deploy, run this read/writeback against the production `DATABASE_URL`:

```sql
UPDATE demo_signups SET sessions_used = 0
WHERE lower(trim(email)) = 'wadeskrimager@icloud.com';
```

## Testing

- `npm run check` (tsc) — clean
- `npm test` — 291 pass, 0 fail (includes 4 new heal tests)

body:
## Summary

Add an explicit `*_service_event` continuation family so split-service handlers return domain events while Tina wraps `ServiceMessage::Event` internally:

- `SleepCall::then_service_event`
- `TypedCall::then_service_event`
- `IsolateCall::then_service_event`
- `IsolateCall::then_service_event_with_request`
- `CancelableCall::then_service_event`
- `CancelCallBuilder::then_service_event`
- request-deferred typed/isolate calls: `reply_service_event`

The distinct spelling is deliberate: existing `SleepCall::then_event` returns the complete isolate message and hides the timer result, while `then_service_event` preserves the typed outcome and hides only the split-service envelope.

Representative applied examples cover every new helper. Domain outcomes, captured `RequestContext`, and cancel handles remain visible and move-only.

## Inventory

`origin/main` has 43 explicit `ServiceMessage::Event` code sites in examples: 42 continuations and one intentional direct send. This branch reduces that to 34 through representative migrations. Remaining sites are either eligible legacy call sites for later mechanical migration or higher-order translator/direct-send shapes; they do not reveal a missing common builder family.

## Adversarial review

An independent reviewer found and fixed two coverage/proof gaps:

1. Ordinary `TypedCall` was omitted, leaving non-timer I/O as an arbitrary raw-envelope exception. `TypedCall::then_service_event` now preserves its complete typed `Result` and is live-tested with an invalid file-close error.
2. The cancelable test dropped its returned handle, and `CancelCallBuilder` lacked the companion helper. The handle is now exercised through cancellation; the live proof observes `CancelOutcome::Cancelled` and verifies the cancelled call continuation does not arrive. The ergonomics playground uses the new cancellation path.

No request-authority or cancellation-truth regression was found. Request helpers move exactly one `RequestContext` into one `FnOnce` continuation; ordinary cancelable helpers intentionally carry no authority.

author: jinliyl
body:
## Summary

This PR makes embedding input truncation aware of CJK and other full-width characters, which typically consume more embedding tokens than ASCII text.

## Motivation

The existing local embedding store truncated every input by its raw Python character count. This treated ASCII and full-width text as equivalent even though CJK and other full-width characters commonly require a larger token budget.

The truncation helper also lived only on LocalEmbeddingStore, preventing other embedding store implementations from sharing the same input-length policy.

## Changes

- Move the truncation helper from LocalEmbeddingStore to BaseEmbeddingStore.
- Preserve the historical character limit and fast path for ASCII input.
- Assign a 1.5-unit cost to Unicode Wide and Fullwidth characters.
- Reserve a 5% safety margin when estimating non-ASCII input length.
- Use integer half-units to avoid floating-point boundary errors.
- Clamp negative maximum input lengths to an empty budget.
- Add regression coverage for ASCII, CJK, narrow non-ASCII, and negative-limit behavior.

## Behavior

Given a configured maximum input length of N:

- ASCII text is truncated to at most N characters, matching the previous behavior.
- Non-ASCII input uses 95% of the configured budget as an estimation safety margin.
- Narrow characters consume one budget unit.
- Wide and full-width characters consume 1.5 budget units.
- Truncation stops before the first character that would exceed the available budget.

## Testing

- uv run pytest tests/unit/test_local_embedding_store.py -q
  - Result: 4 passed

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent inventory picker from showing `On hand: 0` for every part when the stock summary lookup is missing or failed.  The root cause was divergence between the inventory page (which sums `stock_moves.qty_change`) and the request workbench (which relied on `part_stock_summary` and then defaulted missing values to `0`).
- Ensure physical on-hand is the canonical source for the picker UI and avoid silently substituting `qty_available` or stale `parts.quantity` fields for physical on-hand.

### Description
- Introduced a shared helper `loadStockOnHandByPartId` and `sumStockMovesByPartId` in `features/parts/lib/stock-on-hand.ts` that loads `stock_moves.part_id, qty_change`, filters by `shop_id` and part IDs, and returns summed on-hand totals by `part_id`.
- Replaced duplicated on-hand aggregation in `app/parts/inventory/page.tsx` to call `loadStockOnHandByPartId` so the inventory page and request workbench use the same canonical logic.
- Updated `app/parts/requests/[id]/page.tsx` to load stock from `stock_moves` (via the shared helper), use the resulting map for `stockAvailableByPartId` and `inventoryResults.onHandQty`, and surface query failures with a toast instead of defaulting values to zero.
- Changed `mapRequestToWorkbenchModel` (`features/parts/components/request-workbench/mapToWorkbenchModel.ts`) to preserve missing stock as `null` instead of `0` so UI can render unknown stock separately.
- Updated `InventoryPickerModal` (`features/parts/components/request-workbench/InventoryPickerModal.tsx`) to display `On hand: Unavailable` when stock is missing and only show the zero-stock warning for known zero values.
- Added a regression test `features/parts/components/request-workbench/InventoryPickerModal.test.tsx` that uses `sumStockMovesByPartId` to assert that two stock_moves (60 + 40) render `On hand: 100` in the picker.
- Minor test/runtime adjustments: added `React` import to components used in tests and a small typing adapter in the helper to keep compatibility with the Supabase client types.

Files changed: `features/parts/lib/stock-on-hand.ts`, `app/parts/inventory/page.tsx`, `app/parts/requests/[id]/page.tsx`, `features/parts/components/request-workbench/mapToWorkbenchModel.ts`, `features/parts/components/request-workbench/InventoryPickerModal.tsx`, `features/parts/components/request-workbench/WorkbenchModalFrame.tsx`, and added test `features/parts/components/request-workbench/InventoryPickerModal.test.tsx`.

### Motivation

- The previous full-map and dynamic-radar capture paths appended every replicated player, enemy, POI, building, and personal marker without upper bounds, allowing a malicious/abusive server to force unbounded CPU, memory, and JSON serialization work on the client.
- The dynamic telemetry path runs frequently (50 ms) and amplifies the impact of uncapped scans, so bounds are required to preserve client availability.

### Description

- Introduce explicit limits: `kMaxDynamicRadarFriends`, `kMaxDynamicRadarEnemies`, `kMaxFullMapMarkers`, and `kMaxPoiReplicationRecords` and keep the existing `kDynamicRadarTelemetryIntervalSeconds` behavior. 
- Cap dynamic radar loops so friend/enemy collection stops once the configured per-category limits are reached, and cap full-map enemy scanning similarly. 
- Make `AddFullMapMarker` return a boolean and early-return when the `kMaxFullMapMarkers` snapshot cap is reached, and add loop guards to stop building, foundable, base attack, personal marker, POI actor, and POI replication-data scans when the snapshot is full. 
- Add small telemetry reset/guarding around dynamic/local telemetry state and preserve snapshot counts (`FullMapMarkerCount`) so behavior is unchanged up to the configured limits.

author: an1va
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the "cheap image embedding" problem reported in the [handoff doc](https://derive.to/artifacts/cheap-image-embedding-for-artifacts-handoff-x29qarzd): an agent had no cheap way to put a real screenshot in a **single-file** artifact (the reliable kind — `edits`, proposals, clean reads). The only working path (bundles + `asset:<hash>`) never had a standalone URL, and there was zero discoverability of the actual serving route (`/raw/<id>/v/<n>/<path>`), so agents fell back to base64 — ~1 token/char, 100k+ tokens for one modest PNG.
- `POST /v1/assets` now persists an `asset` row (org, sniffed content-type, size — previously discarded) and returns a permanent `url` alongside the existing `ref`.
- New `GET /blob/:hash` route serves those bytes unauthenticated — a Slack/Notion-style capability link (content-addressed, unguessable, immutable). Gated *only* by the presence of an `asset` row, so it can never leak an unrelated blob-store hash (a private bundle's manifest JSON, an HTML page) — verified with a dedicated security test.
- Bundle `asset:<hash>` (existing pattern) is untouched; both mechanisms point at the same underlying bytes.
- Folds staged-asset bytes into the storage quota (previously free forever until referenced by a publish — a quota bypass now that the bytes are permanently servable).
- Bundle `publish` results now surface each file's `/raw/...` URL directly (the discoverability fix).
- `read` (markdown format only) elides giant base64 `data:` URIs so an old base64-laden doc doesn't cost ~175k tokens to read back; `format:'html'` stays byte-exact for `edits`.
- Updates the `derive-publish` skill docs (both copies) with the new flow.

## Why this design (not the doc-gated alternative)

Considered making `asset:` refs resolve to a URL that inherits the artifact's own visibility (signed token, gated by doc access). Went with public capability URLs instead: far simpler (no publish-time scanning, no sanitizer-pipeline concerns, no rewrite machinery), covers the common case (handoffs, walkthroughs, screenshots), and the hash is unguessable — same trust model as an S3 presigned-forever link or a Slack file share.

## Test plan

- [x] `packages/db` store-contract suite (shared across sqlite/D1/pg dialects): stage/read/idempotent-reupload, org-scoped quota sum — passing on sqlite and D1 locally
- [x] New `apps/api/test/blob.test.ts`: happy path, extension-ignored, unknown-hash 404, malformed-hash 404, and the security case (a blob-store hash with no `asset` row 404s even though the bytes exist)
- [x] Extended `apps/api/test/assets.test.ts`: upload response includes `url`; the url actually serves the uploaded bytes back
- [x] `serve-web.test.ts` (the `/blob` worker-first lockstep across wrangler.toml / serve-web.ts / vite proxy)
- [x] Full monorepo `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] Full `apps/api` suite on sqlite backend — clean (1 unrelated pre-existing flaky timeout in `sync-runner.test.ts`, reproduces identically on unmodified main)
- [x] OpenAPI snapshot + `apps/web/src/api-types.ts` regenerated
- [ ] Full suite against real Postgres (`scripts/test-pg.sh`) — running; will report back if anything fails that isn't resource-contention noise
- [ ] Live E2E on prod after deploy (upload → embed → render → verify existing bundle images still serve)

body:
## Summary

Adds deterministic trace/freshness checks between canonical Markdown requirements and FSL tags/scenarios.

Closes #192.

## What changed

- Defines canonical normative sections as `## REQ-n: title` through the next heading.
- Normalizes canonical tag text as title + non-empty body lines with collapsed whitespace.
- Adds `check/verify --docs FILE`.
- Emits `missing_formalization`, `ghost_requirement`, and `stale_tag`; stale findings carry both old and new text.
- Adds `spec X "source: relative.md"` auto-discovery relative to the spec.
- Adds exact Markdown bytes to the verify cache key, so doc-only edits force a cache miss and re-check.
- Updates strict-tags design, language docs, FSL skill/reference, changelog, and generated website references.

## Responsibility boundary

- The checks establish ID existence and copied-text freshness, not natural-language/formula semantic equivalence.
- Text outside an ID section is explicitly non-normative; this format contract is what makes omission detection complete.
- No checksum is embedded into `.fsl`; doc edits produce actionable old/new evidence rather than an acknowledgement-hash ceremony.
- Explicit `--docs` wins over `source:`. Without either, existing output is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Full suite: **1288 passed, 78 skipped** in 12m07s
- Doc/cache/strict-tags/coupled-change/site suite: **52 passed**
- Focused canonical-doc and cache-key completeness suite: **7 passed**
- Snapshot fixes all three warning shapes including old/new text.
- `git diff --check`: clean

## Review focus

- Markdown section termination and canonical whitespace normalization.
- Formal reference collection across tags/acceptance/forbidden.

author: joeyorlando
body:
## What

Fixes three recurring production error signals, all traced from error tracking. Each is either a crash or noise from an upstream/transient condition being reported as a server fault. In the spirit of #6418 and #6506, these cut the remaining high-frequency noise (and one real crash), plus a small follow-on refactor to centralize the network-errno vocabulary the fixes introduced.

### 1. `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')`
`isLoopbackAddress(ip)` is called with `request.ip` from the LLM proxy. Fastify types `request.ip` as `string`, but at runtime it can be `undefined` (a socket with no remote address, or an empty `X-Forwarded-For` under `trustProxy`). The helper then threw on `.startsWith`, 500-ing the request.

Treat a non-string IP as **non-loopback** (the secure default — an unknown origin is never trusted as loopback) rather than throwing. Centralized in the helper so all six call sites are covered.

### 2. `Error: Failed to update conversation with title`
The generate-title handler fetches the conversation, makes a slow async LLM call, then writes the title back. If the conversation is deleted during that window, `ConversationModel.update` matches no row and returns `null` — which raised a 500 that was captured as a server exception.

That's a benign race, not a server fault. Title generation is best-effort, so it now falls through gracefully like the handler's other skip branches instead of throwing.

### 3. `Error: Connection error.` / `Request timed out.`
A connection failure or timeout reaching the upstream provider (SDK `APIConnectionError` / `APIConnectionTimeoutError`, or the libuv/undici errno codes they wrap) carries **no** HTTP status, so `handleError` defaulted it to 500 and the central handler captured it as a server exception.

These are the upstream's/network's failure, not ours. They're now reclassified as gateway errors (**504** timeout, **502** connection) so the central handler logs them but keeps them out of error tracking — it already excludes 502/504. The client still sees the same retryable `ServerError` card (any `statusCode >= 500` maps to it), so no UX change.

### 4. Refactor: centralize the network-errno vocabulary
Fix #3's classifier and the existing embedding retry check each hand-rolled their own set of libuv/undici errno strings (and the LLM proxy also its own cause-chain walker). Extracted a shared `utils/network-errors` module that owns the vocabulary plus `isConnectionErrno` / `isTimeoutErrno` predicates and `collectErrorCodes(error)` (the cause-chain walker). Both consumers now compose from it; the raw sets stay module-private so callers can't diverge on membership again.

Deliberately **not** folded in:
- `database/retry.ts` — Postgres SQLSTATE codes + pool-specific message patterns, a different domain with different matching.
- `utils/docker-localhost-hint.ts` — matches on message substrings, not `error.code`.

`isRetryableEmbeddingError` now retries on a slightly larger but strictly-safe superset (EAI_AGAIN, EPIPE, undici socket/timeout errors) — all genuinely transient.

## Why

All three were among the current highest-frequency error-tracking signals. Two were pure noise from upstream/transient conditions; one (#1) was a real crash on the LLM proxy path.

## Testing

- `isLoopbackAddress` returns `false` for `undefined`/`null`.
- generate-title returns 200 (not 500) when the conversation is deleted mid-generation.
- `handleError` classifies SDK connection errors → 502, timeouts → 504, wrapped `cause` errno chains correctly, and leaves errors with an explicit HTTP status and generic internal errors as 500.
- New `network-errors` unit tests: connection vs timeout predicates, cause-chain collection (incl. circular-cause bound). Existing embedding tests still pass.
- `pnpm type-check`, backend `pnpm knip` (dev + production), and Biome all clean.

author: manlycucumber
body:
Second slice of the **Novus Ordo calendar engine** (v1.1.0, epic #256). Teaches the corpus generator to author an edition as a **whole, unioned peer** (the signed-off architecture) rather than only as diff-blocks on the shared 1962 file — the enabling infrastructure for the NO's own sanctoral. No NO data is declared yet, so the code is **dormant and the corpus is byte-identical**.

## What lands
- **`transformSanctoraleWhole()`** — fans a flat `facts/editions/<dir>/sanctorale.yaml` into identity + attributes + placement. Identity is emitted **only** when an entry declares it (a NO-only observance → merged into the shared union); a saint shared with 1962 is **referenced by id alone** and reuses the union's identity. Partial identity fails closed.
- **`deriveNovusRank()` + the `novusRank` schema field** — the NO grade vocabulary (`solemnity`/`feast`/`memorial`/`optional-memorial`), numeric `RankClass` derived and cited to the same source, kept a **separate bag** from the pre-1960 `legacyRank` grades (mirrors the `deriveLegacyRank` contract).
- **`build.mjs`** — loads the per-edition whole file, merges its identities into the union (dedup-or-throw, exactly like octave identities), and adds a **placement-has-identity gate** (every placed id must have an identity — the converse of the existing orphan gate).

## Safety
- **1962/1954/1955 corpus NDJSON byte-identical** — the only committed data change is the additive `novusRank` schema field; `verify` confirms 32 files reproducible and matching.
- Green: **45 Node tests** (5 new for `transformSanctoraleWhole`), **1040 PHP tests** (schema is opis-validated in PHP too).

Part of #256. Next: the NO temporal cycle (Ordinary Time) and the `NovusOrdoPrecedence` engine, which will exercise this whole-edition path with real NO data.

author: pratikbin
body:
## Problem

`createos sandbox tunnel my-box --remote 8000` fails with `--remote <port> is required` — even though that exact flags-after-positional form is shown in the command's own `--help` examples.

Root cause: urfave/cli v2 stops flag parsing at the first positional argument. The `edit` command already documents and works around this with a hand-rolled `parseEditArgs`; `tunnel` never got the equivalent, so `--remote`/`--local`/`--bind` placed after `<sandbox>` are silently dropped.

This also breaks the **createos-sandbox Claude plugin**, whose `cos` driver invokes `tunnel` in exactly this order — every `/createos-sandbox:tunnel` died on it.

## Fix

Add `parseTunnelArgs`, mirroring `parseEditArgs`: seed from `c.*` (keeps flags placed *before* the positional working), then re-scan the raw args so a later `--remote`/`--local`/`--bind` in any position wins. Handles both `--flag value` and `--flag=value`.

## Verification

Built a linux/amd64 binary and ran against a live sandbox — all three now succeed:

| invocation | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tunnel <id> --remote 9090 --local 9091` (was broken) | `ERROR --remote required` | ✅ `Forwarding` |
| `tunnel <id> --remote=9093 --local=9094` | `ERROR` | ✅ `Forwarding` |
| `tunnel --remote 9095 --local 9096 <id>` (flags-first) | ✅ | ✅ |

`go build` / `go vet` / `gofmt` / `golangci-lint` clean.

body:
## Summary

Two follow-ups you asked for.

### 1. Sidebar now fits one screen (collapsible groups)

The 19-link grouped map is taller than a laptop viewport (the 30px icon chips alone push it past ~1,300px), so it was scrolling internally even on tall screens. Fixed properly:

- **Each group is collapsible** via its header, with a caret showing open/closed state.
- **Auto-fit on load/resize:** the sidebar collapses lower-priority groups until the whole map fits with **no internal scrollbar**. **Overview stays open and Outbound collapses last** (collapse order: Leadership → Demand → Leads → Outbound), so your focus area stays visible. Verified at **0px overflow** on 1000 / 860 / 800 / 740px-tall viewports.
- **Your choice wins:** once you manually open/close any group, auto-fit stops overriding you.
- The group that owns the section you're viewing is **highlighted**, so you always know where you are even when its group is collapsed.
- **Mobile unchanged:** the group wrappers flatten (`display:contents`), so the nav stays a flat horizontal scroller with all links visible and no headers.

### 2. Header keeps the meta pills when pinned

Following your ask: when the header condenses on scroll it now hides **only the logo/title** and **keeps the meta pills** (Period / Calls / Avg duration / Minutes / Cost / Source) visible above the filter row — so you keep dataset context while filtering, not just the controls. author: willprout
body:
Closes #27

## What & why
A gate-green PR whose merge GitHub **refuses** — ordinary branch protection (require approvals, strict up-to-date) or a token without merge rights — used to retry every tick **forever**: no counter, no cap, no park, no notify. A green PR that never landed and never explained itself; the morning report showed it gating indefinitely. This bounds the retries and surfaces the refusal.

## How (house counter/cap pattern, like `launch_failures`/`update_errors`)
- **`gh.merge_pr`** now returns `(ok, reason)` — `(True, "")` on success, `(False, <bounded single-line tail of gh's stderr>)` on refusal. `_run` delegates to a new `_run_full` that also returns stderr; every other caller stays a 2-tuple.
- **`runner._exec_merge`** counts each refusal (`merge_refusals`) and records **why** (`merge_refusal_reason`). Status never advances past the truth (stays `gating`).
- **`actions.decide`** caps at `MERGE_REFUSAL_CAP` (2): retry under the bound, then **park needs-william once** with the reason in the memo **+ one notify**, and stop. A corrupt counter **fails closed** to the park (never re-merge forever on a wrong-typed value).
- **Episode-scoped guard**: both `reapprove` and `regenerate` zero the counter, so a re-approved or rebuilt PR retries the merge from scratch — never forever-latched.

## Bright line held
No force-push, no protection-bypass machinery anywhere. The refusal is **surfaced to the owner** (approve the PR / fix the token / adjust protection), never coached around. Engine-only: all changes under `skills/**`; nothing under `.superlooper/**` or `.github/workflows/**`.

## Tests
Unit (gh `(ok, reason)` contract + bounded/collapsed reason, executor counter + persisted reason, decide cap, corrupt fail-closed, missing-reason memo, reapprove/regenerate reset) **plus two end-to-end simulation drives** through the real runner tick loop against the stateful fake-gh:
- refuse every tick → exactly 2 bounded merge attempts → park needs-william with the branch-protection reason in the memo + one notify → retries stop;
- a transient refusal that clears within the bound merges cleanly with zero noise.

fake-gh fail rules gained an optional custom `stderr` so a refusal message doesn't echo the match string back into the park memo's own gh call (a harness artifact, not a product bug).

Full engine suite: **859 passed**. Fresh-agent review: **no P0/P1** (verdict posted as a PR comment); its two actionable P2s (episode-scope across `regenerate`; corrupt-counter memo wording) are addressed in this diff.

- Groq defaultModel -> openai/gpt-oss-120b, chain: gpt-oss-120b -> gpt-oss-20b -> llama-4-scout-17b -> llama-3.3-70b-versatile -> qwen3-32b
- Cerebras -> llama-3.3-70b, chain: llama-3.3-70b -> gpt-oss-120b -> llama-3.1-8b -> qwen-3-32b
- OpenRouter -> llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free
- callLLM now iterates model candidates per provider, retries on decommissioned/not found errors

author: arjunamarcelino
body:
## Summary

Brings **Scenario 1 (Tutorial — Koperasi Konsumen)** fully to life: a real-time, voice/text NPC conversation over LiveKit, presented as a **visual-novel overlay**, with the end-session action **gated on the scenario goal actually being reached**.

Three layers of work:
1. **Voice transport + session controller** (ported from `web-sementara`): a `SessionTransport` seam with mock (offline, scripted) and LiveKit (real backend) implementations, a generation-token controller, and an agent-ready gate. The kasir NPC triggers the session.
2. **Visual-novel redesign**: the old full-page chat is replaced by an in-hub overlay — the player is frozen over the live map while two big scaled characters (NPC samurai vs player villager) converse in a stream-driven dialogue box, with an icon action rail and a status bar.
3. **Goal-gated ending**: a new backend `goal_reached` signal so the end button only unlocks once the objective is met.

## Visual-novel UI

- **Two big characters** L/R (CSS-cropped frame 0 of the existing 16×16 sheets, scaled ×9 — no new art); active speaker highlighted, listener dimmed.
- **Dialogue box**: name-plate + face crop + the single latest line (auto-advancing, caret while streaming), text input + mic + Kirim.
- **Action rail** (icon-only, hover/focus-expand): Deskripsi, Petunjuk, Akhiri; Maju-Fase only when a scenario emits phases (never the tutorial).
- **Status bar**: NPC name, Drift meter, connection pill, close.
- Deskripsi (briefing) **opens by default**; Deskripsi + Petunjuk have prominent pixel ✕ close buttons.

## Goal-gated ending (new)

Per `backent-prd.md §7.1` / `scenarios.md` — the tutorial completes once the customer agrees to register. Implemented as a real runtime signal:

- **Backend**: `Scenario.goal_tool_prompt` (single-NPC); when set, the agent gets a function-tool `catat_kesepakatan` that publishes participant attribute `goal_reached=1` once (fires when the ibu agrees). Documented in `CONTRACT.md §4f`.
- **Frontend**: `onGoalReached` on the transport (LiveKit attribute listener; mock fires it at the scripted agreement turn), `session.store.goalReached`, and a `gatesEndOnGoal` config flag (tutorial `true`). The end button shows a **lock + "(selesaikan tujuan dulu)"** until the goal fires, then unlocks with a pop.

## Robustness (two deepen rounds)

- Phaser keyboard fully disabled for the **entire** freeze + suppression window, `resetKeys()` on the unfreeze edge → no WASD leak into the frozen player.
- Hub chrome inert while the session is open; exit flag honored only when no overlay.
- Guarded `openSession` (unknown id + close-suppression); agent-join watchdog (~25s), connection re-gate + "Koneksi terputus" panel, document-capture Esc in all states.
- **Functional mic mute**: `setMicEnabled` returns the real resulting track state; the store reconciles to it (denied permission → stays muted), and the session starts muted so the toggle is authoritative. Mic released before teardown.

## Testing

- `typecheck` + `lint` + `build` green.
- **Mock (Playwright)**: enter NPC → idle gesture → VN ready → send turns → NPC lines → end button stays locked → unlocks exactly on the scripted agreement turn → Akhiri → ResultPanel → Kembali → player unfreezes and moves.
- **LIVE (real backend, Playwright text path)**: token server + voice worker up, FE in `livekit` mode. Verified end-to-end:
  - Worker log: `executing tool {"function":"catat_kesepakatan"}` → `Tujuan skenario tercapai — publish goal_reached=1`.
  - FE: agent joins (~5–16s), end button **locked** while the ibu is still asking, **unlocks live** once she agrees, click → live `end_session` → `AuditorResult` report (`scenarios.py` scripted text).
  - Backend tool build asserted against livekit-agents 1.6.5.

> Note: this branch also carries the earlier voice-transport port, so it ships Scenario 1 as one coherent change. Live voice needs the backend running (`VITE_TRANSPORT=livekit`, token server + worker, FE origin matching `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN`); default mock mode runs offline. (Screenshots captured locally — image hosts were unavailable to embed.)

body:
## Summary

UI/UX audit batch for the public pages (legal, support, about, not-found, landing, contact). Fixes one real rendering bug (a dead `zVariant` attribute turning a destructive bulk action into a filled primary CTA), makes the unsubscribe page distinguish transient fetch failures from dead tokens, gives the landing events query real loading/error states so an outage no longer looks like "nothing on sale", and consolidates three divergent hand-rolled outline CTAs into one shared treatment.

## Changes

**Unsubscribe (`features/legal/pages/unsubscribe`)**
- `zVariant="ghost"` → `zType="ghost"` (z-button's input is `zType`; the attribute was dead and the destructive action rendered as a filled primary CTA)
- Wrapped in `app-content-layout` so the header skip link (`#main-content`) resolves
- Service now returns `null` only for backend-rejected tokens (400/404) and throws on network/5xx/malformed payloads; the component branches `resource.error()` into a retry state (with reload) distinct from the invalid-link state
- Per-community checkboxes: in-flight disable (rapid-click race), explicit `checked` reset on mutation failure (zoneless never rewrites an unchanged binding), 24px targets (`h-6 w-6`), `min-h-11` labels
- `z-skeleton` rows replace the pulsing-text loading state
- Full-opacity `text-warning` on the tinted banner (was `text-warning/70`), `rounded-lg`, lowercase toasts

**Legal (`terms-of-service`, `privacy-policy`)**
- `href="/privacy"` full-reload → `routerLink`
- "promoter-event charges" jargon → buyer-facing "charges for community events"
- Syne h2/h3 rendered at weight 400 → `font-bold tracking-tight`

**Support + contact dialog**
- Support page's raw mailto + hand-rolled copy-address fallback replaced by `PlatformContactDialogService.open({subject: 'Braket support'})` (the dialog exists because mailto silently fails)
- Intro filler → terse lowercase routing copy
- Contact dialog: hand-copied ~500-char z-button class string → `<a z-button zType="default" zSize="lg">`; doubled `mr-2` icon gaps dropped; `rounded-lg`; lowercase toasts

**Landing / about / not-found**
- One shared `OUTLINE_MONO_CTA_CLASS` (`features/shared/outline-cta.ts`) replaces the three divergent hand-rolls; no glow hover; `hover:text-white` → `hover:text-primary-foreground`
- Landing hero centers only when the events query is settled-and-empty (was flipping on resource arrival — layout jump on every cold load); skeleton rows while loading; one-line lowercase fallback on error
- About: entrance stagger capped at the `fade-in-delay` utilities, per section not per paragraph (was up to 1.2s of arbitrary delays)
- Not-found: copy now says the page doesn't exist instead of claiming a fix is underway; shouty mono line demoted to a micro label; z-button override pile replaced with the shared CTA

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck:frontend` — pass
- `pnpm lint:angular` — pass
- `pnpm test:frontend -- src/app/features/{legal,support,about,not-found,landing,contact}` — 9 files, 61 tests, all pass. New coverage: unsubscribe error-vs-invalid branching, retry recovery, loading skeleton, ghost variant, checkbox failure reset and in-flight disable; landing loading/error/settled branches and settled-and-empty centering; support dialog-open; 404 copy accuracy
- `git diff origin/develop | pnpm exec ifttt-lint -` — pass (touched the annotated terms file; the coupled date line is unchanged)
- Visual check via `pnpm run screenshot:frontend` on `/`, `/support`, `/about`, and a 404 route
- `pnpm validate` skipped in favor of the targeted typecheck + lint + specs above; full validation runs in CI

## Skipped

- None — every spec item was located and applied.
- Noted (out of batch scope, not touched): `features/dashboard/pages/dashboard/dashboard.component.html` has a fourth copy of the outline-mono CTA hand-roll (`hover:text-white` included).

## Review fixups

Addresses the reviewer note (CLAUDE.md: "migrate every existing duplicated implementation to the helper in the same change") that the dashboard still hand-rolled the outline-mono CTA — the "Noted / out of batch scope" item above is now done.

- Merged `origin/develop` (picks up #232/#233/#234/#227). Confirmed #233 already removed the old `hover:text-white` from the dashboard; no `hover:text-white` / `group-hover:text-white` remains anywhere in `frontend/src`.
- Reworked `features/shared/outline-cta.ts`: `OUTLINE_MONO_CTA_CLASS` is now a `outlineMonoCta({trigger?: 'hover' | 'group', size?: 'xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'|'xl'})` pure function returning just the shared treatment tokens. `size` encodes the border-width + padding preset each real site needs.
- Migrated the dashboard's four outline-mono CTAs to the helper via `[class]` bindings (repo's class-binding convention): community apply chip (`group`/`sm`), compact apply chip (`group`/`xs`), vetting resubmit link (`hover`/`md`), get-tickets button (`hover`/`lg`). Element-specific layout is composed into the same binding string.
- Preserved each site's rendered appearance exactly — verified all five consumers (three public + two dashboard variants) are class-set-equivalent to their originals (same border width, padding, hover trigger, tokens).
- `OUTLINE_MONO_CTA_CLASS` stays exported as a backward-compatible, function-derived public preset (the `xl`/hover treatment plus public button chrome: focus ring, `inline-block`, `text-center`, `bg-transparent`, pointer). The three public consumers keep importing it unchanged, so the public chrome lives in exactly one place instead of being duplicated per consumer — everything routes through `outlineMonoCta`.
- Updated the docstring to list every consuming surface (public pages + dashboard), not just "public pages".

Verification for this fixup: `pnpm typecheck:frontend` pass, `pnpm lint:angular` pass, `pnpm test:frontend` on the dashboard + landing + about + not-found specs (4 files, 92 tests) pass. Full E2E runs in CI.

author: kevinskey
body:
## Problem
Pressing record with only a MIDI track errored: *"Arm at least one audio track first (red R button on the strip)"*. MIDI note capture is gated on `recordingActive`, which only the audio record flow sets — so recording MIDI required arming an audio track and deleting the throwaway mic take. Worse, the Settings dialog told users to "arm it (red R)" on a MIDI track, but MIDI tracks had no R button.

## Fix
- `recordStartMode()` in `midiRecord.ts` — pure, unit-tested decision: `audio` when any audio track is armed (unchanged behavior), `midi` when none is armed but USB MIDI input is on with a target MIDI track (web engine only), `blocked` otherwise with a toast that now mentions the MIDI option.
- MIDI-only take: transport rolls + `recordingActive` set, no mic recorder opened. Stop flushes still-held keys, parks the playhead at the take start, and skips the audio finalize pipeline.
- MIDI tracks render the R arm button (picks the input target among multiple MIDI tracks, matching `midiInputTrack`'s existing armed-first logic).

## Verification
- `vitest run src/lib/studio/` — 167/167 pass (5 new recordStartMode cases)
- Verified live on gleeworld.org with a Williams WP06: ● with no armed audio → "Recording MIDI" toast, transport rolls, ● again → "Recorded 17.2s of MIDI", no new console errors.

Fixes #319.

## Problem

After #306 (a `pending()` step no longer reddens the sbt build — the Task gates on `FeatureResult.isComplete`), the `pretty` reporter's **feature-level** header still rendered a pending-only feature as red `FAILED`. `StatusColor[FeatureResult]` and `statusText(FeatureResult)` lacked the PENDING branch their scenario-level counterparts already have, so a feature whose only non-passing scenario was pending fell through to the red `else` — contradicting the scenario line (`PENDING`), the summary (`Failed: 0`), the JUnit XML (`failures="0"`), and the now-green build.

```
╰─ ◉ Feature: Pending steps ... - FAILED      <- red, wrong
   ╰─ ◑ Scenario: ...          - PENDING      <- orange, correct
    Summary: Passed: 0  Failed: 0  Ignored: 0  Pending: 1   (sbt exit 0)
```

## Fix

Add the `f.hasPending && f.isComplete → orange "PENDING"` branch to both `StatusColor[FeatureResult]` and `statusText(FeatureResult)` in `PrettyReporter.scala`, mirroring the scenario-level logic. `FeatureResult.isComplete` is `false` when any scenario has a hard failure, so a feature with **both** a pending and a failed scenario correctly stays red `FAILED` — pending never masks a real failure.

## Tests

Three `PrettyReporterSpec` regressions:
- pending-only `FeatureResult` → `Orange` (not Red)
- rendered `featureBranch` header → contains `PENDING`, not `FAILED`
- pending **+** failed `FeatureResult` → stays `Red` (hard failure not masked)

All 52 reporter tests pass; `core/scalafmtCheckAll` clean.

## Notes

Found by the standing black-box conformance suite ([zio-bdd-conformance](https://github.com/EtaCassiopeia/zio-bdd-conformance)) while verifying the #306 fix on 1.4.2. Residual of #306; ref epic #192.

## Why

#463 merged `deploy/deploy-authentik-sync.sh` **without** the shellcheck disable that was on the branch head, so `main`'s **Lint** job now fails:

```
In deploy/deploy-authentik-sync.sh line 52:
if ssh "${sshopts[@]}" "$target" "sudo docker exec ${container} ak ldap_sync ${slug}"; then
  ... SC2029 (info): Note that, unescaped, this expands on the client side.
FAIL: shellcheck
```

CI's shellcheck (0.11.0) treats the **SC2029** info note as fatal.

## Fix

The client-side expansion is **intentional** — `container` and `slug` are in-script constants, not remote values. Add `# shellcheck disable=SC2029` with a reason, exactly matching the convention already used in `deploy/deploy-nixos.sh` and `deploy/reboot-fleet.sh`.

One-line change (a comment); no behavior change.
