author: erikg84
body:
## Problem

A successful sign-up that requires email confirmation was surfaced to users as a generic error: **"An error occurred. Please try again."** — even though the account *was* created in `auth.users`.

### Root cause

`SupabaseAuth.signUpWithEmail` decided success/failure by reading the **session-based `currentUser`**. When email confirmation is required there is no session, so `currentUser` was `null` and the method returned:

```kotlin
SupabaseResult.Failure(SupabaseError.Authentication(
    message = "Account created. Please check your email to confirm."))
```

Consumers map `Failure → AuthResult.Error`, and that message matches **no** `mapAuthError` pattern, so it fell through to the generic `"An error occurred. Please try again."` snackbar.

## Fix

Capture the `UserInfo` that `signUpWith(Email)` returns and, when there is no active session, build the `AuthUser` from it and return **`Success` with `emailConfirmed = false`**. This is exactly what consumers already expect — they branch on `AuthUser.emailConfirmed` to show a "check your email" prompt (that path was previously dead code). A genuine no-user response still returns `Failure`.

## Verification

- `:supabase-auth:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` + `:supabase-auth:compileKotlinMetadata` build green on the `main` baseline.
- Logic trace end-to-end: confirm-required → `Success(emailConfirmed=false)` → consumer `AuthResult.Success(null)` → `AuthViewModel` sets `successMessage` ("Account created! Please check your email…") and flips to SIGN_IN, instead of the error path.

Scope: SDK only. No consumer-app changes in this PR.

author: ryanskarnulis
body:
First slice of the agent-reliability epic (TODO.md top item): voice games were dying by attrition because an illegal-move guess ended the turn with no recovery.

## What

- `/api/command` now runs a bounded self-correction loop after dispatch: any result with `ok: false` — or `make_move` with `legal: false` — is fed back to the brain as a correction command against the **fresh** agent state, up to `MAX_TOOL_RETRY_ROUNDS` (2) rounds, before falling through to react.
- Rejected moves include the current legal-move list in the correction, so the brain picks from truth instead of guessing again.
- A retry round that answers in words instead of tools (clarifying question / concession) is treated as the final user-facing reply — react is skipped so the answer isn't buried.
- All attempts stay visible in `tool_results`; the correction command is plumbing and is never recorded in the transcript.

## Why in the pipeline, not LlamaBrain

Domain errors only surface after registry dispatch, which the brain never sees in phase one — so the loop lives in `api.py` and benefits any `Brain` implementation (generalizing LlamaBrain's schema-retry idea). The deterministic core stays the referee: retries go through the same validated registry.

## Tests

TDD red→green: 10 new tests in `test_domain_retry.py` (scripted brain, no live LLM) covering the corrected-move happy path, correction content (error + legal moves, failed calls only), fresh-state retries, the wordy-reply escape, the retry bound, transcript hygiene, and WS broadcast after a retried mutation. Three pre-existing single-failure tests now script the retry round their failure earns. Backend 431.

body:
Fixes #35.

## Bug
`cmd_huddle_open`'s `status:claimed` re-check branch called `is_session_holder(held)` — a name defined nowhere in `bus` (only `_is_huddle_lock` exists, at bus:572). `ast.parse` accepts undefined names (runtime-only), so it shipped via #28. The path **NameError-crashes at runtime** when `bus huddle open --issue N` runs on an issue already labelled `status:claimed` with the Redis lock still held (the durable-label anti-steal guard).

## Fix
One-line rename of the call site to the existing `_is_huddle_lock` helper — the intended callee. `_is_huddle_lock(holder)` returns `holder.startswith("huddle:")`:
- rival **solo** claim → holder is a plain agent id (`cmd_claim` bus:811) → `startswith("huddle:")` False → guard **blocks**. Correct.
- legitimate **huddle** session token `huddle:issue-N:<hex>` (bus:1203) → True → guard **allows**. Correct.

Same helper already used at bus:592 (reap) and bus:695 (board), so this is consistent reuse, not novel logic.

author: vincentvella
body:
`v0.10.0`'s release npm job failed with:

\`\`\`
npm error code MODULE_NOT_FOUND
npm error Cannot find module 'sigstore'   → libnpmpublish/lib/provenance.js
\`\`\`

`npm install -g npm@latest` (required for Trusted Publishing, npm ≥ 11.5.1) intermittently leaves the global npm missing `sigstore`, which provenance needs — so the whole release fails even though installers + the GitHub release published. A manual re-run cleared it.

## Change
Fold the npm self-install into the publish step and **retry up to 3×** so a flaky install self-heals:
- The "already on npm → skip" guard runs first and short-circuits (idempotent if an attempt partially succeeds).
- Each attempt reinstalls `npm@latest` then `npm publish --access public`; on success it exits, else retries after 5s; fails after 3.

No behavior change on the happy path; just resilience. (Workflow file — merge in the UI; can't be API-merged.)

author: likiossedo
body:
## Summary

Align newly authored Siclaw knowledge bundles with OKF v0.1 while keeping three concerns explicit: OKF core conformance, Siclaw's portable-output profile, and compatibility with existing legacy pages.

## What changed

- Parse concept frontmatter with `yaml.safe_load` and require a non-empty string `type`.
- Validate reserved `index.md` and `log.md` structure, including entries in every log date group.
- Treat file-relative Markdown links as a Siclaw producer profile rather than an OKF core rule; bundle-root links remain valid OKF input.
- Ignore fenced and inline code while linting links and body provenance markers.
- Preserve complete imported source filenames, including spaces, nested Chinese/ASCII parentheses, commas, semicolons, and enumeration punctuation.
- Resolve spaced page links in CommonMark angle form, URL-encoded form, and the tolerant raw form already emitted by existing agents.
- Capture format violations at incremental kickoff. Existing violations on pages unchanged by the round remain visible migration debt; violations on actually changed or new pages still fail the gate.
- Teach the runtime consumer to follow nested relative Markdown links while retaining legacy wikilink support.
- Share one Python dependency list between the compile image and KBC CI, including `PyYAML==6.0.3`.
- Keep safe YAML serialization and mandatory type checks in the legacy emitter.

## Review fixes

- A body citation such as `(source: 上线方案（终版）、GPU 调度，修订；v2.md)` no longer becomes an impossible `body_source_malformed` violation.
- Source examples inside fenced or inline code no longer become real provenance requirements.
- Removing the extension or citing a file absent from `compiled_from` remains fail-closed.
- Space-separated source locators such as `(source: report.pdf p.12)` are parsed without truncating filenames; malformed suffixes and uncited files remain fail-closed.
- Incremental format enforcement now keys off pages actually changed this round, so merely authorizing an untouched legacy `index.md` no longer triggers migration.
- Rebased onto the current `main` after #403; the current KBC mTLS test is included in validation.

## Behavior boundary

- Ordinary incremental compilation enforces current rules on pages actually changed or created while leaving unchanged legacy pages byte-stable.
- A non-incremental authoring round still evaluates the full tree and can surface legacy format debt. This PR does not add a separate manual migration command; reviewers should treat that as an explicit product boundary rather than an implicit migration workflow.

## Validation

- [x] `python test_compile_box.py`
- [x] `python test_office_ingest.py`
- [x] `python test_selfcheck.py`
- [x] `python test_redblue.py`
- [x] `python test_mtls_auth.py`
- [x] `python test_incremental.py`
- [x] `npm test -- --run` — 4,391 passed, 2 skipped
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `docker build --check -f platform/pod/Dockerfile .` (from `kbc/`)
- [x] `git diff --check`

## Architecture checklist

- [x] **Incremental boundary**: unchanged historical pages remain byte-stable and are not added to repair scope merely because they were authorized.
- [x] **Consumer compatibility**: standard Markdown links and legacy wikilinks remain supported.
- [x] **Security model**: untrusted YAML uses `safe_load`; no shell execution path changes.
- [x] **Database parity**: not applicable; no database changes.

author: dem-extra1
body:
Closes #740

`Unit._apply_flock_color()` and `_draw()` both computed `0.45 if state == State.ROUTING else 1.0` fresh every frame — a hard binary switch on `state`, so a routing/rally transition jumped translucency instantly instead of easing.

**Fix:** a persistent `_render_alpha` that eases toward its target (`ROUTING_ALPHA`/`ALPHA_FADE_RATE`) via `move_toward()` each frame in `_process()` — not `_physics_process`, since a ROUTING unit's `_physics_process` takes an early return before ever reaching that render tail (confirmed and corrected mid-implementation after an initial wrong placement).

**Scope: only the regimental flag fades.** Per design feedback during this session, the per-soldier marks (`_apply_flock_color()`'s MultiMesh modulate — body/outline/facing-pip) and the rest of the chrome (state ring, shield overlay, stat bars) always stay fully opaque now. The men themselves are still physically present and fighting/fleeing; dimming their icons doesn't represent a routing state — a wavering flag does. Only `UnitSprites.flag()`'s color/alpha reads the fading `_render_alpha`.

**Test:** four new tests in `test/unit/test_unit.gd`:
- the fade drops/rises by exactly `ALPHA_FADE_RATE * delta` this tick, not an instant snap
- it converges cleanly to `ROUTING_ALPHA` with no overshoot
- member icons (body/outline/facing-pip modulate) stay fully opaque throughout a long routing stretch while `_render_alpha` itself does fade

**Verified:** `tools/check.sh validate test chars comments` all green — full GUT suite 1420/1420 passing (1416 + 4 new).

Found via a broader snap/spring audit — confirmed the soldier-body "spring purge" (#497/#448) already eliminated spring mechanics from body arrival, and morale/fatigue/cohesion/camera were already ramping smoothly; this routing alpha was the one clear remaining candidate.

**Demo:** skipping — this is a translucency-easing timing change (a fraction-of-a-second fade vs. an instant switch) on an element (the flag) that isn't reliably legible at typical demo GIF compression/frame-rate, and the actual behavior is directly and precisely verified by the unit tests above (exact per-tick delta, convergence, and the member-icons-stay-opaque invariant) rather than by eyeballing a clip.

<!-- sparta-demo -->
### 🎬 Gameplay demo

🚫 **No gameplay clip for this PR** — The visible change is a translucency EASE (ALPHA_FADE_RATE 2.0/s, so the full 0.55 alpha delta takes ~0.275s) replacing an instant switch, on a single small flag icon -- not a new mechanic, control, or a separately-readable HUD value (confirmed: _render_alpha/ROUTING_ALPHA have no consumer outside scripts/Unit.gd, unlike PR #739's current_speed, which also drove the show_unit_speed HUD label). At typical demo GIF frame-rate/compression this sub-third-of-a-second per-pixel alpha blend on a small icon isn't reliably legible. Directly and precisely verified instead by the unit tests in test/unit/test_unit.gd: the exact per-tick delta (not a snap), clean convergence to the routing target, and that member icons stay fully opaque throughout.

author: sifatulrabbi
body:
## What

grove now creates worktree directories at `<main-root>/.worktrees/<repo>-<title>` instead of `<main-root>/.worktrees/<title>`. `<repo>` is the main repository's directory name — the same value grove already uses for the tmux session name — so worktrees from different repos stay visually distinct under the shared `.worktrees/` layout.

For example, in the `tmux-sessions` repo, `grove worktree --new fix-auth` now creates `.worktrees/tmux-sessions-fix-auth`.

## What stays the same

- **Branch name** is unchanged: `<branch_prefix><title>` (e.g. `sifatul/fix-auth`) — no repo prefix on the branch.
- **tmux session name** is unchanged: `<session_prefix><repo>-<title>` (it already carried the repo name).
- **`grove worktree --list`** still reports the un-prefixed `title`: it strips the `<repo>-` prefix from the directory basename, and falls back to the full basename for worktrees created before this change.
- The **`--json`** contract shape is unchanged — only the `path` value reflects the new naming.

## Legacy worktrees

Worktrees created before this change keep their un-prefixed directory names; grove never renames or migrates them. Because idempotent reuse now keys off the new prefixed path, re-running `--new` with such a title creates a fresh (prefixed) worktree rather than reusing the old one — and if that title's branch is still checked out in the old worktree, git refuses the add and grove surfaces the error. This is documented in the usage guide; the workaround is to remove the old worktree or pick a new title.

CI has been **red on `main`** for a while (every recent PR, incl. #88–#91, shows a failing *Backend tests* check). The failure is **not** in those PRs — it's three route-contract "unchanged" guard tests that went stale:

- `dashboard/backend/tests/test_app_composition.py::test_full_route_contract_unchanged`

Add each tuple, in sorted position, to the frozen sets:

- `EXPECTED_BACKTESTS_ROUTES` (`test_app_composition.py`) → `get_run_trades`
- `EXPECTED_FULL_CONTRACT` (`test_app_composition.py`) → all three full paths

author: lavs9
body:
Substantial completion of **quantwave-5ipk.5** (docs long-tail quality + broken-link elimination). Fixes a systemic broken-link problem that the CI doc checker was masking.

## Root cause
`check_doc_drift.py` resolved links with a directory-URL model (one `../` too many) and `continue`d past links that escape the docs tree — so it validated broken `../../../foo.md` links as fine, and only checked 10 hub pages anyway. A `mkdocs build --strict` surfaced **362** broken-link warnings.

## Two real classes fixed (both were 404ing on the live site)
- **~159 `.md`/asset links** with one extra `../`, plus 60 candlestick pages linking a non-existent `../price_action/market_structure.md` (real page is same-dir). Fixed to mkdocs's file-path resolution (its own "Did you mean" suggestions).
- **~161 directory-URL links** with a missing `../` (`[SuperTrend](supertrend/)` → `native/<page>/supertrend/` 404; correct `../supertrend/`). Verified against built HTML.

## Enforcement (respecting the "strict is brittle" concern)
- New **`scripts/check_doc_links.py`** — fast, build-free, comprehensive (all pages, dual-model resolution matching mkdocs, skips code fences/assets/api). Wired into the sanity CI job. Catches every broken link in ~1s.
- **`check_doc_drift.py`** resolver fixed to match mkdocs and to flag (not skip) links escaping docs.
- Targeted **`validation:`** block in `mkdocs.yml` for manual `--strict` runs.
- Generator `docs/upgrade_to_standards.py` fixed so regenerated footers are correct.

We deliberately did **not** gate CI on blanket `mkdocs build --strict`: after the link fixes it still emits 13 warnings, all benign (`griffe` annotations, `mkdocs_autorefs` misreading docstring examples, `README`/`index` conflicts, `api/` nav) — none are broken links, and every future PR would risk new such noise. The fast checkers achieve the goal without the brittleness.

## Verification
- `mkdocs build --strict` → **0 link warnings** (was 362)
- `check_doc_links.py`, `check_doc_latex.py`, and full `check_doc_drift.py` all pass; the new checker fails on a reintroduced broken link.

Work delegated across two Sonnet subagents (the two link classes); resolution-model + checker corrections done by the orchestrator.

## Remaining on 5ipk.5 (follow-up, non-blocking)
- 8 `mkdocs_autorefs` warnings from the 5ipk.6 docstring examples (`[0]`, `[24800.0]` read as refs); redirect-stub → `mkdocs-redirects` migration; consolidated mkdocstrings API page. None are broken links.

author: balloob
body:
During a pooled update, a single block answering with a Modbus exception PDU (e.g. illegal data address) was caught, its fields stored as `None`, and the read continued. That made a partial read fault indistinguishable from a legitimately unimplemented point — both decoded to `None` — with nothing logged or raised.

This treats it as an error instead. `_read_blocks_by_space` now re-raises the device exception as a new `BlockReadError`, and the now-unused `failed`-set machinery is removed from the bulk readers.

## `BlockReadError`

Lives in `exceptions.py` with the rest of the hierarchy and **subclasses `ModbusExceptionError`** — the device did return an exception response, so it inherits `.exception_code` (why the read was refused) and adds `.space` / `.address` / `.count` (which block failed). The original is chained as `__cause__`, and `except ModbusExceptionError` still catches it. It is exported from the top-level package.

```
ModbusError
└── ModbusExceptionError      (.exception_code)
    └── BlockReadError        (.space, .address, .count)
```

A device with genuinely optional blocks should read those on a separate component so their absence doesn't fail the update.

## Docs

Documented on `Component.async_update` (the core read path) and the exceptions reference, with `ComponentGroup` noting it inherits the behavior.

## Verification

Full suite (271) passes, mypy clean, ruff clean. Tests updated to assert the raise plus `space` / `address` / `count` / `exception_code`.

Closes #44

author: copilot
body:
The `verify-updater-manifest` CI job was failing with HTTP 403 because the GitHub API requires at least `contents: write` to access **draft** releases — `contents: read` is insufficient. Since the release remains a draft throughout the build and verify phases (only published in the final `publish-release` job), the verification step could never authenticate successfully.

## Change

```yaml
# .github/workflows/publish_and_create_version_tag.yml
verify-updater-manifest:
  permissions:
-   contents: read
+   contents: write
```

This aligns the permission with the `build-tauri` and `publish-release` jobs, which already use `contents: write` to interact with the same draft release.

author: 1589701052p-alt
body:
## Problem

On the distributed Windows `.exe` (double-clicked / GUI-launched), the Settings "Test" button for opencode and claude-code fails with:

- `binary failed to start: ENOENT: no such file or directory, uv_spawn 'opencode'`
- `binary failed to start: ENOENT: no such file or directory, uv_spawn 'claude'`

The daemon itself starts fine (`opencode probe ok` at boot), so the failure looked opencode/claude-specific.

## Root cause

`Bun.spawn`'s child PATH resolution is **case-sensitive** — libuv consults only a var literally named `PATH` (uppercase). Windows stores the registry PATH as `Path` (mixed case), and a GUI/explorer-launched daemon inherits it under that casing. So `{ ...process.env }` child envs carry a `Path` key, and the child is spawned with NO resolvable `PATH` → `ENOENT: uv_spawn '<binary>'` for every bare command resolving to a `.cmd`/`.bat` shim (opencode, claude — both npm-installed).

Why it's sneaky:
- A **shell-launched** daemon (bash, CI) gets `PATH` (uppercase) → unaffected. So `bun run` / CI never reproduce it — only the `bun build --compile` `.exe` double-clicked in explorer does.
- The **boot `--version` probe** spawns with no `env` option (inherits OS env, case-insensitively), so it passes → daemon starts fine. Only spawns that pass `env: { ...process.env }` fail: the Settings Test button (`runtimeSmoke`), real task dispatch (`runner` / `memoryDistiller` via `buildOpencodeEnv` / `buildClaudeSpawn`), and all git ops (`nonInteractiveGitEnv`).
- `git.exe` survives (real PE; CreateProcess runs it directly via a `Path`-cased env), so the failure looked opencode/claude-specific. The bug also silently breaks every git op on a GUI-launched daemon (worktree / commit / snapshot) — just not yet triggered.

The pre-existing `git-noninteractive-env.test.ts` had already documented this `Path`/`PATH` "false mismatch" but only worked around it in-test (used a marker var instead of PATH); the production bug was never fixed.

## Fix

New `normalizePathKey(env)` in `util/platform.ts` promotes a mixed-case `Path` to uppercase `PATH` in place. Wired into the 3 spawn-env builders built from `...process.env`:

- `runtime/opencode/spawn.ts` → `buildOpencodeEnv`
- `runtime/claudeCode/spawn.ts` → `buildClaudeSpawn`
- `util/git.ts` → `nonInteractiveGitEnv`

No-op on POSIX / bash-launched Windows (PATH already uppercase). Golden / source-grep locks (`runtime-opencode-golden`, `opencode-spawn-pwd-env`, `rfc143-business-spawn`) unchanged — the env literal stays; the normalize call is added after it.

## Tests

- New `tests/spawn-env-path-casing.test.ts`: `normalizePathKey` unit cases + stub behavioral red-then-green (`{Path: dir}` bare spawn ENOENTs; normalized `{PATH: dir}` exits 0) + source-grep that the 3 builders call it.
- Tightened `git-noninteractive-env.test.ts` with a PATH-passthrough assertion (now testable).
- Full backend suite: **4745 pass / 0 fail**. `typecheck` + `format:check` green.

## Verification

Reproduced the exact error on the running v1.0.1 daemon, applied the fix, rebuilt the exe, restarted the daemon. Fresh probes:

- opencode: `spawn-failed: uv_spawn 'opencode'` → **`conforms`**
- claude-code: `spawn-failed: uv_spawn 'claude'` → **`conforms`**

body:
## Summary

Authors [PEP-058: Production Release Readiness](peps/PEP-058-production-release-readiness.md) — the wave-structured plan produced by the 2026-07-11 three-way production-readiness audit (docs/README · onboarding/examples/playground · AI-affordances/publish-pipeline) — and lands Wave 1:

- **Un-breaks the release pipeline.** `.changeset/config.json`'s `ignore` list has made config validation throw on every Release run since ~April (ignored packages with non-ignored private dependents) — npm has been stale at 0.1.1 (2026-04-03) through ~20 PEPs of correctness work, with 16 changesets queued. The ignore list is removed *entirely* rather than patched: the ignored packages are public and published, so version-freezing them breaks dependency coherence (Zed npm-installs `@typesugar/lsp-server`), and queued changesets already referenced them anyway. PEP-048's freeze intent survives without version-freezing (superseded note added to its ledger). `privatePackages: { version: true, tag: false }` keeps private packages versioned (feeding `vsce` fresh versions) but never npm-published.
- **Resurrects the VS Code extension's CI tests.** The `ci.yml` filters said `@typesugar/vscode` but the package is named `typesugar-vscode` — the test jobs have been silent no-ops since they were added. Fixed (3 occurrences); unit tests verified passing locally (122 tests, 6 files). The integration harness runs and exits 0 with no test files — hollow-but-green, noted in the PEP.
- **`engines.node >=20`** on all 32 publishable packages (repo-wide patch changeset).
- **npm provenance** enabled in `release.yml` (`NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true`; `id-token: write` already granted) and the `vsce publish` step guarded to skip when the Marketplace already has the current version.
- `peps/README.md`: PEP-033 corrected to Done; PEP-058 row added.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx changeset status` exits 0 — sane bumps (typesugar/core/macros/transformer/transformer-core/std/fp/effect/contracts/playground → minor = 0.2.0; rest patch)
- [x] `pnpm --filter typesugar-vscode test:unit` — 122 tests pass; integration harness boots VS Code and exits 0

- [x] `npx prettier --check .` — clean

## ⚠️ On merge

This PR's merge will make the Release workflow produce a **"Version Packages" PR** (the 16 queued changesets + this wave's). Per PEP-058, that version PR must **NOT** be merged until Wave 3 — Wave 2 first fixes everything baked into the published artifacts (compiler-emitted typesugar.dev URLs, the init bundler-patch bug, etc.).

W2 onboarding + pre-release source fixes → W3 the 0.2.0 release (npm + Marketplace) → W4 error catalog → W5 llms.txt → W6 consumer AI context (init-scaffolded AGENTS.md + Claude Code skill) → W7 docs polish → W8 examples → W9 release verification.

author: 7robe
body:
## FSRCNNX Native Shader Support

This PR adds first-class FSRCNNX upscaling support to Harbor's libmpv player, following the same architecture as the existing Anime4K integration.

### What's added

#### `src-tauri/src/fsrcnnx.rs` — Rust backend
- `fsrcnnx_dir` — returns shader directory path if shader is present
- `fsrcnnx_download(force)` — downloads `FSRCNNX_x2_8-0-4-1.glsl` from the [igv/FSRCNN-TensorFlow releases](https://github.com/igv/FSRCNN-TensorFlow/releases) into `app_data/fsrcnnx/`
- `fsrcnnx_set` — applies the shader via `glsl-shaders` and enforces `fbo-format=rgba16f` (required for correct FSRCNNX operation)
- `fsrcnnx_clear` — clears the shader and resets `fbo-format` to `auto`

#### `src/components/player/fsrcnnx-indicator.tsx` — Player HUD badge
- Polls `glsl-shaders` every 2 s and shows a gold **FSRCNNX** badge when active
- Mirrors the `anime4k-indicator` pattern

#### `src/components/player/fsrcnnx-toggle.tsx` — Settings toggle
- Toggle switch in Settings → Player
- Auto-downloads shader on first enable (no manual file copy needed)
- Shows download progress and error states
- Disabling clears both `glsl-shaders` and `fbo-format`

### Integration needed by maintainers

1. Add `mod fsrcnnx;` and register the four commands in `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` `invoke_handler`:
   ```rust
   fsrcnnx::fsrcnnx_dir,
   fsrcnnx::fsrcnnx_download,
   fsrcnnx::fsrcnnx_set,
   fsrcnnx::fsrcnnx_clear,
   ```
2. Place `<FsrcnnxToggle />` inside the Player settings section (alongside the Anime4K toggle).
3. Place `<FsrcnnxIndicator />` in the player HUD overlay (alongside `<Anime4kIndicator />`).

### Notes
- FSRCNNX is a **live-action** upscaler; Anime4K is for animation. They should not be stacked — enabling one should ideally disable the other (the toggle components are independent for now, maintainers can add mutual exclusion).
- Only applies when the player engine is **native libmpv**.
- The shader file (~50 KB) is downloaded on demand; nothing is bundled.

Built extensions for easy testing:
https://df.cssnr.com/raw/auto-auth-0.0.0-chrome.zip
https://df.cssnr.com/raw/auto-auth-0.0.0-firefox.zip

## Wildcard Matching

Use `*` to match any subdomain or port in saved host patterns:

- `*.example.com` matches `sub.example.com` but not `a.b.example.com`
- `example.com:*` matches `example.com:8080`
- `*.*.com` matches `sub.example.com` but not `a.b.example.com`

Each `*` replaces exactly one part. If multiple patterns match, the most specific one (fewest `*` characters) is used.

```
*.example.com       ✅  sub.example.com
*.example.com       ❌  a.b.example.com
*.*.com             ❌  a.b.example.com
*.example.com       ❌  example.com
example.com:*       ✅  example.com:8080
example.com:*       ✅  example.com
example.com:8080    ✅  example.com:8080
example.com:9090    ❌  example.com:8080
*.*.com             ✅  sub.example.com
example.com         ✅  example.com
*                   ❌  example.com
*.example.com:*     ✅  sub.example.com:8080
*.example.com:9090  ❌  sub.example.com:8080
```

## Notable Changes

### `src/utils/hosts.ts`

- Added wildcard matching top level functions
- Updated `Hosts` class with wildcard matching functions

author: larry-yatch
body:
## What & why

The #914 "deep-review-held PRs on the Approvals tab" surface was showing **stale approvals for PRs that had already merged or closed** — Larry saw #823/#830/#833/#904 listed as "held for deep review" *after* they'd already resolved.

**Root cause:** `_reconcile_deep_review_held_approvals` only resolves an approval when its entry leaves `DEEP_REVIEW_HELD_FILE` — but nothing removes the entry when a PR merges/closes **out-of-band** (desktop `merge_reviewed_pr.sh`, auto-merge, manual close). The sibling self-heal in `_deep_review_hold_suppresses_dispatch` clears such stale entries, but it only fires when a Mirror review is *attempted*, which never happens for a closed PR. So the entry lingers forever and its approval stays on the tab.

## Fix

`_reconcile_deep_review_held_approvals` now self-heals against **live PR state**: an entry whose PR is definitively `MERGED`/`CLOSED` (`_gh_pr_is_open(...) is False`) is cleared from the held file and left out of `live_ids`, so `_resolve_cleared_deep_review_approvals` resolves its approval off the tab (`approved` if it carries `deep-review-passed`, else `expired`).

- **Fail-open:** an undeterminable state (`None` — gh hiccup / backoff) never prunes, so a transient error can't drop a legit hold. Mirrors step 2 of the existing `_deep_review_hold_suppresses_dispatch`.
- **Throttled:** the state recheck runs on a slow cadence (`_DEEP_REVIEW_HELD_STATE_RECHECK_INTERVAL_S`, default 600s, env-overridable) decoupled from the 60s reconcile — catching an out-of-band merge within minutes fully resolves the cosmetic lag, without adding one `gh` state call per held PR every tick to the shared GraphQL pool (which the account has exhausted before).

## Tests

`test_deep_review_held_surface.py` — +4 cases: merged-out-of-band prunes + resolves `approved`; closed-out-of-band prunes + `expired`; unknown state fail-open (kept); open PR untouched. Teaches the `gh` mock `--json state`. **15 green** (stdlib unittest).

## Review status

`deep-review-required` (touches `outbox_notifier.py`). Built + adversarially reviewed on the desktop side — the finder confirmed correctness on all axes and flagged the gh-polling cost, which the throttle above addresses. Held for the deep-review gate + manual merge, per critical-path policy.

author: qubered
body:
## Summary

Group and kit revenue now splits by **purchase value** (replacement cost × quantity) whenever the items inside don't *all* have a hire rate.

Before, the hire-rate weighting rule fired if **any** item had a rate — so a mixed set left the rate-less items at **\$0**. A \$1,000 group with a \$100/day receiver and a rate-less \$500 headset gave the receiver the whole \$1,000 and the headset nothing. For a fleet whose gear mostly has no hire rates set (the common case here), a single rated item in a group would starve everything else.

Now the rule is all-or-nothing: hire rate is used only when **every** item in the set has one; otherwise the set falls straight through to replacement cost, so nothing is left at zero and the split stays in one consistent signal. A **fully-rated** group still splits by hire rate, unchanged.

This is a one-condition change in `chooseWeights` (`weights.some(w>0)` → `weights.every(w>0)` on rule 3) and applies to kits as well — a mixed-rate kit no longer zeroes its rate-less members.

## Why purchase value

Replacement cost is the figure ROI already divides by, so for gear without hire rates it's the natural, consistent basis: each item earns a share of the bundle proportional to what it's worth to replace. Where hire rates *are* fully set, they still win (they reveal which gear rents high relative to its cost).

## Behaviour, precisely

| Group / kit contents | Split basis |
|---|---|
| Every item priced (own line total) | that line total |
| Every item has a hire rate | hire rate × qty |
| **Not all rated** (one or more rate-less) | **replacement cost × qty** ← the change |
| No rate and no cost anywhere | equal split |

## Review

Codex (high reasoning): checked the empty/single-participant edge, the recursion (each nesting level decides independently), the `selfId`/accessory-parent path, and that `SUM(children) == pool` still holds since only *which weights* changed, not the distribution. **Verdict: SAFE TO MERGE.**

## Tests

- The reported mixed group (rate-less items get their purchase share, not \$0).
- A mixed-rate kit (rate-less member earns instead of \$0).
- A fully-rated group (still splits by hire rate, not cost).
- The stale-allocation fixture updated to rate all its models so it keeps demonstrating a weighted fall-through.

## Rollout

Applies going forward automatically. Historical ROI updates on the next project edit, or immediately for all projects via `pnpm convex:backfill:revenue-allocation` after deploy.

## Test plan

- [x] 3042 unit tests pass
- [x] Typecheck clean, lint 0 errors, `npm run build` compiles
- [x] Codex: SAFE TO MERGE

author: neuromechanist
body:
Closes #92.

## Summary
Makes pyAMICA a drop-in replacement for EEGLAB's AMICA: a PyTorch NG fit can now
be written as the exact `loadmodout15` binary output directory, so it loads in
EEGLAB with the components in the same order and orientation, with no manual
re-sorting, sign-flipping, or reformatting.

Previously only the legacy NumPy backend could write this format; the primary
PyTorch backend could only `torch.save` a private dict.

## What changed
- **Shared writer** `write_amicaout()` in `numpy_impl/load.py` (co-located with its
  `loadmodout` reader counterpart): emits `gm, W, S, mean, c, alpha, mu, sbeta,
  rho, comp_list, LL`. `numpy_impl/core.py:_write_results` now delegates to it
  (byte-identical, no duplication).
- **`AMICATorchNG.write_amica_output(outdir)`** and the **`AMICA.write_amica_output`**
  wrapper (with the `_check_usable` degenerate-fit guard, #50).
- **`variance_order()`** on backend + wrapper: EEGLAB back-projected-variance order
  (IC1 = highest), using the same `W` convention real MATLAB `loadmodout15.m` uses.
- **Docs:** `docs/guides/eeglab.md` (EEGLAB interop + round-trip), wired into the nav.

## Validation (real data + Fortran binary, no mocks)
- NumPy-vs-Fortran parity tests still pass (writer refactor is byte-identical).
- New round-trip tests (`test_amica_ng_wrapper.py`): byte-fidelity of every written
  file, `loadmodout` readability + shapes, variance ordering, and the requires-fit
  guard. Full non-slow suite green (166 passed).
- **MATLAB `loadmodout15` round-trip (column-major, exactly as MATLAB reads):** on
  a converged fit (LL -3.399), `variance_order()` equals the reader's `origord`,
  svar is descending, and per-component mixture proportions sum to 1.0 -- i.e. the
  written directory is read correctly by real EEGLAB with the components in the
  right order. Matched-config IC equivalence vs Fortran stays the ~0.997 from
  `validate_implementations.py`.
- **A format defect was caught and fixed here** (see review-response comment): the
  mixture params were written C-order but EEGLAB/Fortran store column-major, so
  MATLAB would have read scrambled mixture proportions. Fixed writer + both numpy
  readers to Fortran order; single-model output is now byte-faithful to Fortran.

## Notes
- Single-model output is byte-identical to the Fortran reference. Multi-model output
  is self-consistent (round-trips through `loadmodout15`) but not byte-identical to a
  native multi-model AMICA run (issue #27 scope).
- The Python port `loadmodout` reads C-order where MATLAB reads column-major (a
  pre-existing latent transpose in the reader, out of this writer's scope); recorded
  in `.context/scratch_history.md`. The written bytes are correct for real EEGLAB.

Tested: yes (see Validation).

author: posthog[bot]
body:
## Problem

The Custom REST source AI manifest builder ("draft a manifest from docs") already handles expected backend errors gracefully: when a pasted docs URL can't be fetched (e.g. it returns a 403), the backend returns a clean 400 with a user-safe message, and the frontend shows a `lemonToast.error`.

The catch: the loader path threw the `ApiError`, which routed through the global kea-loaders `onFailure` handler in `initKea.ts` and got auto-captured into error tracking via `posthog.captureException`. So a fully-handled "fix your input" case turned into error-tracking inbox noise even though nothing was actually broken for the user.

## Changes

- In the `generateFromDocs` loader (`customSourceManifestBuilderLogic.ts`), catch the `ApiError`, toast the specific backend reason (`data.message`, or a 429 throttle's `data.detail`), and resolve to `null` instead of throwing. Because it no longer becomes a kea-loaders failure, it is no longer captured as an exception.
- Non-`ApiError` throws still re-throw, so genuinely unexpected bugs continue to surface in error tracking via the existing failure path.
- `generateFromDocsFailure` is now the fallback only for those unexpected errors.

No user-facing behavior change — the toast still shows exactly as before.

## How did you test this code?

Automated (Jest, `customSourceManifestBuilderLogic.test.ts`):

- Updated the parameterized 429/400 case to assert the handled error resolves via `generateFromDocsSuccess` and does **not** dispatch `generateFromDocsFailure`, while still toasting the backend reason — this guards the exact regression (a handled 4xx leaking to capture).
- Added a case asserting a non-`ApiError` throw still routes through `generateFromDocsFailure` (where the global handler captures it), so the suppression is scoped to handled API errors only.

All 20 tests in the file pass. Logic file typechecks clean after typegen. I did not manually exercise the UI.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

<!-- No docs affected. -->

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

Authored by PostHog Code from an inbox report about a handled 4xx (a forbidden external docs URL) leaking into error tracking as noise. Invoked the `/writing-tests` skill before changing the test to apply the value gate. Considered a global capture-suppression list in `initKea.ts` but rejected it as too broad; scoped the fix to the specific loader path instead, which is the smallest change that fully addresses the symptom while preserving capture of genuine bugs.

author: nagmo-starkware
body:
## What

Adds the **firehose-keys** transport (option **D**) — a cost-reduced alternative to the existing `firehose` transport (option **C**).

Option C opens ONE empty-filter WSS subscription and demuxes the WHOLE chain's events (~18 ev/s) in-process, keeping only the sliver it tracks — so Alchemy bills `subscribeEvents` CU for every discarded event. Option D opens MULTIPLE key-filtered subscriptions so the node only delivers events this deployment cares about:

1. **one keys-sub** on the union of option-family event selectors (Transfer/Approval excluded), chain-wide, demuxed by tracked address (foreign name-collisions dropped by the router);
2. **one address-sub per static non-wildcard contract** (ERC20 tokens, the UDC discovery address), using its configured key filter;
3. **one address-sub per active OptionToken child**, filtered to `{Transfer, Approval}` — the two ERC20 classes the keys-sub excludes — so option-token transfers stay indexed (completeness parity with C).

Each `(address, event-class)` is delivered on exactly one subscription (clean filter partition → no duplicate delivery between streams).

## Why / measured

A live 3×120s spike on the dev Alchemy mainnet endpoint measured D delivering **~23% of C's event volume** → **~77% `subscribeEvents` CU reduction**. Residual cost is ~entirely STRK (the fee token) Transfers; the option keys-sub delivered 0 events with zero foreign name-collision noise. Selector union = 21 selectors.

## Core invariant (the subtle part)

Every stream owns its **own per-address cursor**. The only cross-stream state is the tracked-membership set. An OptionToken child's cursor is touched by two streams (keys-sub for its non-Transfer events, its own address-sub for Transfer/Approval); if they shared one cursor (as C's single-stream `firehoseSink` does), the faster stream would advance past the address and the slower stream would silently drop still-unforwarded events. `TestForwardStreamPerStreamCursorIsolation` is the regression test for exactly this. Reorgs observed on any stream roll back all streams; the engine's reorg handler is idempotent so N-stream duplicate notifications are safe no-ops.

## Wiring

- Engine computes the option-selector union once at `setup()` from every wildcard contract's ABI **plus every factory's declared `ChildABI`** (resolved by name — children are discovered later but their event set is known from config), excluding Transfer/Approval.
- `ContractSubscription` gains `Wildcard`/`ERC20` classification flags, set at all (static + dynamic-child) construction sites.
- Enabled via `transport: "firehose-keys"` or `IBIS_TRANSPORT=firehose-keys`. **Option C is untouched** — the instant revert path.

## Tests

New `firehose_keys_test.go` (tracked/untracked/dedup, intra-block, **per-stream cursor isolation**, rollback-all-streams, add/remove ERC20 child, end-to-end Start) and `option_selectors_test.go` (union correctness + ChildABI dedup). `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and `go test -race` for the touched packages all pass. (Pre-existing `internal/abi` + `internal/schema` test breakage at this commit is unrelated and untouched.)

body:
Security & quality hardening sweep implementing stints 0025–0043 from the 2026-07-11 audit. One commit per stint; all 19 implemented.

## What changed (per stint)

- **0025** — `search_users` and `get_profile` now require `AuthenticatedUser` (were fully anonymous, allowing user-table enumeration / profile disclosure). Regression test asserts 401 without a token.
- **0026** — Deleted the fail-open `create_router` (it defaulted to `Development` on config error, mounting passwordless login). Production already uses `create_router_with_security_config`; the two integration tests now pass an explicit config.
- **0027** — nginx resolves the real client IP behind Railway's edge (`set_real_ip_from` + `real_ip_recursive`) and keys `limit_req` on it. `http::extract_client_ip` now trusts only the nginx-written `X-Real-IP` (no forgeable XFF); `admin.rs` consolidated onto that helper. In-process limiter's single-instance scope documented.
- **0028** — Split demo vs persistent-API deployments in-repo: `FIDO_DEPLOY_MODE` (demo/api) in `start.sh`, an API-only `nginx-api.conf`, Dockerfile default `demo`, and the installed TUI default server URL now points at the API host (not the demo). Two-service topology documented in `docs/DEPLOY.md`.
- **0029** — Per-user WebSocket connection cap (`try_connect`), `max_message_size`/`max_frame_size` on the upgrade, and an inbound-frame throttle that closes floods with a policy-violation frame. Unit + integration tests.
- **0030** — Added `idx_memberships_user_id`, `idx_posts_author_id`, `idx_notifications_user_created`. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN test asserts index use and no temp B-tree.
- **0031** — Batched feed vote lookups (`get_votes_for_posts`, one bound `IN (...)` query) replacing the per-post N+1; DM conversation list now JOINs username + conversation state so the service no longer loops.
- **0032** — `list_members` and community detail (`get_view`) now enforce `require_membership`; non-members get 403.
- **0033** — `record_vote` rejects self-votes; `notify_mentions` only notifies mentioned users who are community members.
- **0034** — TUI session temp file created `0600` via `create_new`; token refused over non-loopback `http://`/`ws://`; tungstenite capped below TRACE so `--verbose` can't leak the token; debug log created `0600`; stray `fido_debug.log` removed.
- **0035** — Repository transactions: vote write (upsert + recount) and DM soft-delete each run in one transaction; user creation is idempotent (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` + re-select), username collisions disambiguated; corrected the misleading DM request-state error message.
- **0036** — In-memory test pool now shares one DB across connections (unique named shared-cache URI); migrations propagate real errors and ignore only "duplicate column name".
- **0037** — Production startup now requires `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`; revocation-skip logs at warn; contributor check compares the current `github_login` case-insensitively; username tracks GitHub renames.
- **0038** — Server now accepts the `session_token` cookie as an auth source (CSRF-safe via SameSite=Strict); `max_request_size` config is wired into the body-limit layer; admin endpoints get a supported production grant path (`FIDO_ADMIN_LOGINS` allowlist).
- **0039** — Dockerfile base images pinned by verified multi-arch digest (`rust:1.91-bookworm`, `debian:bookworm-slim`), with a documented refresh command.
- **0040** — Documented `contains_dangerous_patterns` as a non-authoritative defense-in-depth denylist (not the XSS boundary); added a note to `security/AGENTS.md`. Verified the current `web/` client renders no user content into HTML.
- **0041** — Added `[workspace.lints.clippy]` (`all = deny`, `pedantic = warn` with the noisy lints allowed, `redundant_clone = warn`), each crate opts in, plus a GitHub Actions CI workflow (fmt/clippy/test) using verified action tags (`actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/cache@v4`).
- **0042** — Removed `#![allow(dead_code)]` from the seven v2 repository files; the layer is fully wired (all pub and used), so no feature gate or deletion was needed and no dead code remains.
- **0043** — Server `ApiError` now derives `thiserror::Error` (+ `#[non_exhaustive]`); `event_loop.rs` session-restore task uses `anyhow::Result` instead of `String`; static security headers use `HeaderValue::from_static`.

2. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — **PASS**
3. `cargo test --workspace --features sqlite-tests` — **PASS** (no failures)

author: f1uke
body:
## Problem
On macOS, closing the window **without quitting** (red button / Cmd-W) and reopening (Dock click / app activate) recreated the `BrowserWindow` at the **fixed** default size — the user's last-used size/position was lost. `createWindow()` hard-coded `width/height`, and the `activate` handler simply re-called it.

## Fix (Electron main process only — Go untouched)
New pure, unit-tested module **`frontend/src/main/window-state.ts`**:
- **`clampWindowState(saved, workAreas, opts)`** — resolves the bounds to open at. First run / no displays → default **clamped to the screen**. Otherwise clamps saved size to the **largest work area** and keeps the saved position **only if it stays visible** on some display (≥48px grabbable per axis). A position from a now-disconnected monitor is dropped so the OS re-centers instead of opening off-screen.
- **`coerceWindowState`** tolerates missing/corrupt JSON; **`readWindowStateSync`** (sync, for the `createWindow` path), **`writeWindowState`** (async, debounced), **`writeWindowStateSync`** (durable on close). Atomic temp+rename, mirroring `app-state.ts` / `update-settings.ts`.

**`frontend/src/main.ts`** wiring:
- Restore on **every** window create/re-create — the broken `activate`/reopen path now reuses saved bounds; `maximize()`/`setFullScreen(true)` restored after construction.
- Persist on `resize`/`move` (debounced 400ms), `maximize`/`unmaximize`, full-screen toggles, and **synchronously on `close`** (durable across quit). Captures `getNormalBounds()` so un-maximize restores the last normal size.
- First-run default **1320×860 → 1440×900** (old size was "too small"); clamped to fit smaller screens.

## Storage (~/.ao hard rule honored)
`~/.ao/window-state.json` (prod) / `~/.ao/dev/window-state.json` (dev) = `dirname(runFilePath())`, same dir as `app-state.json`. The `~/.ao/electron` userData pin is untouched. Never `~/Library/Application Support`.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `prettier --check` clean.
- `vitest run` — **745 pass** (78 files; +22 new in `window-state.test.ts`).
- `npm run package` — builds a valid `.app` (arm64/darwin).

## On-device checklist (main-process behavior isn't headless-verifiable)
1. Resize+move → **close without quitting** (Cmd-W) → reopen from Dock → **same size + position**.
2. Resize/move → **Cmd-Q** → relaunch → **restored**.
3. Maximize → close-without-quit → reopen → **maximized**.
4. Window on a 2nd monitor → quit → disconnect monitor → relaunch → **on primary, on-screen**.
5. First run (no `window-state.json`) → **1440×900 centered**.

body:
## What & why

Standardises the runtime-environment model so `NODE_ENV=local` is a **first-class, valid value** instead of one that crashes at boot and fails the build guard. Pairs with the sibling core-fe change (adds `local` to Vite `MODE`) so both repos share the same three-value vocabulary.

`NODE_ENV` enum: `development | production` → **`local | development | production`**.

- **`local`** = a developer's machine. `NODE_ENV=local` makes `.env.local` the **primary** file (self-contained, no `.env.development` inheritance — the existing `!== primary` check already collapses the override step). The loader logic is unchanged.
- **Default stays `development`**, so unset contexts (CI, a stock `pnpm dev`, the Vitest suite) behave exactly as before. `local` is opt-in.
- **`development` / `production` remain the only two DEPLOY targets** — the deploy-target enums in `tooling/setup/` are untouched; you never deploy to `local`.
- **Fail-loud is preserved**: `env.config.ts` eager-parses `envSchema` at module load, so an out-of-enum value (e.g. `staging`) still throws at boot — never a silent default.

## Changes

## Summary

First pass of production-readiness fixes toward the "build SIA AI as a real, working assistant" goal — this PR focuses on getting the existing `sia-lab` scaffold's own test/build pipeline actually green, since `make ci` was broken on `main`.

- `sft.py` (invoked with no args by `make smoke`) silently defaulted to a **real GPU training run** instead of `--dry-run`, crashing with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'` in any environment without the full training stack installed. Fixed the `Makefile` to pass `--dry-run` explicitly for the smoke target.
- `train_gcp.py`'s `dry_run()` unconditionally imported `trl` and failed hard if it wasn't installed — contradicting its own documented contract ("no GPU, no heavy deps"). Now treats a missing `trl` as expected/non-fatal in dry-run, while still surfacing real import/API errors if `trl` *is* installed.
- Removed the stale `--run` flag from four docs (`README.md`, `COLAB_GUIDE.md`, `sia-lab/posttrain/P1_EVAL_SUMMARY.md`, `sia-lab/posttrain/adapter/README.md`) — that flag was never a real `argparse` option on `train_gcp.py`, so anyone following the documented GPU-training command would immediately hit `error: unrecognized arguments: --run`.
- Added `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to run `make ci` and `make run` on every push/PR, so this class of regression (docs/Makefile drifting from the actual CLI) is caught automatically going forward.

## Test plan
- [x] `make ci` — now passes end-to-end (lint, validate, smoke, eval, status), previously crashed at the smoke step.

author: williamlabdev
body:
## Summary

First slice of the governance-differential benchmark plan (#5, D1–D6): `orvena bench --governance off,light,engineering` runs the same task set under each posture and reports **what the brakes buy**.

### What lands

- **Ground truth on every run**: the harness re-runs each task's `verify` after the loop, independent of any in-loop gate → every report carries `verified`/`verified_rate` next to the claimed completion rate.
- **False-done rate (M2)**: of the runs that claimed done, the fraction whose external verify fails.
- **`off` = bench-only ungoverned baseline (D2)**: identical prompt (same writable lists shown), no scope enforcement, no gates — "done" is the model's own unverified claim; the run ends on zero actions or `max_steps`. Root escape stays blocked (host protection, not governance). Crate-private (`Scope::unrestricted_baseline` + `Agent::run_ungoverned_baseline`) so no product path reaches it — the product still ships `light`/`engineering` only.
- **Matrix + differential**: per-posture false-done/verified rates and M4 cost ratios (governed/baseline steps + tokens). M1 containment waits for the independent violation oracle (slice-012, D3).

### Live-verified (offline provider, deterministic)

```
── governance differential (engineering vs off) ──
false-done:  off: 100% of claims  →  engineering: 0% of claims
verified:    off: 50%  →  engineering: 50%
overhead:    ×1.00 steps, ×1.05 tokens (governed / baseline)
```

The read-only trap task is the story in one line: the ungoverned baseline reports "2/2 solved (100%)" while ground truth shows every claim was false; under engineering the false claim is structurally impossible.

### Verification

70 tests passing (5 new integration tests + 3 new scope unit tests), `clippy -D warnings` clean, boundary check PASS, plus a live CLI matrix run.

author: hashiiiii
body:
## Summary

Upgrade the `typescript` devDependency from `6.0.3` to `7.0.2`, the GA release of the native Go compiler.

## Motivation

reknotes uses `tsc` purely as a type checker (`bunx tsc --noEmit` in `bun run check`); Bun handles runtime transpilation. TypeScript 7.0 type-checks roughly 10x faster with type-checking logic structurally identical to 6.0, so this speeds up `bun run check` locally and in CI at low risk.

Closes #174

## Changes

- Bump `typescript` from `6.0.3` to `7.0.2` (exact GA patch pin, as before) in `package.json`, update `bun.lock`.
- No change to the `check` script: at GA the `tsc` binary from the `typescript` package is the native compiler, so `bunx tsc --noEmit` works as-is.
- No `tsconfig.json` changes needed: `target`/`module: ESNext`, `moduleResolution: bundler`, `strict`, `skipLibCheck`, and `types: [bun]` are all accepted by the native compiler (verified by running it).

author: copilot
body:
Adds a bidirectional ZeroMQ bridge so pure-Python strategies (including SB3 RL agents) can plug into the same Java framework used for live trading and backtesting, with no changes to the existing Java algorithm path.

## Java — `PythonAlgorithm`

- New `PythonAlgorithm` extends `SingleInstrumentAlgorithm`; registered in `TradingAlgorithmsProvider` under prefix `"PythonAlgorithm"`
- Binds a **PUB** socket (default 7700) and publishes `depth` / `trade` / `execution_report` events as versioned JSON envelopes: `{"v":1,"type":"...","instrument":"...","data":{...}}`
- Binds a **PULL** socket (default 7701); background thread deserialises incoming commands (`order_request`, `quote_request`, `request_info`) and routes them to `sendOrderRequest` / `sendQuoteRequest` / `requestInfo`
- `QuoteRequest.instrument` is resolved via `Instrument.getInstrument(pk)` rather than blind GSON deserialization
- Config parameters: `python_md_pub_port`, `python_cmd_pull_port`, `python_host`

## Python — `python/python_algo/`

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `messages.py` | Versioned dataclasses: `DepthMsg`, `TradeMsg`, `ExecutionReportMsg`, `Envelope` (inbound); `OrderRequestCmd`, `QuoteRequestCmd`, `RequestInfoCmd` (outbound) |
| `transport.py` | `Transport` ABC + `ZmqTransport` (SUB ← Java PUB, PUSH → Java PULL) |
| `strategy.py` | `PythonStrategy` ABC — `on_depth` / `on_trade` / `on_execution_report` callbacks; blocking `run()` or single-step `step()` |
| `live_env.py` | `PythonAlgoEnv` — Gymnasium env for SB3; abstract `observe` / `reward` / `act`; works identically in backtest and live |

```python
from python_algo import PythonStrategy, ZmqTransport, OrderRequestCmd

class MyStrategy(PythonStrategy):
    def on_depth(self, depth):
        self.send_order(OrderRequestCmd(
            depth.instrument, "Buy", "Limit", quantity=0.01, price=depth.best_bid
        ))
    def on_trade(self, trade): ...
    def on_execution_report(self, er): ...

transport = ZmqTransport(md_sub_port=7700, cmd_push_port=7701)
transport.subscribe("")          # all instruments
MyStrategy(transport).run()      # blocking event loop
```

For SB3 training, subclass `PythonAlgoEnv` and implement `observe` / `reward` / `act`, then pass to any SB3 model directly.

author: nya-a-cat
body:
## Summary

- Include `<cuda_device_runtime_api.h>` in the SM90 and SM100 HyperConnection pre-norm GEMM kernels.
- Make the `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()` declaration available to the NVRTC compilation path.

## Root cause

Both HyperConnection kernels call the Programmatic Dependent Launch synchronization intrinsic. With `DG_JIT_USE_NVRTC=1`, the current include chain does not expose its device-runtime declaration, so NVRTC fails with:

```text
identifier "cudaGridDependencySynchronize" is undefined
```

NVCC provides the declaration implicitly in this path, which is why the failure is NVRTC-specific.

## Impact

This restores NVRTC compilation for both SM90 and SM100 HyperConnection kernels. It does not change kernel logic, synchronization behavior, or launch configuration.

## Validation

- CUDA 12.9.1 NVRTC compile-only regression:
  - [Before the fix](https://github.com/nya-a-cat/DeepGEMM/actions/runs/29105589876): SM90 compilation fails with the undefined identifier above.
  - [After the fix](https://github.com/nya-a-cat/DeepGEMM/actions/runs/29108998119): the SM90 and SM100 header instantiations compile successfully.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`

GPU runtime validation was not performed because the Actions runner did not have an NVIDIA GPU.

Fixes #359

author: mrubens
body:
## Problem

Enabling the Zero integration breaks every subsequent task at environment start:

```
Command failed with exit code 127: opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 33175 ...
/home/roomote/.local/bin/opencode: line 2: /sandbox/node_modules/.bin/opencode: No such file or directory
```

### Root cause

With npm 7+, `npm install --prefix <dir> --no-save <pkg>` reifies the prefix's `node_modules` down to just the requested package's tree — everything else is pruned. (Verified empirically: installing package A then package B this way silently deletes A.)

The worker image bakes `opencode-ai` + `node-pty` into `/sandbox/node_modules`, with `~/.local/bin/opencode` as a shim pointing at `/sandbox/node_modules/.bin/opencode`. When Zero is enabled, `installZeroCli` runs at task start (`run-task.ts`) — before the harness launches `opencode serve` — and installs `@zeroxyz/cli` into that same `/sandbox` prefix. npm prunes `opencode-ai` and `node-pty`, the shim's target vanishes, and `opencode serve` exits 127.

`installAgentClis` already guards against this hazard for its own package set (that's why `getSharedSandboxRuntimePackageSpecs` installs `opencode-ai` and `node-pty` in a single npm command); `installZeroCli` didn't follow the pattern.

## Fix

Install the Zero CLI into a dedicated prefix, `/sandbox/zero-cli`, so the two installs can't reify each other away in either direction. The `~/.local/bin/zero` wrapper now points at `/sandbox/zero-cli/node_modules/.bin/zero`. A new `resolveZeroCliInstallRoot` helper documents the constraint so the prefixes don't get reunified later.

No migration needed: fresh sandboxes start from the baked image with opencode intact, and older sandboxes with `zero` at the legacy location keep working (the version check passes through the existing wrapper).

## Validation

- `agent-clis` unit tests updated to pin the dedicated prefix and wrapper target; all pass
- `lint`, `check-types`, `knip` clean (pre-push hooks)
- Reproduced the npm prune behavior and confirmed the nested-prefix layout isolates installs both ways using a scratch npm prefix

author: legacyasphere-id
body:
## Summary
- `KnowledgeUpload.tsx`: replaces the static placeholder with a real dropzone (click or drag-drop), client-side validation (PDF/TXT/DOCX, 10MB cap) before hitting the API, upload status messaging, and a document list that refreshes after a successful upload.
- `knowledge/page.tsx`: fetches the initial document list server-side via the service-role client (bypasses RLS so the list always renders, independent of the admin session — upload itself still requires auth via the API route) and passes it to `KnowledgeUpload` as `initialDocuments`.

`src/app/api/knowledge/route.ts` is fully untouched, per instructions.

## Two corrections to the supplied code
Neither touches the forbidden API route:
- `page.tsx` imported `createServiceClient` from a nonexistent `@/lib/supabase/service` module — it actually lives in `@/lib/supabase/server`, where every other file in this codebase already imports it from. Would have been a build-breaking module-not-found error otherwise.
- `KnowledgeUpload`'s `fetchDocuments()` expected the GET response shaped as `{documents: [...]}`, but the existing (untouched) route returns a plain array — so refetching after upload would have always reset the list to empty, silently defeating the "document list" half of this PR. Changed to read the array directly.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] `npm run build` succeeds
- [x] Diff confirmed scoped to exactly the 2 specified files (`git diff --stat` vs `main`)

author: sanketsahu
body:
Follow-up work on top of the (now-merged) #26. Groups several playground/UX polish commits plus a node-compat correctness fix.

## node-compat: return to the prompt after prompt-based CLIs
`create-expo-app` and similar CLIs finish their work but leave stdin in raw mode with a stray keypress listener that's never torn down. The node runner's quiescence loop saw an "active" stdin consumer and hung until the user pressed Enter, instead of returning to the shell prompt.

The old consecutive-tick counters couldn't handle it: after the CLI finishes, `isActive()`/rawMode *flicker* (the leftover listener toggles), resetting the counters before they reached threshold. Reworked to be wall-clock based — track the last moment real work happened (async op in flight, new module loading, or fresh user input) and stop once nothing meaningful has moved for a grace window (500ms once an ESM main resolves, 2.5s otherwise so a slow-to-answer CJS prompt isn't cut short). Adds `stdin.inputSeq` to tell genuine input from a leftover listener.

Verified: create-expo-app returns to the prompt on its own (no Enter needed) and the shell accepts the next command; ESM and CJS scripts that leave a raw-mode keypress listener both exit gracefully.

## Playground UX
- Replace the "Show commands" button with a first-position, non-selected **README.md** tab in terminals (only for examples that have one).
- Drop redundant `cd <dir>` lines from README snippets where the cwd is already that directory.
- Dull the playground border lines (lower contrast).

## Docs / harness
- `ROADMAP.md` — North Star, scope, and phased roadmap (benchmarks, single distributable binary for isolated host VMs, tunnelling / Docker-free).
- `bench/` — runnable Node benchmark harness (boot, command throughput, fs, memory).

author: wallydoodlez
body:
## #13397 — Fix flaky static-gate test: test_wizard_13337_deny_list.py::TestCli::test_cli_unknown_flag_exits_2

A flaky test *inside the static gate* is a false-negative ship blocker — any agent running the gate can hit a spurious red and reblock a clean PR. This closes it.

### Root cause
`cmd_merge_deny_list`'s unknown-flag / usage-error path is a **deterministic** `exit(2)` (an unknown flag is caught before any FS read and returns 2). The **only fallible operation** on that path is the `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` that precedes the `return 2`. Under heavy concurrent I/O in the full static gate, a transient stderr-pipe write failure raised, propagated unhandled through `sys.exit(main())`, and terminated the process with **Python's unhandled-exception code 1** — flipping the intended `exit(2)` into a spurious `exit(1)`.

This matches every observed symptom: deterministic logic, exit-1 = Python's unhandled-exception code, and unreproducible in isolation. I ran the exact subprocess **280 times (120 sequential + 160 concurrent @ 16 workers)** — all returned 2, zero exit-1. The flake only manifests under full-suite load, consistent with a load-induced stderr-write failure rather than a logic bug.

### Fix
- **wizard.py** — new `_cli_usage_error(message)` guards the stderr write (`try/except`, best-effort message; the exit code is the contract the caller asserts). Both usage-error sites in `cmd_merge_deny_list` route through it, so a transient write failure can no longer turn `exit(2)` into `exit(1)`.
- **test `_run`** — explicit `cwd=REPO_ROOT` + `encoding="utf-8"` (isolate the subprocess environment, matching the sibling `test_cli_dispatch_registered`) so an inherited cwd or locale-dependent stdio encoding cannot perturb the assertion.
- **regression** — three locks:
  - `test_unknown_flag_returns_2_in_process` — the exit-2 contract at the logic level (both usage-error sites), no subprocess.
  - `test_usage_error_returns_2_even_if_stderr_write_fails` — simulates the exact vector (stderr write raises) and asserts exit stays 2. **Fails against the old unguarded code** (the raise would propagate out as an error).
  - `test_cli_unknown_flag_exit_2_is_deterministic` — 6× subprocess loop.

### Honest scope note
The exit-1 was **not reproducible in isolation**, so I can't claim 100% elimination of every conceivable full-suite interaction. The fix closes the one identifiable in-code exception vector on this path *and* isolates the test environment, and the regression locks the vector deterministically. Scoped to the reported command (no refactor of other CLI usage-error sites — the guard pattern generalizes if another CLI test ever flakes the same way).

### Verification
- New/updated suite green: `tests/test_wizard_13337_deny_list.py` 25 passed.
- Full static gate: **5289 gated, 0 failures, 0 errors.**

Reported by: qa. Cross-ref: #13337 (source of the test), #13369 (verification run that surfaced it), #13352 (prior test-determinism class).

body:
## Summary

Harden local and CI builds, repair worker-only runtime failures discovered through a real Docker upload, update dependency tooling, and align the documentation with the current application.

Closes #332
Closes #333
Closes #334
Closes #337

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Refactor
- [x] CI / tooling

## What changed

- Align Node 22 and pnpm 11 across Docker, CI, and package metadata; patch audited frontend dependencies and allow the Sharp install script.
- Build one deterministic backend image per Compose profile and pin PostgreSQL/pgvector, Redis, and MinIO images.
- Lazily initialize storage in RQ worker processes, serialize NumPy embeddings safely for pgvector, and prevent duplicated MinIO endpoint paths.
- Remove the scoped SQLAlchemy, naive UTC, and pytest collection warnings.
- Update the README and documentation index for the current UI, vault, sharing, models, and light/full runtime profiles.
- Add focused regressions for worker storage initialization, MinIO URLs, duplicate detection, and reprocessing.

## Root cause and impact

The API initialized storage during FastAPI lifespan startup, but RQ workers run in separate processes and never execute that lifespan. In addition, NumPy's string representation is not a valid pgvector literal, and the configured MinIO bucket path could be prepended twice during presigned URL rewriting. These defects allowed healthy containers to fail during real image processing.

After this change, a first-run light-stack build is reproducible and a fresh upload completes indexing with working original and thumbnail URLs.

## Screenshots / recordings

No visual behavior changed. The production UI routes were smoke-tested from the rebuilt Docker image.

docker compose -f docker-compose.light.yml config --quiet

body:
Follow-up to #3088 (which auto-merged before this review fix could land on the branch). Adversarial review finding:

`hindsightImageRef` floats non-normalizable tags to `:latest`, so `switchroom memory setup --tag sha-deadbeef` printed "Using hindsight image tag sha-deadbeef (explicit --tag)" but actually pulled and ran `:latest` — a silent un-pin plus a lying status line, the exact footgun class #2857 exists to close.

## Fix
- `resolveMemorySetupTag` now normalizes an explicit `--tag` to canonical `vX.Y.Z`, so the printed tag is EXACTLY the tag that runs.
- A non-normalizable, non-`latest` explicit tag returns `reason: "invalid"`; the CLI exits 1 with an error naming the valid forms (`vX.Y.Z`, `X.Y.Z`, `latest`) instead of silently floating.
- Other `hindsightImageRef`/`startHindsight` callers audited: `src/cli/setup.ts` passes `undefined`; update/rollout thread tags already validated by `resolveHindsightPinTag`.

## Tests

author: hayahaya-ai
body:
## What changed

- close the Phase 5.1 release-candidate correctness gaps with paired adversarial fixtures and an eight-repository calibration resweep
- add first-class `destructive-agent-authority` detection for Codex full access, Claude permission bypass, and inherited subagent authority
- model occurrence-connected destructive filesystem reachability to developer home data
- recognize structurally valid destructive-command hooks as defense in depth without treating them as filesystem containment
- distinguish workspace/read-only sandboxes from host-wide destructive authority
- update verdict, issue, fleet, schema, analyst, plugin, and operator guidance contracts
- expand Story Lab from 57 to 72 worlds, including connected/disconnected guards, script/direct-API bypasses, recovery-only evidence, and safe inverses

## Why

A well-intentioned agent does not need malicious instructions to cause catastrophic damage. Full host filesystem authority can turn an ordinary cleanup mistake into irreversible deletion of developer data. The previous three-family benchmark did not represent that active authority path, and a command guard alone cannot contain script indirection, direct filesystem APIs, uncovered routes, or fail-open behavior.

## Impact

Ariadne now reports host-destructive authority as a distinct reckless family, points operators first to workspace/read-only sandboxing or ephemeral isolation, and preserves per-occurrence path identity so unrelated safe runtimes and controls cannot protect unsafe ones. All previous exposure families retain 100% precision and recall.

## Validation

- `make check`
- `make eval` — 72/72 verdict accuracy; 100% precision/recall for all four families
- `make verify-first-run`
- Phase 5.1 exact pinned eight-repository calibration resweep: 8/8 complete, 0 errors

Potential fix for [https://github.com/Bryan-Roe/Aria/security/code-scanning/2257](https://github.com/Bryan-Roe/Aria/security/code-scanning/2257)

To fix this class of issue, ensure multiplication is performed in the destination wider type (`size_t`) by casting operands **before** multiplying.

Best fix here (without changing functionality): in `pxt_modules/screen/image.cpp`, inside `scroll()` at the `dx < 0` branch, change the `memmove` length argument from `(w - dx) * bh` to `static_cast<size_t>(w - dx) * static_cast<size_t>(bh)`. This mirrors the existing safe style already used at line 514 and keeps logic identical.

No new methods or dependencies are needed; no imports are required.

author: digitalesich
body:
## Problem

Parents had to manually start network discovery and enter a pairing code before selecting a child device. This felt technical and added unnecessary steps for a same-Wi-Fi/LAN-first product.

## Solution

- Parent discovery starts automatically when entering the parent screen and stops on leave.
- The global pairing-code field is removed from the main discovery view.
- The primary flow is now: open parent mode, see nearby child devices, tap one.
- Unknown or pairing-reset devices open a pairing dialog that asks for the code shown on the child device, then stores the child as trusted and connects.
- Known valid children connect directly without any pairing dialog or feedback warning.
- QR scan stores the trusted pairing only and does not auto-start listening.
- A feedback guidance notice is shown only for new pairing flows, reminding the parent to move away from the child device before listening.

## Why this approach

This follows the agreed direction of making discovery and pairing the normal flow, similar to selecting a Wi-Fi network. It keeps manual address entry and Wi-Fi Direct as advanced fallbacks. The feedback warning is scoped to new pairings only, because connecting to a known child normally happens when the devices are already in separate rooms.

## Verification

- ./gradlew assembleDebug
- ./gradlew assembleDebugAndroidTest
- ./gradlew assembleRelease testReleaseUnitTest lintRelease

## Partially addresses

- #147 — Restructure DiscoverScreen into guided parent connection flow with auto-start after QR scan. This PR implements automatic discovery and pairing-after-selection. The remaining QR-scan-guided transitional state and typed `QrScanResult` from #147 are not included.

## License confirmation

I confirm that this contribution is made under the project license, GPLv3 or later.

## Summary

- render `code` inside `pre` as a block so its padding applies evenly to every line
- keep inline code styling and long highlighted-line scrolling unchanged

Fixes #151

## Root cause

The theme applies `padding: 2px` to all inline `code` elements. In Firefox, a multiline inline `code` element applies its inline-start padding to the first line fragment, shifting that line two pixels to the right of the remaining lines.

## Verification

- reproduced with Firefox 148.0.2 and the reported Hugo 0.147.7 build: first-line `x=282`, remaining lines `x=280`
- after the change, all ten lines start at the same position on desktop and at a 463px mobile viewport
- verified the same alignment in Chromium
- verified highlighted blocks keep aligned line-number and source columns
- verified long highlighted lines still scroll horizontally and retain their full-width background
- built the example site with Hugo 0.147.7 and Hugo 0.164.0 using the CI build flags
- ran `npm test`

author: jwincltd
body:
The custom gesture was fighting Safari instead of getting out of its way. Two of our own CSS rules were the actual bug all along:

- `overscroll-behavior: none` on the body **disabled Safari's native pull-to-refresh** outright.
- `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the thesis/firm scroll wraps **blocked scroll chaining**, so the browser never received the pull on those tabs — which is why native refresh only ever worked on Your book.

Now:
- **Safari: zero custom code.** Native vertical overscroll restored, chaining unblocked — Safari's own pull-to-refresh works on all four tabs exactly as it does on every other site.
- **Home-Screen app only:** the custom wheel (page-follows-finger + iOS spinner) remains, because iOS provides no native gesture there; the body bounce is suppressed in that mode only so the pull isn't eaten by `touchcancel`.

Verified headless: browser mode has no `#ptr` element, `overscroll-behavior-y: auto` everywhere, pull gestures produce zero custom side effects; standalone mode keeps the working wheel with bounce suppressed.

author: yamam
body:
Fixes #5355.

## Summary
Avoid copying plugin WASM assets when the destination already contains
identical contents.
Previously, `move_plugin_to_assets()` always copied release plugin
artifacts into `zellij-utils/assets/plugins`, even when the generated
WASM file had not changed.
This updated the destination file's modification time, causing Cargo to
consider `zellij-utils` stale and triggering rebuilds of dependent
native crates (`zellij-utils`, `zellij-server`, `zellij-client`, and
the main `zellij` binary).
## Changes
- Compare source and destination plugin assets before copying
- Skip the copy when the files are identical
- Continue copying when:
  - the destination file does not exist
  - file sizes differ
  - file contents differ
## Result
The following workflow now reuses existing native build artifacts:
```sh
cargo xtask build --release
cargo xtask build --release
```
Likewise:
```sh
cargo xtask build --release
cargo xtask install ~/.cargo/bin
```
no longer rebuilds native crates when plugin assets are unchanged.
## Notes
This change only affects release builds, where
`move_plugin_to_assets()` is used.
Debug builds continue to use the existing plugin stamp mechanism.

/cf worker domains <worker>

author: pauldiepold
body:
## Problem

Google stellte die Startseite in der Suche ungünstig dar:
- **Titel vertauscht/umgeschrieben** ("Jugendarztpraxis Holstein-Diepold & Dr. Diepold: Kinder")
- **Snippet zeigte die erste News** statt eines Intro-Textes, weil sie die einzige prominente Textstelle mit dem Praxisnamen war.

Ursache in beiden Fällen: Googles algorithmisches Title-/Snippet-Rewriting, weil der Titel am Längenlimit lag und mit einem generischen Begriff begann, und kein besserer Snippet-Kandidat existierte.

## Änderungen

- **Titel** (`app/pages/index.vue`): `Holstein-Diepold & Dr. Diepold – Kinderarztpraxis Northeim` (Marke + Ort zuerst, kürzer).
- **titleTemplate** (`nuxt.config.ts`): Unterseiten-Suffix → `Holstein-Diepold & Dr. Diepold`.
- **Meta-Description** (Startseite + `site.description`): mit Praxisname + Ort.
- **Hero-Text**: doppelte Begrüßung entfernt, Name/Ort/Leistungen personlich eingewoben → starker Snippet-Kandidat.
- Business-Name (schema.org / og:site_name) bewusst **unverändert** (echter Entitätsname).
- `TeamMemberCard.vue`: nur Lint-Formatierung.

## Hinweis

Wirkung in der Suche erst nach erneutem Google-Crawl sichtbar (per Search Console beschleunigbar).

author: darylemb
body:
## 🔴 Problem

PR #26 introduced `directory.exclude` using **YAML list syntax**, but Argo CD's CRD expects a **string**:

```
The Application "root-app" is invalid: spec.source.directory.exclude:
Invalid value: "array": spec.source.directory.exclude in body must be
of type string: "array"
```

When applied directly to the cluster, the list syntax fails validation. Root-app remained `OutOfSync` until manually patched with string syntax.

## 🔧 Fix

Changed `directory.exclude` from YAML list to **quoted string**:

```diff
   directory:
-    exclude:
-      - disk-usage-alerts.yaml
+    exclude: "disk-usage-alerts.yaml"
```

## 📋 Verification

Verified working: I patched the cluster directly with the string syntax (`exclude: "disk-usage-alerts.yaml"`) and root-app moved from `OutOfSync / ComparisonError` → `Synced / Healthy`. The same PrometheusRule ownership conflict resolved cleanly:

| App | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `root-app` | OutOfSync / ComparisonError | **Synced / Healthy** |
| `disk-usage-alerts` | Synced / Healthy | **Synced / Healthy** |

## ⚠️ Why this matters

If we don't merge this fix, the next time someone re-applies bootstrap/root-app.yaml (e.g. disaster recovery, fresh cluster), root-app will fail validation and break the entire GitOps chain.

## 🎯 Bonus: kube-prometheus-stack still Progressing

Once you merge this, the only remaining issue is `kube-prometheus-stack` showing `Health: Progressing` because the node-exporter DaemonSet pod on `rocky-worker` reports `Ready: False`. This is a kubelet issue on the rocky node (condition propagation), not Argo. Suggested next step: `systemctl restart k3s-agent` on rocky-worker.
