body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @agent-native/core@0.98.0

### Minor Changes

-   38ca6fa: Add an opt-in projected resource load to access checks so callers that only need the access decision can skip fetching heavy resource columns. Default behavior unchanged.

    `resolveAccess()`/`assertAccess()` now accept `{ skipResourceBody: true }` (as the trailing options argument) to load only the columns the access decision itself reads — `id`, `ownerEmail`, `orgId`, `visibility` — instead of the full resource row (`resource` is typed as `AccessProjectedResource` in this mode). This is automatically ignored, falling back to a full row load, for any resource type registered with a `publicAccessRole` _function_ resolver, since that callback can read arbitrary resource fields the projection would have omitted. Passing nothing (the default) is a pure no-op: `loadResourceForAccess` still runs `db.select()` exactly as before, so none of the ~317 existing `assertAccess`/`resolveAccess` call sites change behavior.

    This is a mechanism only — no call sites are migrated in this change. `templates/design/actions/update-design.ts`'s bare `assertAccess("design", id, "editor")` — which currently pulls the full `data` blob it doesn't otherwise need — was the motivating example and is the intended first adopter as a follow-up. Note: the `"design"` resource type itself is registered with a dynamic `publicAccessRole` resolver (`publicDesignAccessRole`), which the guard above always excludes from projection, so that specific call would keep loading the full row even after opting in; `"design-system"` (checked a few lines later in the same action) has no such resolver and is a real candidate. Follow-up migration work should account for this per resource type rather than assuming every `assertAccess`/`resolveAccess` call site benefits.

### Patch Changes

-   38ca6fa: Fix realtime voice microphone selection, connection teardown, stalled sessions, and compact audio-reactive controls.
-   38ca6fa: Add an optional `agentInputSchema` to `defineAction` — a Standard Schema used ONLY to build the tool definition advertised to the model/MCP/A2A listings, while runtime validation keeps enforcing the full `schema`. Applied it in `templates/plan` to `create-visual-plan`, `create-ui-plan`, `create-plan-design`, `create-prototype-plan`, `update-visual-plan`, and `update-local-plan-folder`: their advertised `content`/`contentPatches` block shapes now show a compact `type` enum plus a pointer to `get-plan-blocks` instead of embedding the full per-block-type union, cutting each action's serialized tool definition by roughly half to three-quarters (largest actions went from ~55-58KB down to ~24-27KB; the rest from ~45-47KB down to ~13-15KB) without changing what content is accepted or how validation errors are reported.
-   38ca6fa: Default app chats to compact first-turn tool and resource catalogs, keep uncommon actions, instructions, and integrations discoverable on demand, parallelize resource summaries, and record first-request prompt and tool payload sizes in run diagnostics.
-   38ca6fa: Add optional content-free positive, negative, and neutral message sentiment tracking, enabled by default for first-party hosted apps with GPT-5.6 Luna.
-   38ca6fa: Advertise and accept the standard `offline_access` OAuth scope so ChatGPT MCP apps can retain refresh-token access without repeated sign-in.
-   38ca6fa: Removed the long-deprecated `ProductionAgentPanel` and `useProductionAgent` client exports (superseded by `AgentSidebar`/`AgentToggleButton`). No internal consumers remained.
-   38ca6fa: Track content-free positive and negative sentiment events for explicit agent response feedback, including the associated model when available.
-   38ca6fa: Render one cacheable, session-independent app shell for normal page requests and gate private UI through `AppProviders` on the client. Explicit auth pages remain cached login documents, signed-in visitors redirect without cache-buster query loops, APIs/actions remain server-protected, and generated edge workers now enforce the same anonymous public-shell cache policy as Nitro and Netlify.
-   38ca6fa: Keep React Router hydration scoped to an app's workspace mount path so index redirects and nested pages route correctly.
-   38ca6fa: Coalesce Nitro dev full-reloads so bursts of file edits trigger one server re-import instead of one per file.
-   38ca6fa: Reduce serialized tool-schema payload on background agent runs. `webhook-handler.ts` and `google-docs-poller.ts` now defer framework-added tools (integration memory, `call-agent`) behind an attached `tool-search` entry on the first request, keeping only the app's own actions visible up front — `createIntegrationsPlugin` supplies the app action names via a new `initialToolNames` option. `scheduler.ts` (`SchedulerDeps.getInitialToolNames`), `dispatcher.ts` (`TriggerDispatcherDeps.getInitialToolNames`), and `agent-teams.ts` (`AgentTeamRunConfig.initialToolNames`) gained the same opt-in filtering plumbing (tool-search attach + `filterInitialEngineTools` + `availableTools` for mid-run expansion), inactive by default so existing behavior is unchanged until a caller supplies an initial tool list.
-   38ca6fa: Reduce first-request token usage further: recurring jobs and automation triggers now defer framework-addition tools behind tool-search instead of always seeing the full registry; the MCP `ask_app` inner loop now uses the same compact initial-tool surface as interactive chat and A2A; the corpus-tools prompt (provider-api-request/provider-corpus-job/query-staged-dataset/run-code) no longer teaches tools by name that are missing from the first request's active tool set; oversized LEARNINGS.md/MEMORY.md content is capped instead of inlined in full outside lazy-context mode; and the First-Session Personalization block is now gated on the owner's persisted `personalization` flag instead of thread history, so a thread's system prompt stays byte-identical across turns 1 and 2 (fixing a prompt-cache break on every thread's second request).
-   38ca6fa: Keep realtime voice setup actions on one line, describe Builder credits as free, and prevent false setup prompts by cross-checking successful connection statuses.
-   38ca6fa: Explain browser loopback permissions and bridge lifecycle requirements when serving local Plans.
-   38ca6fa: Motion polish across shared UI: overlay primitives (tooltip, popover, select, context/menubar menus) now scale from their trigger, exit with ease-out, and respect prefers-reduced-motion; new shared easing tokens (--ease-drawer, --ease-collapse, --ease-out-strong); press feedback on the shared Button and composer send button; GPU-friendly progress fills; chat tool cells (files-changed/edit/write) animate open/closed like other disclosures.

author: lovishtater
body:
## Summary
This fork was compromised as part of the PolinRider incident (2026-07-06, DPRK-linked actor using a stolen OAuth token). This fork has ~180 commits ahead of upstream from years of accepted PRs (normal, unrelated to the attack), so no attempt was made to find a single "amended" commit — the current working tree/HEAD was audited and cleaned directly.

## What was removed (in a new commit, on top of current HEAD)
- `.vscode/` directory — `tasks.json`/`settings.json` contained tasks configured with `"runOn": "folderOpen"` that execute `node ./public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2` automatically when the folder is opened in VS Code.
- `public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2` — a fake font file (wrong magic bytes `20202020` instead of the real woff2 magic `774f4632`) that is actually the malicious payload being executed by the task above.

## What was preserved
- No commits were reverted, reset, or rewritten — all ~180 commits ahead of upstream (legitimate accepted PRs) remain intact.
- All legitimate FontAwesome font files (`fa-brands-400.woff2`, `fa-regular-400.woff2`, `fa-solid-900.woff2`, etc.) were kept untouched — only the single fake-magic-byte file was removed.

## Do NOT merge until reviewed.

author: siongsheng
body:
## Why
The architecture reviewer ran clean of denials (0 after #23) but posted **nothing** — `claude-code-action`'s inline-comment model buffers no comment for a clean/grouped review, so the Claude-family **architecture floor was a silent no-op**, and stayed green (#27; the arch side of the #28 masking gap). It also never passed an explicit `github_token` (#19).

## Impact to Stakeholders
- The architecture review is now **always visible** on every PR — including a clean "no issues found" confirmation, so reviewers can tell "reviewed, sound" from "not reviewed."
- A run that produces nothing is a **loud `::error::`**, never a green no-op.

## What's in this PR
Mirrors the findings-ledger fix (#29) — split **analysis (agent)** from **posting (bash)** in `architecture-review.yml` (template + dogfood copy):
- **Gather diff** (bash) → `.arch-review/diff.patch`.
- **Compose** — agent reads the diff + uses `Read/Grep/Glob` on the repo, WRITES `.arch-review/arch-review.md` (posts nothing). Kept on the **default model** (deep reasoning, unlike the ledger's mechanical compose → Haiku).
- **Post** (bash) — normalizes a fenced output, **asserts the `## 🏛️ Architecture Review` marker**, then PATCHes the one sticky comment (else POSTs). Missing/malformed file → `::error::` + skip.
- Passes `github_token` (#19); `pull-requests: read → write` for the sticky post.

## Notable decision
Reused the exact compose→post pattern (and the awk-normalize + marker-assert hardening) from #29 so both CI agent-reviewers behave identically and neither can silently no-op or self-duplicate. Kept the review criteria/prompt unchanged.

## Validation
- YAML parses; `bash -n` clean on all `run:` blocks; template ↔ dogfood body identical (header-only diff); `bin/tdd-check` PASS (`ci:` commit).
- awk-normalize + marker-assert + jq `startswith` logic verified locally (same as #29).
- **Behavior only testable post-merge** — `claude-code-action` skips a workflow a PR modifies, so the Compose step won't run on this PR (the Post step will emit its `::error::` no-op, as designed). The first PR after merge exercises it: an architecture comment should appear even when clean.

Closes #19 · Closes #27 · Refs #28 (ledger side handled by #29)

author: patrob
body:
## Summary

Nightly eval regressions used to die silently as a red Actions run — the per-case
detail lived only in the job log. This wires the existing baseline comparison up to
`gh issue create`/`gh issue edit` so a regression opens (or updates) a single, stable
`evals`-labeled GitHub issue with per-case pass/rubric deltas and a link to the run.
A green night still files nothing.

## Changes

- New pure formatter `formatRegressionIssue` in `@on-par/factory-core` turns an eval
  summary + baseline + comparison into a deterministic Markdown issue body (marker
  comment, overall pass rate, a per-case delta table, regressions, and notes).
- New `scripts/regression-issue.ts` CLI (`npm run regression-issue`) recomputes the
  baseline comparison from the saved report/baseline JSON and writes the issue body
  to a file only when there's a real regression — the file's existence is the
  workflow's gate for whether to call `gh` at all.
- `.github/workflows/nightly-evals.yml`: the eval step now `continue-on-error`s so
  later steps can run on failure; on regression it builds the issue body, dedupes
  against any existing open issue titled "Nightly eval regression" by exact title
  match (update + comment instead of duplicate), and re-fails the job afterward so
  the nightly still shows red.
- Fixed a bug found in review: `gh --jq`'s "no existing issue" result is the literal
  string `null`, which was passing the shell's `-n` truthiness check and routing the
  very first regression into `gh issue edit` (which fails, since issue "null" doesn't
  exist) instead of `gh issue create`. Added `// empty` to the jq filter so a missing
  match is genuinely empty.
- Escaped `|` characters in case IDs before they're interpolated into the Markdown
  table, so an ID containing a pipe can't corrupt the table layout.

## Testing

- [x] `scripts/verify.sh` green (build, typecheck, unit tests incl. `--coverage`,
      stub eval) — 165 tests passing
- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] Manual smoke test of `regression-issue.ts`: verified it writes the expected
      Markdown body on a synthetic regression, and writes nothing (correct
      exit code, no file) on a synthetic green comparison
- [x] `/code-review` (high effort, workflow-backed) and `/security-review` run
      against this branch; the two correctness bugs they surfaced are fixed above,
      security review reported no findings

## Notes for reviewers

A few review findings were deliberately **not** changed because they match the
frozen spec's explicit direction rather than being bugs:
- `scripts/regression-issue.ts` lets `readFileSync` throw uncaught when the report
  is missing (eval crashed before writing it) — the spec explicitly calls for this,
  relying on the workflow's file-existence guard to skip filing in that case.
- The per-case `⚠️` marker in the issue table re-derives the regression predicate
  inline rather than consuming `compareToBaseline`'s output — the spec explicitly
  directs mirroring that logic inline (there's no structured per-case output from
  `compareToBaseline`, only aggregate regression/note strings).
- The issue body's "Overall pass rate" line renders the raw float rather than a
  rounded percentage — the spec's literal template uses the raw value.
- `regression-issue.ts` recomputes the comparison from disk rather than reusing the
  one `scripts/eval.ts` already computed — these are two separate CI steps/process
  invocations, so there's no in-memory value to share; the spec calls this out as
  intentionally cheap to redo.

This branch was rebased onto `main` mid-flight to pick up two concurrently merged
PRs: one that re-added CI's `Lint` step (unrelated to this change — an earlier diff
against a stale `main` made it look like this PR removed it, but it never touched
`ci.yml`), and one that added a routing-accuracy metric to the eval types — this PR's
test fixtures were updated to match the new required fields.

Closes #91

body:
Claude driven development of a MOS6502 assembler.  I've manually reviewed each step, each phase and now the PR.  Suggesting changes for clarity, simplicity and readability along the way.

## Phased delivery (one phase at a time, checkpoint before proceeding — same cadence as the opcode-implementation phases)

1. **Line scanning** — `SourceLine`, `LineScanner`. Tests: `LineScannerTest`.
2. **Operand grammar** — `AddressingMode`, `Operand`, `OperandParser` (all 13 modes, mnemonic-agnostic). Tests: `OperandParserTest`.
3. **Mnemonic resolution + straight-line assembly** — `OpCodeTable`, `InstructionResolver`, first-cut `Assembler`/`AssembledProgram`/`AssemblyException` for programs with no label *references* (labels may be defined, just unused). Tests: `OpCodeTableTest`, `InstructionResolverTest`, `AssemblerTest` (straight-line).
4. **Two-pass label resolution** — `SymbolTable`; extend `Assembler` to full two-pass (branches, forward/backward labels, out-of-range offsets). Completes the assembler's public API. Tests: `SymbolTableTest`, `AssemblerTest` (including assembling the exact sample program and checking bytes/labels).
5. **Integration** — flesh out `MOS6502IntegrationTest.simpleProgram()` end-to-end per above.

author: sureshvl
body:
## Summary

Two things needed to run the app locally on Windows:

1. **Native launch scripts** (Windows PowerShell can't run `.sh`):
   - `scripts/dev-local.ps1` — detects `python`/`py`, generates the security secret, writes env files, installs deps, opens backend + frontend each in its own window.
   - `scripts/dev-local.sh` — resolves `python3`-or-`python` so it also works under Git Bash on Windows.

2. **Fix an event-loop-blocking bug in auth** (found while bringing the app up on Windows):
   - `get_current_user` (the auth dependency) and the org-scoping middleware called `_verify_token` **synchronously on the asyncio event loop**.
   - When no local JWT secret is configured, `_verify_token` makes a blocking network call to Supabase `/auth/v1/user`. Running that on the loop stalls the single worker, so concurrent requests — even `/health` — hang until they time out. Symptom: all dashboard requests pending ~30s then `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` (very visible on Windows).
   - Fix: wrap both calls in `asyncio.to_thread` so the blocking validation runs off the event loop.

## Testing

- 34 auth/security tests pass (`test_security_hardening.py`, `test_auth_and_infra.py`).
- Backend boots clean; verified end-to-end login against real Supabase.

## Notes

`SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is left blank by default (plaintext fallback with a logged warning); set it for at-rest encryption in production.

Refs #46. Completa #47, #48, #49, #50, #51 y #52. #53 permanece abierto por smoke productivo pendiente.

`dashboard_fg` implementa de forma independiente:

`cantidad_valorizada = produccion × coeficiente`

`valor_unitario = tarifa_base × cotizacion`

author: vanchha16
body:
An account that registered but never finished OTP verification (expired code, closed tab mid-signup, etc.) was completely stuck: forgot-password silently skipped sending anything for unverified users, and register() separately blocks re-signup for any existing email regardless of verification status. From the user's perspective this looked exactly like "the reset code never arrives" with no error to explain why.

Reset codes now send regardless of is_verified — the anti-enumeration protection already comes from the generic response message, not this gate — and successfully completing a reset also marks the account verified, since proving inbox ownership via the emailed code satisfies verification on its own.

Verified end-to-end: an account with is_verified=False now receives a code, resets its password, and comes out verified and able to log in.

## Summary
Ajoute une page publique **`/box`** qui liste les box utilisant AthleX, pour que les athlètes trouvent une salle depuis le site web. Chaque carte renvoie vers la page publique existante `/box/[slug]`. Recherche texte (nom / ville / sport / tagline, insensible aux accents) + filtre par ville. Pas de carte pour l'instant (demandé plus tard).

### Filtre d'éligibilité (côté serveur)
Une box est listée uniquement si elle est **légitime/active** :
```
is_active = true
AND is_listed = true            // colonne existante, défaut true
AND slug IS NOT NULL
AND ( stripe_onboarding_complete    // peut encaisser
      OR box_subscriptions.status ∈ {active, trialing, past_due} )  // client AthleX vivant
```
La requête tourne en **service role** dans le server component (`app/box/page.tsx`), et n'expose que des champs publics (`name, slug, tagline, logo_url, cover_url, city, sport_type, member_count`). Tri par `member_count` desc. `revalidate = 300` (ISR, SEO-friendly).

- `app/box/BoxDirectory.tsx` (client) : champ recherche + `<select>` ville dérivé des données, grille de cartes (cover, logo, ville, nb membres, sport).

body:
## Summary
- Adds the auction UI: `BiddingControls` (bid-amount entry/raise/pass for the human) and `TrumpSelector` (trump call for whoever wins the bid), driven by `bidding.ts`'s valuation math (`bestBaseBid`) and a UI-layer state machine (`auctionReducer.ts`) that mirrors `pinochle_engine.py`'s `Round._bidding_loop` (turn rotation left-of-dealer, 3-pass auction end, dealer forced to `FORCED_BID` if nobody ever bids).
- Adds the 3-card pass UI: `PassSelector` lets the human pick exactly `PASS_COUNT` cards from their hand; the two-leg partner-to-bidder / bidder-to-partner exchange (`passing.ts`'s real `choosePassCards` for AI seats) is driven by the same state machine.
- Adds `AuctionLog` — every bid, pass, forced contract, trump call, and card exchange (AI or human) appends a visible log entry, so AI decisions are never silent. Card-pass entries deliberately omit which cards moved (count only) since passed cards are private between sender/receiver.
- Issue #29's stateful `chooseBid`/`chooseTrump` AI decision wrapper hasn't landed, so AI bid/trump decisions use a simplified stand-in (`mock/aiDecisions.ts`, built directly on `bidding.ts`'s `bestBaseBid`/`maxBid`/`OPENER_THRESHOLD`) — isolated to that one file so it's a small swap once #29 ships.
- All new components take plain data props (`auctionTypes.ts`), mirroring the `tableTypes.ts`/`scoreTypes.ts` approach from #33/#36, so a later live-Round issue can drive this UI without changing the components.
- Mounts into the existing `Table` scaffold (#33): widens `TableState`'s `trumpSuit`/`bidWinner` to nullable (there's no contract yet during bidding) and gives `Table` optional `overlay`/`logPanel` slots so the auction controls and log render over/alongside the seats instead of replacing them. `App.tsx` now runs `AuctionFlow` against mock dealt hands instead of the static demo table.

Trick-play (#35) picks up once the auction completes — `AuctionFlow`'s `onComplete` hands back the post-pass hands, trump, bid winner, and bid amount for that issue to consume.

Closes #34

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 123/123 passing (17 files), including a full component-level walkthrough of bidding → trump call → pass in `AuctionFlow.test.tsx` with deliberately weak AI hands to keep the auction outcome deterministic

author: marc-aurele-besner
body:
## Problem

The Foundry test suite's real assertions lived behind a single-author npm package:

- `contracts/test/MyMultiSig*.t.sol` (and `MyMultiSigFactory*.t.sol`, `*ChugSplash*.t.sol`) were 11-line shells — the bodies that held every real assertion were imported from `foundry-test-utility` via `remappings.txt:4` and `package.json:77`.
- The package (`@0.1.1`, MIT, single maintainer) is a vendored copy of forge-std + a small EIP-712 helper module. No other consumer, no security audit, pinned to one author.
- The whole suite depends on that transitive supply chain to even compile.

## Fix

Drop `foundry-test-utility` entirely. Replace with `forge-std` (Apache-2.0/MIT, the official Foundry test library) plus a tiny in-tree `Signatures` mixin.

| # | Commit | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `chore(deps): drop foundry-test-utility, vendor forge-std` | remove the npm dep, drop the remapping line, add `lib/forge-std` as a git submodule pinned in `foundry.lock`, switch `foundry.toml` libs from `[]` → `["lib"]` |
| 2 | `test(foundry): replace foundry-test-utility imports with first-party code` | rewrite `shared/errors.t.sol` (`DSTest`→`forge-std/Test`), `helper.t.sol` (`stdCheats.skip`→`vm.warp`), `functions.t.sol` (drop unused `CheatCodes`+`console`), `tests.t.sol`; add `contracts/test/shared/signatures.t.sol` containing only the 3-arg `signature_signHashed(pk, domainSeparator, hash)` form the suite actually used; strip the unused `console.sol` import from every `*ChugSplash*.t.sol`, `*Factory*.t.sol`, `MockERC*.t.sol`, and `MockERC721.sol` shell |
| 3 | `ci(foundry): check out submodules for forge-std` | `actions/checkout@v3` skips submodules by default; pass `submodules: recursive` so CI sees forge-std |
| 4 | `fix(ci): teach Hardhat to read remappings.txt + symlink forge-std` | Hardhat's stock `TASK_COMPILE_GET_REMAPPINGS` returns `{}` and ignores `remappings.txt` — override it in `hardhat.config.ts` to parse the file, normalising the `to` side to end in `/` (Hardhat's plain-prefix replace would otherwise collapse `@openzeppelin/contracts/` + `security/Foo.sol` → `node_modules/@openzeppelin/contractssecurity/Foo.sol`). Add a `postinstall` hook that symlinks `node_modules/forge-std` → `../lib/forge-std` when the submodule is present. |

After: `grep -RIn foundry-test-utility contracts/ hardhat.config.ts package.json yarn.lock remappings.txt` returns zero hits (the only remaining mentions are three NatSpec comments documenting the migration).

## Verification

```
yarn install                     # postinstall creates node_modules/forge-std symlink
forge test                       # 9 suites, 75 tests passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped
npx hardhat compile              # 99 artifacts, no errors
npm run build                    # 6 ABIs + 4 TypeScript types written
```

author: theonetheycallneo
body:
## What

Three UX improvements to how the Slack bridge replies, driven by dogfooding it as a per-repo agent channel. All in `server.ts`.

### 1. Channel/thread-aware replies
The system prompt only said *"use thread_ts to reply in a thread"*, so top-level channel messages inconsistently got **threaded** replies. New explicit rule:
- incoming message **has** `thread_ts` → reply **in that thread**
- incoming message is **top-level** → reply **in the channel** (omit `thread_ts`)

Mirrors where the human wrote.

### 2. Streaming on by default
Instruct the model to always pass `stream:true` so replies stream in progressively via `chat.update` instead of landing in one shot.

### 3. Native "working" status (Hermes-style)
A rotating gerund — `Galloping…`, `Shimmying…`, `Pondering…` (+12 more) — shown under the bot via Slack's **`assistant.threads.setStatus`** the moment a message is received, so the channel shows the agent is on it before the reply lands. Cleared when the reply posts, or by a TTL timer if the message is left unanswered.

- Degrades to a **silent no-op** if the app lacks the Assistant feature / `assistant:write` scope (the existing `ackReaction` still fires).
- Keyed by `(channel, thread)` so it matches the reply destination under the threading rule above.

## Testing / gates
- ✅ `tsc --noEmit` clean
- ✅ `biome check` clean
- ⚠️ The new status helpers (`setAssistantStatus`, `clearWorkingStatus`, receipt hook) don't yet have unit tests, so the **95% coverage gate** would need tests added before merge. Happy to add them if you want to take this upstream.

## Notes
- `assistant.threads.setStatus` is built for Slack's AI-assistant surface; whether the gerund renders inside a *regular channel thread* vs. only the assistant pane is still being verified in the field.

body:
## Summary

- Set `determinate: false` on the `DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@main` step in `.github/workflows/flake-update.yml`.
- Also set the same input on the identical installer invocations in `.github/workflows/check.yml` for consistency.

## Verification / docs

- Upstream `action.yml` defines the input literally as `determinate` and describes it as whether to install Determinate Nix, with default `true`: https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action/blob/a7ad9c4f0c65208097f4d34f3cfa1913b80cce5c/action.yml#L10-L13
- The README configuration table lists `determinate` as a `Boolean` defaulting to `true`: https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action/blob/a7ad9c4f0c65208097f4d34f3cfa1913b80cce5c/README.md#L98-L104
- The README upstream-Nix section says Determinate Nix is the default and shows `determinate: false` as the documented way to install upstream Nix: https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action/blob/a7ad9c4f0c65208097f4d34f3cfa1913b80cce5c/README.md#L140-L149
- The action bundle gates the hash-mismatch annotation path on `this.determinate`; with `determinate: false`, `annotateMismatches()` returns before calling `determinate-nixd`: https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action/blob/a7ad9c4f0c65208097f4d34f3cfa1913b80cce5c/dist/index.js#L115414-L115436
- The README installation differences show the installer enables `nix-command` and `flakes`, and these workflows still pass `accept-flake-config = true` through `extra-conf`, so the `nix flake update` / `nix build` calls still have the required Nix features: https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action/blob/a7ad9c4f0c65208097f4d34f3cfa1913b80cce5c/README.md#L84-L96

## check.yml consistency decision

I updated `check.yml` too. It had the same unset `determinate` input in four installer steps, including the same self-hosted NixOS runner class, so leaving it implicit would preserve the same noisy Determinate-mode behavior in CI while fixing only the scheduled flake-update workflow. Making all installer steps explicit keeps the workflows aligned and avoids depending on the action current default.

## Scope

This only removes a non-fatal warning and unused Determinate Nix/hash-mismatch annotation path. The reported dry-run already succeeded.

## Validation

- `nix run nixpkgs#actionlint -- .github/workflows/flake-update.yml .github/workflows/check.yml` returned only the known custom self-hosted runner label findings for `nixos`.
- `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; ARGV.each { |f| YAML.load_file(f); puts "#{f}: ok" }' .github/workflows/flake-update.yml .github/workflows/check.yml`
- `git diff --check`

I did not run the real self-hosted workflow.

author: rusackas
body:
### SUMMARY

This is a test-only TDD pull request validating [#27510](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/27510) ("Using Filter per value of Column of type BIGINT breaks UI when the value is large"). It adds no product code — only a regression test. The original bug: a native (dashboard) filter on a `BIGINT` column with a large value (16+ digits, exceeding `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`) broke the filter UI with React error #31 ("Objects are not valid as a React child, found: object with keys {s, e, c}") — the `{s, e, c}` object being a `json-bigint` `BigNumber` that leaked into rendering, plus silent precision loss when such values were coerced through a JS number. The test exercises `getDataRecordFormatter` in `superset-frontend/src/filters/utils.ts` — the label formatter that produces the rendered Select-filter option — and asserts that a large `bigint` column value is formatted to its exact decimal string (full precision, a plain string React can render), while confirming that the pre-fix path of routing the same value through a JS number corrupts the trailing digits.

### How to interpret CI

- **Green (test passes):** the bug is already fixed on current `master` (large BIGINT values are decoded to native `bigint` by the `json-bigint` parse and rendered as exact strings). Merging this PR adds a permanent regression guard and closes the issue.
- **Red (test fails):** the bug is live. The suspected fix location is the filter value handling path: `superset-frontend/src/filters/utils.ts` (`getDataRecordFormatter`) and the `json-bigint` decode in `superset-frontend/packages/superset-ui-core/src/connection/callApi/parseResponse.ts`, which must yield a native `bigint`/string rather than a `BigNumber` object so large BIGINT values keep full precision in the native filter Select.

### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS

```bash
cd superset-frontend
npx jest src/filters/utils.test.ts -t "Regression for #27510"
```

### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

- [ ] Has associated issue: Closes #27510

author: gumbees
body:
A Calendar pane that renders the events already emerging from your journal on a month grid. Fold-safe by design.

## What
- **Month grid**: prev/next nav, today highlighted, events placed in their day cell by a lenient `at` parser (frozen ISO / `YYYY-MM-DD` / datetime, space or `T`), ≤3 per cell + "+N more".
- **Undated list**: events with a vague or missing `at` (common for journal-emerged events) render below the grid so nothing hides.
- **Create/edit/delete** through the same `EntityDetail` view contacts and tasks use — date+time inputs compose a clean ISO into `at`; an unparseable stored value surfaces as a raw "When (as written)" field so nothing is lost; two-step delete. The source journal entry appears under "Related in your journal" via `links_for_entity`.
- `events_update` (entity.update over existing columns) + `events_delete` (tombstone + link.remove). Pure, chrono-free calendar math (Sakamoto weekday, leap/month-length, 42-cell grid), all unit-tested.

## Fold-safe (the important part)
No `core/src/fold/` change, FOLD_VERSION still 3, DROP_DERIVED/DDL untouched — only existing event columns and existing record kinds. A fold bump would drop the embeddings table and force a full re-embed of your 411-entry store; this avoids it. **Recurrence, reminders, timezone, and CalDAV sync are deferred to a future batched fold migration** so your store re-embeds once, not once per feature.

## Tests
**220 no-DB (+11: `at` parser incl. leap/garbage rejection, weekday+grid math, `events_update` round-trip, `events_delete` tombstone survives replay) + 10 importer, 0 failed.** fmt/clippy clean. fold/FOLD_VERSION/DROP_DERIVED zero diff.

body:
## Summary

`python manage.py check` (and therefore `runserver`, `test`, and any CI
step that boots Django) currently fails on a clean `main` checkout. This
PR fixes three separate, pre-existing errors encountered one after another
while trying to get the backend to actually start - each one was masking
the next.

## Fixes #1436 

### 1. `backend/apps/feature_flags/admin.py`
Imported `Experiment` and `FeatureFlagAuditLog` from `models.py`, but
neither class exists there (only `FeatureFlag` does) - introduced in PR
#920. Rewrote the file to a minimal admin matching the real `FeatureFlag`
model (`name`, `enabled`, `description`). A/B testing and audit logging
should be reintroduced in a future PR once those models are actually
designed and migrated.

### 2. `backend/config/urls.py`
The `if settings.DEBUG:` block at the end of the file was syntactically
broken - a series of `path(...)` expressions with no `urlpatterns +=`
assignment, closed by a stray `]` with no matching `[`. Fixed the syntax,
removed duplicate `api/schema/`/`api/docs/`/`graphql/` registrations that
already exist unconditionally earlier in the file, and wired up the
previously-imported-but-unused `feature_flags_debug_view` to an actual
route.

### 3. `backend/apps/progress/views.py`
Inside `except LessonProgress.DoesNotExist:`, a `XPEvent.objects.create(...)`
call and `created = True` were indented one level too deep - as if still
inside the already-closed `LessonProgress.objects.create(...)` call above
them - causing an `IndentationError`. Dedented to align with the rest of
the `except` block.

## Verification
- `python manage.py check` now passes cleanly (previously failed on all
  three of these in sequence).

## Files changed
- `backend/apps/feature_flags/admin.py`
- `backend/config/urls.py`
- `backend/apps/progress/views.py`

author: lllyys
body:
Gate-1/Gate-2 planning for feature #133 (Android in-reader find-in-book). GH #1925. **Docs-only** — plan + tracker note, no code, no version bump.

Independent Gate-2 audit ran **3 rounds** (rule 47 max), catching real model-assumption failures before any implementation:
- **r1**: 2 Critical / 5 High / 7 Medium / 2 Low.
- **r2**: 2 Critical / 2 Medium (the r1 fixes surfaced deeper issues).
- **r3**: 1 Medium (closed).

**Load-bearing redesigns the audit forced:**
1. **EPUB search does NOT reuse the FTS index for position.** The text-quote-only reconstruction was *impossible* — `ReadiumLocatorReconstructor.toReadium` requires a nonblank `href`, there's no publication-wide text-quote search, and `sectionIndex` is a content-iterator counter (not `readingOrder` index; href never persisted). → EPUB pivots to **Readium 3.3.0's own `SearchService`** (verified present incl. the bundled `StringSearchService`/`IcuAlgorithm` engine in `readium-shared-3.3.0-runtime.jar`); the FTS index serves TXT/MD only.
2. **Occurrence extraction can't reuse `BuiltQuery.tokens`** (flat highlight list — wrong for CJK phrases / prefix / AND) → new additive `SearchQueryBuilder.structuredQuery` + a dedicated `RawOffsetMatcher` (raw UTF-16 offsets honoring phrase/prefix/AND + CJK + surrogate pairs + NFKC) with a **resumable intra-chunk pagination cursor** so append-on-scroll is complete (no silent hit drop).
3. **DB stays v7** (Readium search obviates the href column — no migration).
4. **No needs-design** (`p.N` omitted matching shipped iOS; indexing→NoResults hint; PDF/AZW3 hidden; jump-failure→sheet-stays-open; truncation surface removed).

12 WIs, each with enumerated files; WI-10/WI-11 serialize the shared `AppContainer` edit. Full plan + revision history in `dev-docs/plans/20260710-feature-133-android-find-in-book.md`. Row → READY TO BUILD (dispatch follows).

author: pinterb
body:
Implements the GPG key family for commit-signature verification (maintainer decision 2026-07-11, D3 companion): the GO-031 key-family seam gains an OpenPGP arm so this repository's own GPG-signed history verifies, while the SSH-only conformance contract stays intact.

## What changed

- **`internal/pgp`** (new; added to the ci.yml ADR-018 `time.Now` guard): parses an armored OpenPGP public keyring and verifies detached signatures over commit payload bytes at an injected instant, threaded through `packet.Config.Time` so creation/expiry/revocation are evaluated at that instant (ADR-018). Uses `github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto/openpgp` (go-git's maintained fork, promoted from transitive to direct); the frozen `golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp` is not used.
- **`internal/vcs`**: `VerifyCommitSignature` now takes a `TrustedSigners` struct (SSH registry + optional PGP keyring). PGP armor dispatches to `internal/pgp` when a keyring is injected; failures map onto the existing sentinels (`ErrUnknownSigner` / `ErrRevokedSigner` / `ErrInvalidSignature`) so `errors.Is` identity is uniform across families.
- **`internal/verify` + CLI**: new `semver-trust verify --gpg-keyring <armored-keyring>` flag. GPG-verified principals default to `IdentityHuman` unless listed in policy `bot_accounts`, same §9 rule as SSH.

## Conformance contract preserved (fail-closed rider, fixture plan §2.1)

GPG verification activates **only** when a keyring is injected. With none — the conformance suite injects none — a PGP signature still aborts with `ErrUnsupportedKeyFamily`, message now noting `no OpenPGP keyring injected`. The vendored `crypto/ssh/gpg-family-fails-closed` vector and **all 125 conformance tests pass unchanged**.

## Judgment calls

1. **API shape**: a `TrustedSigners` struct rather than an extra parameter — the next key family extends the struct, not every call site. Both existing callers updated.
2. **Sentinels**: `internal/pgp` defines local errors mirroring the unknown/revoked/invalid split; the vcs layer maps them onto the existing sentinels, keeping `internal/pgp` free of the `sshsig` import.
3. **Multi-block keyrings**: go-crypto's `ReadArmoredKeyRing` reads only the *first* armor block; a keyring assembled by concatenating per-key `gpg --export --armor` outputs would silently drop every later key — a silent drop that turns valid signers into aborts. `ParseKeyring` splits blocks textually (armor.Decode over-reads a shared reader) and loads them all.
4. **Key created after the instant**: rejected explicitly as revoked-class — go-crypto checks expiry/revocation at config time but not existence.
5. **Flag-only keyring**: the §9 policy vocabulary has no `identity.human` field for a GPG keyring; adding one is a spec-repo question, so `internal/policy` is untouched.
6. **Pure-GPG runs need no SSH registry**: with a keyring injected and no allowed-signers source, the SSH registry is empty rather than an abort; SSH-signed commits then still abort as unknown signers (no grant added).
7. **Per-run test keys**: OpenPGP entities are generated in-test with a fixed config time (`internal/pgp/pgptest`, hermetic — no network, no gpg binary; signed commits are assembled as raw objects with the armored sig as the `gpgsig` header, the technique of the vendored `build-fixture-repos.sh`). The cross-implementation vendored-GPG-fixture question is explicitly deferred to a future spec-repo round (fixture plan §2.1, §7 OQ3).

## Dogfood: verifying this repository's own history

```sh
gpg --export --armor 6B703B3EA9F83907 >  /tmp/keyring.asc
gpg --export --armor C5489F821F1180FB >> /tmp/keyring.asc
semver-trust verify --repo . --from 793a444 --to e4bbd2d \
  --gpg-keyring /tmp/keyring.asc --verify-time 2026-07-12T00:00:00Z
```

Observed (the GPG signature of a real history commit **verifies** — the run gets past §10 step 3 — and then aborts honestly at the §5.4 meta-path check, because that agent-authored commit touches `.semver-trust/**` at a level below the required T2):

```text
Error: §10 step 1 (§5.4 meta-path level): commits touch a meta-path below required level T2 (§5.4 fails outright, not demote): [e4bbd2dd868805fc54f642408bd346509ecf32a2]
```

That abort is expected and honest: signature verification of GPG commits now works; the meta-path policy does its own job.

Full-history run (`--from '' --to HEAD`) currently aborts fail-closed at the first commit signed by key `B5690EEEBB952194`, whose public key is not exportable on this machine (the keys.openpgp.org copy has its identity stripped, which go-crypto rejects):

```text
Error: §10 step 3 (verify signature): verify 4e67d10ad4d811975290bc8b982ab853e4a771bb: OpenPGP: signing key is not an allowed signer
```

With that key exported into the keyring by its owner, the same invocation verifies the whole history's signatures. Two more honest aborts observed while dogfooding, both correct: verifying at an instant *before* a signing key's creation aborts as revoked-class ("key expired" from go-crypto's instant check), and a range whose TO tree carries no policy aborts at step 1.

## Gates

- `task test`: 422 tests pass
- `task conformance`: **125/125 unchanged** (incl. `crypto/ssh/gpg-family-fails-closed`)
- `task lint`: `lint:go` 0 issues; `lint:markdown` pass; `lint:yaml` fails in linked worktrees with `stat .git/**: not a directory` (pre-existing, fixed by the "lint tracked YAML only" commit not yet on upstream/main), so the remaining linters were run individually: `lint:python`, `lint:bash`, `lint:gha` all pass, and the edited `ci.yml` lints clean with `yamlfmt -lint`
- `task vuln`: 0 vulnerabilities affecting this code
- `grep -rn "time.Now(" internal/` → empty (internal/pgp included; the instant rides `packet.Config.Time`)

Closes #42

## Summary

- add a driver-neutral async repository for OIDC login states
- remove DB, schema, concrete adapter, and Drizzle imports from the OIDC service

Issue #363 requires production services to depend only on driver-neutral async persistence contracts. OIDC still stored, swept, queried, and deleted state directly through the SQLite schema. OIDC login starts and callbacks now work through a remote-capable interface, while provider isolation, expiry behavior, redirect state, and PKCE data remain unchanged. A valid state can be consumed exactly once.

author: charliek
body:
Converts the Tauri client's Preferences from a modal into a **dedicated native window** matching the mac app — fixed-size (520×640), titled "shed desktop — Preferences", singleton (reopening focuses it, closing hides it for fast reopen) — and closes the config parity gaps the modal never had.

## What changed

**1. Plumbing (`f6ede26`)** — the shared coordinator gains a real provider-mode surface (`set_provider_mode` validating `aws-credentials`/`docker-credentials`, `provider_modes()` read-back) and `remove_shed_rule`, all in the established actor pattern; provider modes + per-shed `extra_rules` are now persisted in prefs.json (`#[serde(default)]`, corrupt-tolerant, shed-scope-filtered hydration) and hydrated into the coordinator at startup — including `persist: true` approval decisions, which previously created rules that never survived a restart. New managed appearance state backs cross-window theme sync (`ui.set_appearance` updates it in Rust before emitting, killing a listener-attach race).

**2. The window (`7630081`)** — a third webview entry (`preferences.html`, own React root, per-label capability file) following the popover pattern but cross-platform and decorated. All open paths repointed (tray menu, popover footer, dashboard gear, `ui.show_preferences` + new `ui.open_preferences` alias); the modal, the `show-preferences` event, and the `"prefs"` modal state are gone. Full mac-parity grouped form: General, Terminal (dynamic per-preset descriptions), Approvals empty-state, SSH approvals (conditional Duration/Method), **AWS + Docker credentials** (Allow|Deny segmented, live), **Per-shed overrides** (with remove) — visibility driven by the host-agent's gated namespaces. Open/close are FIFO-consistent (whole check-create-or-focus marshalled to the main thread) and all prefs fetches are generation-guarded.

**3. Docs/skills (`2cf66c0`)** — the new drive surface documented; the Linux screenshot recipe fixed (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`, HOST_OUT expansion gotcha); new gremlins (WebKitGTK dark-mode raw `<select>` illegibility, `policy.set` vs `extra_rules`, no per-window capture).

## Drivability (north star)

The window reports under its own label: `prefs.dump → {visible, title, prefs: {sections, values, mode}}` (Rust-side visibility merged in), `prefs.close`, `prefs.set_provider`/`prefs.provider_modes`, `prefs.remove_shed_rule`, plus a `prefs-changed` nudge so IPC-driven mutations refresh the window. `ui.modal` now reports only `create|launch|null`.

## Verification

- shed-app: 75 tests (+4 new: provider set/reject/deny-unset, single-rule removal), workspace clippy clean, rc leg green
- `make e2e-tauri`: 75 passed / 31 skipped (replaced modal test + 4 new window tests: open/values/close/reopen-focus, theme sync, gated sections via fake host-agent re-handshake, shed-rule add/remove)
- `make tauri-build-linux` (WebKitGTK render gate): 77 passed / 29 skipped

- Plan hardened by the Codex/Kimi/CodeRabbit panel; per-commit /simplify + review (Cursor as correctness reviewer — the Codex CLI needs an upgrade for its new default model); all findings fixed (window-create/close FIFO race, reloadAll generation guard, shed-scope hydration filter, removal semantics)

## Summary

`TestRunnerClient.findTestFile` (`clients/test-runner-client.ts`) mapped an edited source file to its test file via same-directory, `dir/__tests__/`, and flat top-level `tests/<basename>`/`__tests__/<basename>` candidates, plus an import-scan fallback. It did not check the **mirrored subdirectory** layout — `tests/<same-relative-subdir>/<basename><testExt>` — which is exactly this repo's own layout (`clients/knip-client.ts` → `tests/clients/knip-client.test.ts`). As a result, pi-lens's own `turn_end` test-runner integration (`runtime-turn.ts:645`, on by default) could only resolve its own tests via the slower/brittle import-scan fallback.

## What changed

- `clients/test-runner-client.ts`:
  - Added `relativeSourceDir(sourceFilePath, cwd)` — computes the source file's directory relative to `cwd`, or `null` when the file is at the project root or falls outside `cwd`.
  - `findTestFile`'s exact-match (TS/JS) search now also tries `tests/<relDir>/<basename><testExt>` and `__tests__/<relDir>/<basename><testExt>`, attempted alongside the existing candidates and before the flat top-level checks and the import-scan fallback.
  - The Python glob search (`test_*.py` / `*_test.py`) now also searches the mirrored `tests/<relDir>` / `test/<relDir>` directory, in addition to the existing single search directory.
  - Purely additive — same-dir, `__tests__/`, flat-`tests/`, and import-scan behavior are unchanged and unreordered relative to each other.
- `tests/clients/test-runner-client.test.ts`: added a `findTestFile — mirrored test-tree layout (#547)` describe block covering: TS mirrored under `tests/<subdir>/`, TS mirrored under `__tests__/<subdir>/`, Python mirrored under `tests/<subdir>/`, colocated-test regression guard, flat-`tests/`-dir regression guard, and same-dir-wins-over-mirrored precedence.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `[Unreleased] / Fixed` entry.

## Dogfood check

Built `dist/` and ran `TestRunnerClient.findTestFile("clients/knip-client.ts", <repoRoot>)` against this repo's real tree. Before the fix this only resolved via the import-scan fallback; after the fix it resolves directly via the new mirrored-dir candidate:

```
[test-runner] Detected runner via config: vitest
[test-runner] Found test file: .../tests/clients/knip-client.test.ts
{ "testFile": ".../tests/clients/knip-client.test.ts", "runner": "vitest" }
```

## Audit: other test-discovery hardening gaps (not fixed — noted for triage)

Per the issue's ask to look for related "breaks down at scale" gaps in this file's discovery path:

- `detectRunner`'s Priority-3 `node_modules` check (`clients/test-runner-client.ts:258-269`) only checks `path.join(cwd, "node_modules")`, not a monorepo workspace root. In an npm/yarn/pnpm workspace where `node_modules` is hoisted to the repo root, a package subdirectory's `cwd` won't have its own `node_modules/vitest`, so this check silently misses it (config-file and `package.json` deps checks earlier in the same function may still catch it, but not always). Real gap, but fixing it correctly needs a bounded upward-walk with a clear stopping rule (e.g. reuse this project's existing home-dir/marker-escape guards), which is more than a same-shape inline change — left for a separate issue.
- The Python glob search only searches the (now: same-dir-relative-mirrored-or-flat) directories, not recursively. A `tests/` tree with further nesting that doesn't exactly mirror the source tree (e.g. `tests/unit/test_foo.py` for `pkg/foo.py`) is still missed. Recursive/fuzzy matching by basename alone risks false positives (multiple files with the same basename across a large tree) — a real but non-trivial design question, left for separate triage rather than folded into this additive fix.
- `findTestFileByImport`'s import-scan fallback stays brittle for source files tested only via a shared harness/fixture (no direct import), e.g. this repo's own `tests/clients/dispatch/` suites. Inherent to a text-scan approach; not addressed here (out of scope for #547, which only asked for the mirrored-path fix).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npx vitest run tests/clients/test-runner-client.test.ts` — 13/13 passed
- [x] Full `npm test` — 3374 passed, 5 skipped, 4 failed. The 4 failures are in `tests/clients/tree-sitter-client-init.test.ts` and `tests/clients/dispatch/runners/tree-sitter-skip-test-files.test.ts` (tree-sitter WASM grammar loading), unrelated to this change, reproduced consistently on a re-run, and untouched by this diff.
- [x] Dogfood check against this repo's own tree (see above)

author: fernandox7
body:
## Summary

This PR adds achievements to World of ClaudeCraft: **the Book of Deeds**. Players earn 192 deeds worth 2365 Renown across progression, combat, dungeons, delves, zone Chronicles, collection, PvP, social, exploration, feats, and a shelf of hidden delights. Rewards are strictly cosmetic: 19 unique titles, 3 character-sheet badge borders, and the flex. The design contract (vocabulary, architecture, binding rules, the add-a-deed recipe) lives in `docs/design/deeds.md`; open calls and deferrals for review are collected in `docs/achievements/maintainer-notes.md`.

**The player loop.** Shift+Z (rebindable) opens the Book: a summary strip (Renown, completion, recent unlocks, a nearly-there list), a category rail, entry cards with painted crest art, progress bars, global rarity percentages (online), and search plus All/Earned/Unearned/Nearly done filters. It also opens from a side-menu dock button under the quest log (keycap "s-z"; modified bindings render compact keycaps via the new keyCapLabel helper while aria labels carry the full combo), from the character sheet, the mobile More tray, and three new Chronicler NPCs who anchor per-zone Chronicles in the world (Saul in Eastbrook Vale, Osric Fenn in Mirefen Marsh, Zenzie in Thornpeak Heights). A Titles pane equips any earned title, which then renders on the nameplate, target frame, chat lines on every channel, friends and guild rosters, the inspect card, the player card, and the leaderboards. A watchlist (cap 5, persisted per character) drives a HUD tracker under the quest tracker. Unlocks batch into a gold chat line per deed, one banner, one celebration sound, and a firework burst (skipped under reduced motion).

**One sim, three hosts.** The catalog is data-as-code (`src/sim/content/deeds.ts`) and the evaluator is a sim module behind the `SimContext` seam: it runs at the tick tail, draws zero rng, and only observes persisted state, so the same code decides deeds offline, online, and headless. Deeds asserting state a veteran already holds (levels, quests done, items held, craft skills) grant retroactively on first login, batched into a single catch-up summary with no banner spam; new lifetime counters start at zero for everyone. The legacy lifetime-XP milestone titles are unified into deeds at the same thresholds, and persisted picks carry over. Render and UI consume a new `IWorldDeeds` facet implemented by both the offline `Sim` and the online `ClientWorld` mirror; titles cross the wire as deed ids, never text, and are localized client-side.

**Server.** The sim alone grants deeds; the server observes. Unlocks mirror into a `character_deeds` index (idempotent inserts, the state blob stays the source of truth) that feeds an account-level Renown leaderboard (50 Renown entry floor, self rank and top percentile), an anonymous global rarity read, and character sheets. Marquee unlocks broadcast to online guildmates and followers with a per-account opt-out, ignore lists honored, and retro credits never broadcast. Banned and suspended accounts are now delisted from every player-derived public board (arena, lifetime XP, guild, daily rewards, and the new Renown board) and relist when a suspension expires.

**Steam, dark by default.** On the Steam desktop channel players can link (never log in with) a Steam account: the shell mints a session ticket, the server verifies it upstream and mirrors mapped unlocks to Steam achievements through the publisher Web API, reconciling on link. 72 curated marquee deeds map to permanent ACH_ names under a hard cap of 100. Everything is env-gated and off by default: with `STEAM_ENABLED` unset every route answers disabled, no client renders link UI, and website builds never load Steam code.

**Wiki.** A spoiler-safe `/wiki/deeds` page lists the 183 public deeds with crest art, Renown, and rewards; hidden deeds and all earn criteria are filtered out at generation time and never reach the bundle. The guide also picks up a presentation pass: grouped, token-ranked search with "/" and Ctrl/Cmd+K shortcuts, a sticky contents rail, self-hosted fonts replacing the Google Fonts CDN, druid form stills in the model gallery, and prose expansions across a dozen pages.

**Localization and art.** Every player-visible string is localized in every locale: window chrome, unlock and broadcast lines (composed client-side from ids), and each deed's name, description, and title via an entity table in the `talent_i18n` pattern. All 192 deeds ship painted 128px WebP crests with a deterministic ingest pipeline (`npm run assets:deeds`); procedural category crests remain as the fallback tier.

One new runtime dependency: `steamworks.js`, loaded lazily on the Steam desktop channel only. Web bundles never include or load it.

## Type of change

- [x] Feature: new functionality
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests

## How was this tested?

- Commands:
  - `npm test`: the full suite is green at the branch tip, 1011 test files and 12754 tests passed. The branch adds 26 test files (about 415 cases): evaluator triggers with negative cases, catalog integrity pins, persistence round trips, server SQL and board moderation delisting, the Steam mirror contract (never awaited on the game loop, in-flight dedupe, retry ladder), pure view cores, wiki spoiler safety, and an exact icon-to-file bijection. All 49 parity goldens are re-pinned because deed state rides the snapshot wire.
  - `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run build`, `npm run build:server`, and `npm run build:env` green; Biome clean on the changed files.
  - Guard suites: `tests/architecture.test.ts` (sim purity, determinism, the pure-core allowlist), `tests/world_api_parity.test.ts` (IWorld pinned at 212 members across 26 facets), `tests/localization_fixes.test.ts`, and `tests/i18n_completeness.test.ts` (registry pending is zero in every locale).
  - Local `npm run gate`: every step green except the sfx asset conformance check, which fails identically on an untouched checkout of the base branch (pre-existing audio debt, none of it touched here; noted in `docs/achievements/maintainer-notes.md`).
- Manual steps:
  - `scripts/deeds_screenshots.mjs` drives the real client through actual play: it earns deeds live (a Chronicle streak, discovery pickups, a bursar visit), equips a title, exercises every surface below at desktop 1600x900 and phone landscape 844x390, and pixel-verifies the unlock banner in the saved captures. The committed evidence set below is its output.
  - Spot checks in the dev client: the mobile More tray entry point, tracker collapse persistence, watch cap behavior, the broadcast opt-out toggle, and the offline sandbox showing an empty Renown board by design (accounts are server-side only).

## Screenshots / recordings

The evidence set is committed under `docs/achievements/screenshots/` (captured by the harness above); wiki shots under `docs/screenshots/`.

### The unlock moment

![Deed unlock moment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/52fd05f89142b3b2b29a0cfd2ffd53d4632108d9/docs/achievements/screenshots/01-unlock-moment-1600x900.png)

### The Book of Deeds window

![Book of Deeds window, phone landscape](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/52fd05f89142b3b2b29a0cfd2ffd53d4632108d9/docs/achievements/screenshots/02-book-window-844x390.png)

author: philippsyrov
body:
## Review fixes round 3 at `95f0976` (remaining P1 verified and fixed)

**Engine probe never cached.** The `mlx_lm.__version__` probe was memoized per interpreter path — the same stale-identity class just closed for model bytes. The cache is removed: every launch (sessions and crash-restarts) re-probes and refuses if the served version drifted from the one records carry. Pinned by a test with a stub interpreter whose version comes from a mutable file: resolves at 9.9.9, refuses both launch paths after the file changes to 10.0.0; the reverted mutation fails exactly that test. Also fixed the `git diff --check` blank-line-at-EOF nit in `model-identity.ts`.

Suite 299 (+1). `git diff --check` clean. Live smoke re-run: 6/6 completed (warm median 122.4 ms / cold 245.6 ms), no orphans.

## Review fixes round 2 at `fce0fe6` (both residual findings verified and fixed)

1. **Digest cache removed entirely**: Codex reproduced a same-size rewrite with a restored mtime that the stat-level fingerprint could not see. There is now no cache — identity verification is a full re-digest of the actual bytes at resolve and before every server launch (seconds per launch, always outside the timed windows). Pinned by a test doing exactly Codex's reproduction: same-length rewrite + `utimesSync` restore → launch refuses.
2. **Group sweep on every leader-death path**: `close()` no longer early-returns when the leader is already dead, and the startup early-exit path sweeps the group before throwing. Pinned by two tests: a worker forked before a startup crash is reaped, and `close()` after an out-of-band leader death still kills a SIGINT-immune worker.

3 reverted mutations each failed exactly their own tests. Suite 298 (+2). Live smoke re-run: 6/6 completed, warm median 125.4 ms / cold 244.4 ms, no orphaned processes.

## Review fixes at `8538af4` (Codex findings, all four verified and fixed)

1. **`--model` bypass closed**: exactly one two-token `--model server.modelDir` occurrence; duplicates and the `--model=` form are refused (argparse would let a later duplicate load bytes the digest never described). `openai-sse` now also refuses any engine other than `mlx-lm` — other declarations would be recorded unprobed.
2. **No stale digest**: the per-process digest cache is guarded by a stat-level fingerprint re-checked on every call, and identity is re-verified at every server launch (sessions and crash-restarts), not only at resolve.
3. **Timing ends at `[DONE]`**: generation/end-to-end timestamps are taken when `[DONE]` is parsed, never at socket closure — a server lingering with the connection open (previously: until the timeout abort) no longer inflates a completed run.
4. **Group shutdown**: the server is spawned as a process-group leader; SIGINT and the final unconditional SIGKILL sweep target the whole group, so a forked worker — even one ignoring SIGINT, as shell background jobs do — cannot outlive the session.

Each fix has a regression test whose reverted mutation fails exactly that test (5 mutations checked). Suite is now 296 (+7). Live smoke re-run after the fixes: 6/6 completed, warm median 123.2 ms / cold 242.1 ms, no orphaned processes.

## What changed

**The first real runtime adapter** for the D129 benchmark harness: Plume-managed `mlx_lm.server` behind `transport: "openai-sse"`.

- `scripts/benchmark/runtime-factory.ts` (new): transport-based session resolution. `stdio-jsonl` stays the scripted fake; `openai-sse` is the real adapter. The factory is also where **verified identity** lives — before any run: the model directory is re-digested (sha256 over every file, sorted order, symlinks refused) and must equal the declared `model.artifact.sha256`; the server command's `--model` argument must be exactly the digested directory (otherwise the digest would vouch for bytes the server never serves); the interpreter's actual `mlx_lm.__version__` is probed and must match a declared version or fill a null one. Any mismatch refuses the run. The factory also owns transport-specific crash-restart mechanics for the cancellation-restart suite.
- `scripts/benchmark/mlx-runtime.ts` (new): the session. Owns one `python -m mlx_lm server --model <dir> --host 127.0.0.1 --port <ephemeral>` process supervisor-style (spawn → poll `GET /health` under a startup budget → serve → SIGINT with 3 s grace → SIGKILL). **Client-observed, monotonic timing** (`timing.method: "clientObserved"`): TTFT = request write → first non-empty content delta (mlx-lm's keepalive comment frames before the first token correctly don't count); generation = first delta → terminal `[DONE]`; end-to-end = write → terminal; `promptEvaluationMs` stays null (not client-observable), so the prompt rate stays null too. Token counts come **only** from server-reported `usage` (`stream_options.include_usage`); SSE deltas are never counted as tokens. Deliberate cancellation aborts the stream; latency runs from abort to conclusive close.
- `scripts/benchmark/model-identity.ts` (new): model-dir digest (cached per process) + `mlx_lm.__version__` probe.
- **Warm/cold population semantics carry over unchanged**: a warm group is one primed live server; a cold attempt is a fresh server per invocation (`processRestart` — model load happens before the request, timings start at request send).
- `benchmarks/fixtures/short-chat/pong-001` (new): the real-model smoke fixture (calibrated live: Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct-4bit at temperature 0 answers exactly `pong`).
- `scripts/benchmark-mlx-smoke.sh` (new): one-command verified warm+cold matrix against a locally present checkpoint. Discovery mirrors the existing smoke scripts (`PLUME_MLX_PYTHON` → `~/.venvs/mlx-env` → `python3`; `PLUME_MODEL_DIR` → repo/worktree-primary → `~/plume-models`); quantization identity is read from the checkpoint's own `config.json`. Records stay in gitignored `benchmark-artifacts/`.
- `run-model.ts` / `run-suite.ts`: sessions now come from the factory; `timing.method` follows the transport; no behavior change for the fake runtime (all 80 pre-existing harness tests unchanged and green).
- Docs: `BENCHMARK_HARNESS.md` gains the adapter section (and re-scopes the non-goals to D129B/D129C); `DEVELOPMENT.md` smoke command; AGENTS.md status entry.

## One finding worth reading (caught live, now pinned by test)

The first smoke run classified all 6 attempts as malformed. Root cause: the request's `model` field was a placeholder string, and `mlx_lm.server` treats an unknown model id as something to **resolve — up to an outbound HuggingFace fetch** (observed live: a 401 from `huggingface.co/api/models/plume-benchmark`). Exactly the class of accidental network call this harness must never make. Fix: the request's model id is now the exact `--model` path (the same convention Plume's own Rust client uses), pinned by a unit test, and the factory's command/`--model`/`modelDir` consistency check closes the adjacent identity gap.

## Smoke matrix (mechanics validation only — NOT a benchmark result)

Single dev machine, tiny counts, `plume.dirty: true`, records not committed. Reproduced by `scripts/benchmark-mlx-smoke.sh`; all 6 records pass reader validation:

> HARNESS MECHANICS DATA — Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct-4bit, mlx-lm 0.31.3, short-chat pong fixture, 3 warm + 3 cold:
> warm endToEndMs median 114.7 (min 114.5, max 134.6); cold median 252.5 (min 235.2, max 483.5) — the warm/cold split behaves as designed (cold pays first-request costs); gen tok/s medians 64.2 warm / 63.4 cold. 0 crashes / malformed / timeouts.

## What did not change

- No product code (`src/`, `src-tauri/` untouched), no new dependencies (node's built-in fetch; vite-node as before), no model downloads, no README performance claims, no committed results.
- The fake-runtime path, the D128 contract text, and all D129 record/validator semantics — untouched; the D129 test suite runs unmodified.
- Reserved for follow-ups per the commission: resource probes (**D129B**), `plumeOrchestration` path + Rust patch-validato

author: matteobortolazzo
body:
Closes #110

## Problem

`agentwatch run refine <ticket>` sessions in the sandbox failed with `Unknown command: /agentflow:refine`, even after #104 provisioned `enabledPlugins` in `settings.json`.

Root cause: inside the home volume, `.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` recorded agentflow as installed at an `installPath` under `plugins/cache/…` — but the cache directory didn't exist (first-run auto-install interrupted after writing metadata, before populating the cache). Claude Code trusts the metadata, skips reinstall, finds no skill files, and nothing ever self-heals the volume.

## Fix

- **`lib/migrate-settings.sh`** — new `heal_plugin_installs <plugins-dir>`:
  - no `installed_plugins.json` → no-op
  - invalid JSON → delete the file (unlike `.claude.json` it holds no unrecoverable state; Claude Code regenerates it)
  - valid JSON → drop install records whose `installPath` is missing on disk, then drop plugin keys left with no records (`.plugins` maps each key to an *array* of records). jq can't stat, so paths are checked in bash and fed back via `--args`. Atomic write, idempotent.
- **`entrypoint.sh`** — call it after the settings migration, so a broken volume heals on next container start and Claude Code reinstalls from the marketplace.

## Tests

- New `tests/heal-plugins.test.sh` (same host-side harness pattern as `settings-merge.test.sh`): healthy file untouched, one broken plugin among two, one broken record inside a plugin's array, all paths missing → `.plugins == {}`, invalid JSON removed, missing file no-op, idempotency. **11/11 pass**; existing `settings-merge.test.sh` still 22/22.
- End-to-end: seeded a throwaway volume with broken metadata, ran the container with the new entrypoint — file healed to `{"version":2,"plugins":{}}`; second run is a no-op.

body:
## Summary

`Ensure-TaskFolder` in `internal/winclient/scheduled_task.go` called the **non-existent COM method** `CreateSubFolder` on `ITaskFolder`, so creating any `windows_scheduled_task` in a non-root folder failed with:

```
Folder creation failed: Method invocation failed because
[System.__ComObject] does not contain a method named 'CreateSubFolder'.
```

## Fix

- Replace the segment-by-segment loop with a single `ITaskFolder::CreateFolder(path, $null)` call. Per the [MS docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/taskschd/taskfolder-createfolder), `CreateFolder` builds the **entire nested folder tree** in one call when given a multi-level path.
- A `GetFolder` guard keeps creation **idempotent** when the folder already exists.
- Unblocks the shared scheduled_task data-source acceptance fixture (`TestAccWindowsScheduledTaskDataSource_Basic` / `_NotFound`).

## Tests

- Strengthened `TestSTCreate_RecursiveFolderCreation` with a script-level regression guard (asserts `CreateFolder(` present, `CreateSubFolder` absent) — the mock cannot exercise the COM call itself.
- `go build`, full `go test -short ./...`, `gofmt`, `go vet`, and `golangci-lint v2.5.0` all green locally.
- The COM-level behavior is validated in CI (`testacc-windows`) since it needs a live Windows/WinRM target.

author: sc2ben
body:
The deployed playground (pozeiden.sc2.in) fails to load with:

```
Failed to load pozeiden.wasm LinkError: import object field 'random_get' is not a Function
```

## Cause
The Zig std library imports **27** `wasi_snapshot_preview1` functions transitively (verified by parsing the wasm import section): `random_get`, `clock_time_get`, `clock_res_get`, `environ_*`, and a long tail of `fd_*`/`path_*` operations. Rendering is deterministic and touches none of them, but every imported field must resolve to a Function or `WebAssembly.instantiate` throws a `LinkError`. The hand-written shim only defined `fd_write` and a few `fd_*` stubs, so it died on the first unresolved import (`random_get`).

## Fix
Implement the few that can actually run — `random_get` (via `crypto.getRandomValues`), `clock_time_get`/`clock_res_get`, `environ_sizes_get`, `fd_write` — and wrap the namespace in a `Proxy` that returns a harmless `EBADF` stub for any other field. The module now links regardless of which imports a future std pulls in.

## Verification
Instantiated `zig-out/playground/pozeiden.wasm` under Node with this exact shim: links cleanly, `_initialize` runs, and rendering the screenshot's styled flowchart (including its `click … href`) produces valid SVG (`<svg …>…</svg>`, 3226 bytes) with the expected `rel="noopener noreferrer"` on the link.

Deploys to pozeiden.sc2.in via the existing deploy workflow. No wasm/code change — shim only.

Merge after #47 (this branch is based on the fixed `main`).

author: kishiguro
body:
## Summary

A static route whose gateway is covered by an SRv6-encapsulated route (a BGP-over-SRv6 service route, `encapsulation-type srv6`) previously resolved to a plain IPv6 nexthop — the covering route's H.Encap segment list was dropped, so traffic left unencapsulated and died in a core that routes only on locators. SR-MPLS label stacks were already inherited by recursive resolution; this brings SRv6 to parity.

- **nht**: `ResolvedNexthop` grows `segs` + `seg_encap`; recursion accumulates transport in a `Transport` struct. Segments prepend (deeper level = visited first, SRH order). A chain that would need both MPLS labels and SRv6 segments is refused — a kernel nexthop carries at most one encap.
- **resolve**: `entry_resolvable` accepts BGP routes carrying segs alongside the existing BGP-LU (MPLS) arm — an SRv6-encapsulated BGP route is legitimate transport for recursion, same as a labeled one.
- **static**: `apply_resolved` stamps `segs`/`encap_type` (H.Encap default); the resolved uni comes out shaped like an explicit-`segments` route, so the nexthop group dedupes with the covering route's group and the FIB install path is unchanged.
- **show**: the recursive two-liner renders inherited SRv6 transport as `via seg6 [...]` on the resolved line:

```
S  *> 3001:db8::1/128 [1/0] via 2001:db8:cafe::1 (recursive), 00:00:03
                            via seg6 [fcbb:bbbb:1:40::], i1
```

- **Book**: the recursive-static and SRv6-static chapters now document the inheritance and its boundaries (plain IGP-SRv6 routes carry nothing to inherit; mixed MPLS+SRv6 chains refuse).

## Test plan

- Unit: new resolver tests (inheritance, deeper-recursion survival, multi-level prepend order, mixed-transport refusal, v4-over-SRv6) + static resolver stamping test; `cargo test --workspace --exclude bdd` all green; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean.
- BDD: new `@static_srv6_nht` — three-router line (ingress/egress iBGP over SRv6, locator-only core) + host behind the egress; asserts recursive rendering, kernel `proto static … encap seg6`, end-to-end ping through the inherited encapsulation (the core cannot route the inner prefix, so the ping proves the tunnel), and fallback to the covering BGP route on delete.
- BDD regressions over shared resolver paths: `isis_srmpls`, `bgp_srv6_redistribute`, `rib_static_ipv6`, `bgp_interas_option_c` (BGP-LU arm), `static_vrf` — all pass.

author: an1va
body:
## What this is

A tech-debt paydown pass on the publish/side-effect layer, plus two custom guard lints so the debt can't silently recur. Grew out of a full-repo debt survey ([Derive doc](https://derive.to/artifacts/tech-debt-paydown-plan-july-2026-w8rjylx2)).

**Important:** the survey was taken against an older commit and much of the original plan was already merged on `main` (the MCP-publish webhook bug was already fixed; `isMember`, `makePrPreview`, `useApiMutation`, and the `lint:mutations`/`lint:surfaces` guards already exist). So this PR does **not** re-fix fixed things — it's the genuinely-remaining work: regression-prevention consolidation and a couple of real "load fails → renders blank" spots.

## Commits

1. **`refactor(api)` — one `afterPublish` helper for every publish path.** The "a new version went live" chain (`version.published` bus event, webhook, preview render, follower fan-out, thread re-anchor sweep) was consistent but hand-copied across HTTP publish, HTTP restore, MCP publish, and proposal-approve — the exact shape that drifted once before (an MCP publish silently skipping webhooks). Consolidated into `apps/api/src/lib/after-publish.ts` (`emitVersionBump` core + `afterPublish`). Side benefit: an MCP publish of a new *public* artifact now fans out to the acting human's followers, matching the HTTP route.

2. **`fix(web)` — surface failed loads instead of blanking.** The share dialog's member list and the insights popover swallowed load errors into a blank/skeleton view (looked like "no one has access" / stuck loading). Both now say the load failed.

3. **`fix(api)` — emit sweep events when a merged PR graduates.** `foldIntoCanonical` re-anchored the canonical doc's threads state-only (`sweepAnchors`), so a tab open on the canonical doc kept stale thread states after a PR merged. Now uses `publishSweepEvents` like every other version-bump path.

## Custom guard lints (the "protect from happening again" ask)

- **`lint:api`** now forbids constructing a raw `version.published` bus event or the follower fan-out anywhere but `after-publish.ts` — every publish path must share the one chain.
- **`lint:frontend`** now forbids `.catch(() => setX([]))` (a failed load is not an empty list). Debounced typeahead, where clearing on an aborted keystroke is intended, is annotated as the one legitimate exception.

Both were negative-tested (throwaway violation files confirmed they fire).

## Testing (local)

- `pnpm typecheck` (tsgo, incl. the Workers config): clean.
- `pnpm test`: **api 873, web 146, db 191, storage 16, mcp 19 — all pass**, including a new integration test that drives the real MCP JSON-RPC `publish` and asserts a `version.published` webhook delivery lands (parity with the HTTP route — the original bug class).
- Full lint gate (biome + all `lint:*` + knip + boundaries): green. The two `noUnusedImports` warnings in `workspace.ts` are pre-existing on `main`, non-blocking, and untouched here.

## Deliberately not in this PR

The store-dialect merge and `MetaStore` split (explicit non-goals). The share-dialog split (WP5) and CRUD-section generalization (WP4) are optional polish with real regression surface — deferred rather than rushed, since the mutation/error-surface guardrails they'd protect already exist on `main`.
