author: awdr74100
body:
## Why

Two of the most safety-critical grounding rules lived only in prose (skill / prompt): "use detail full for codegen" and "ground an oversized page section by section, never retry unscoped". A caller that skips the prose gets either a styling-free compact tree (and eyeballs values off the screenshot — the classic accuracy failure) or a giant blob that freezes the plugin and then errors out of the client's result cap, delivering nothing. This PR moves both rules into the protocol as guardrails. **Zero breaking changes**: defaults are untouched, and every guard only fires where today's behaviour is already a failure.

## What

Three nets, **public tool path only**:

1. **Plugin-side pre-serialization bail** — the mcp handler arms the dispatch with `budget: true`; at full detail the plugin first runs a cheap sync count walk and past `DESIGN_CONTEXT_BAIL_NODES` (1500) returns a **`sectionPlan`** (top-level subtrees + sizes) without starting the heavy per-node serialization at all. The threshold is deliberately high — real whole-page groundings of several hundred nodes succeed today and must keep working (the count also can't model `dedupeComponents`, so it over-estimates).
2. **MCP-side payload net** — a full result past `DESIGN_CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET` (100k chars ≈ Claude Code's default 25k-token MCP result cap, beyond which the result **errors out and delivers nothing today**) is replaced by the same plan built from the payload. If there's nothing to split into (<2 sections), the original payload is kept — a plan must never strand the caller.
3. **Below-full note** — compact/minimal results carry one deterministic line pointing codegen callers at `detail: 'full'`. The tool result is the only guidance surface every caller is guaranteed to read.

## The safety property: guard-flag direction

Internal consumers (`design_diff` snapshots, `component_map` / `icon_map` walks) read the payload **in-process** — it never enters an LLM context — so they must always get the raw tree. The public handler *injects* `budget: true` (a caller-supplied value is stripped by the input schema); internal dispatches never carry it. Forgetting the flag on a future internal consumer therefore degrades to **today's behaviour**, not a corrupted snapshot. `design_diff`'s dispatch is pinned by test (`not.toHaveProperty('budget')`).

## Details

- Section plans descend through single-child wrappers (a page-like frame) to section at the real content level, cap at 60 sections (`sectionsOmitted` reports the rest), and keep only the roots' identity in `nodes`.
- `sectionPlan` / `note` are optional additions to the shared result schema; old plugin builds simply never set them (compatible both directions).
- #47's URL normalization wraps **every** registered tool (generic or special-cased), so special-casing this handler loses nothing — verified.
- Tool description, `figma_to_code` prompt, and `grounding.md` teach the sectionPlan → ground-per-section next step (the prompt-tool-names guard from #57 covers the new text).

## Tests

+17: plugin bail (fires only with budget × full × over-threshold; honors depth caps; wide-tree cap; single-child descent), mcp net (arming + caller-budget stripping, note on default detail, small-full passthrough, plugin-plan passthrough, oversized replacement, nothing-to-split keep), design_diff raw-dispatch pin. 863 green; typecheck / lint / format:check / knip / build pass.

## After merge

Live round-trip planned (read-path change): big-page bail, compact note, and a large-node `design_diff` snapshot staying plan-free — requires main + `pnpm build` + MCP reconnect.

author: joel4893
body:
## What

Reshapes `@invokehq/cli` around the **builder path** — the eight commands an AI engineer types between `npm install -g @invokehq/cli` and a proven, replayable run:

```
login · init · deploy · run · inspect · receipts · graph · replay
```

Four of those (`inspect`, `receipts`, `graph`, `replay`) didn't exist yet. This adds them, re-implemented against **this repo's** helpers (`runtime_request` / `require_credentials` / `load_workspace`) — not copied from the monorepo, whose helper signatures differ.

## New commands (runtime executions API)

- **`inspect <id|last>`** — a run's full story: pipeline glyphs, cost, and its exact ledger slice.
- **`receipts [id] [--verify]`** — list or show signed receipts; `--verify` checks a receipt's hash + signature + chain, or the **whole ledger** when no id is given (exits 1 on tamper).
- **`graph`** — folds agents, their tasks, and recent runs into a terminal picture of the workspace (mirrors the web console's Agent Graph).
- **`replay <id|last>`** — re-run an execution with the same tool/params/intent; prints the diff verdict vs. the original.

## Deliberately kept

`run` stays **"run an agent or a workflow file"** — it already fits the `init → deploy → run → inspect` story, so it wasn't repurposed. `trace` and `watch` alias to `inspect` and `logs`.

## Deprecated tier

`tools`, `call`, `search`, `preflight`, `execute`, `workflow`, `approvals` are demoted: hidden from the layer help, still functional, each printing where the capability moved (governed tool calls → `invoke gateway call`; approvals → the web console). `--help` now leads with the builder path; the README front page (Quick Start, command table, feature bullet) is updated to match.

## Heads-up before release

`replay` calls `POST /executions/{id}/replay`, which is **new on the runtime backend and not deployed yet** — it will 404 until the backend ships. `inspect` / `receipts` / `graph` hit endpoints already live. Suggest cutting the release tag only after the backend deploy.

## Tests

`tests/node/invoke-cli.test.js`: updated the layer-help test and added coverage for the builder-path lead, deprecated commands hidden-but-functional, the four new subcommands parsing, `receipts --verify`, and the `trace`/`watch` aliases. **24/24 green** (`npm test`). The four commands were also exercised end-to-end against a mocked API locally.

## Summary

**Background job queue (opt-in via `REDIS_URL`, falls back to inline execution when unset):**
- `backend/src/queues/index.ts` - `getQueue()`/`QUEUE_NAMES`
- `backend/src/queues/notification.queue.ts` - `enqueueFeeReminders()`: queues a fee-reminder job when Redis is available, otherwise runs `sendFeeReminders()` inline (identical to pre-Phase-5 behavior)
- `backend/src/queues/report.queue.ts` - `enqueueDefaultersCsvExport()` (producer ready for a future queued CSV export endpoint; the existing synchronous export endpoint is untouched)
- `backend/src/workers/index.ts` - standalone worker process entrypoint (run separately from `server.ts` via `npm run dev:worker` / `npm run worker:start`)
- `backend/src/workers/notificationWorker.ts` / `reportWorker.ts` - process `"fee-reminders"` and `"defaulters-csv"` jobs
- `feeCollection.controller.ts`'s `sendFeeRemindersHandler` now returns `202 { queued: true, jobId }` when Redis is configured (or the original synchronous response otherwise) - branches with many defaulters no longer risk a request timeout sending Email+SMS to every parent

**Database indexes** (`db/prisma/schema.prisma`) targeting the actual hot query paths:
- `Payment`: `[branchId, paidAt]`, `[branchId, status]`, `[studentId]` (day book / collection trend / payment mode breakdown / student payment history)
- `FeeAssignment`: `[status]` (defaulters list, fee reminders)
- `StudentAttendance`: `[sectionId, date]`, `[studentId, date]` (attendance marking, attendance history)
- `StaffAttendance`: `[date]` (branch-wide date attendance lookup)

**Docs:** `DEPLOY.md` gets a new "Background worker process" section; `docker-compose.yml`'s Redis comment updated (it's now actually used by Phase 4 caching + this phase's queues, not just reserved for later).

## Tested
- `npx tsc --noEmit` / `npm test` (**56 suites / 485 tests**, up from 51/470 - 5 new suites, zero regressions) / `npm run build` - all clean
- `npx prisma validate` + `npx prisma generate` - schema with new indexes is valid, client regenerates/re-links cleanly
- **Real Bull + Redis end-to-end test**: started the Phase 3 docker-compose Redis service, ran a script against the actual *compiled* `dist/queues/index.js` (not just the bare Bull library) - confirmed a job added via `queue.add()` was picked up by a `queue.process()` handler and returned its result via `job.finished()`, the exact producer/consumer pattern this phase's code uses

## Known limitations
- No separate `email.queue.ts`/`emailWorker.ts` - emails already go through `notification.service.ts`'s multi-channel `notify()`, which the fee-reminders job already calls; a distinct email-only queue had no clear separate use case yet
- Query optimization (broad `select`/`include` audit, cursor pagination across ~20 files) was scoped out of this phase - judged lower-value than queues+indexes for the time available, and risky to do without a larger review (could silently drop fields a frontend page depends on)
- The report queue (`enqueueDefaultersCsvExport`) has a worker ready but isn't wired into a new HTTP endpoint yet - the existing synchronous CSV export is untouched/still works; a future "queue if large branch" endpoint can use this producer directly
- A production deployment needs the worker process (`npm run worker:start`) running as its own service alongside the API server - it will not run automatically just by setting `REDIS_URL` on the API server alone

author: hama210
body:
## Root cause
FLUX.2 generation was working, but prompt creation and retry returned immediately and moved the image task into `ctx.waitUntil`. The long image job was canceled before the After image reached R2, leaving D1 stuck on `generating`.

## Fix
- prompt creation now waits for the full Before/After result
- admin edit and Retry missing images now wait and return the real status and URLs
- the image health repair runs synchronously
- stale `generating` jobs older than two minutes are recovered and retried
- the current stuck prompt reuses its saved Before image and generates the missing After image
- exposes pipeline marker `flux2-klein-sync-v7`

This prevents future prompts from reporting success before their images are actually stored.

author: saurabhav88
body:
## What this is

Part of **#1317** (P1: silent all-zero recordings get no recovery or user feedback). This PR lands **only the proof bench** — a DEBUG-only test instrument that reproduces the production dead-mic fault on command, proves it fired, and measures whether the app handles it honestly. **No production behavior changes.** The reactive recovery + user feedback fix lands in a follow-up PR that uses this bench to prove it beats the release build offline, before any user sees it.

## Why the bench first

The founder's hard constraint on this heart-path fix is "prove it empirically before shipping — no guinea-pigging the 100 users." This bench is that proof instrument. Merging it separately keeps the fix PR a clean, production-only diff and puts the harness on `main` where the fix can validate against it.

## What it does

- **Injector core** (`DebugZeroFillController`, `#if DEBUG`): forces all-zero ("digital silence") audio from start, after a threshold, or for a bounded budget — the exact production dead-mic signature. Proven index-safe for negative inputs (`DebugZeroFillControllerTests.negativeBudgetIsSafe`).
- **Wired into all three capture sources** via the single fan-out point (`PreRollForwarder.route`), behind buffer-shape guards so an unsupported buffer never claims a fault hit.
- **DEBUG XPC arm/status channel** so the harness can arm a fault and read back what actually happened (armed / hit / zeroed-sample-count / source-incarnation / **capture source type**).
- **Fail-closed Python harness** (`Tests/RuntimeUAT/faultInjection.py`, `run_gauntlet.py`): scenarios Z1 (dead from start), Z2 (real speech then dead), Z3 (brief dead then recover), negative controls, build-manifest stamping, running-identity verification, and a JSON scorecard whose exit contract fails only on invalid evidence.

## Validation

- All 2820 Debug-lane tests pass (`scripts/xcode-test.sh`).
- Codex grounded review: **PROCEED-AS-IS** (audits `docs/audits/2026-07-11-1317-grounded-review-r*.txt`).
- Runtime-verified live last session on built-in **and** Bluetooth routes (`capture_source=hal_device_input` confirmed on BT).
- Everything new is `#if DEBUG` — release builds are unaffected.

## Empirical finding this bench established

Today's build handles a dead mic **honestly but does not auto-recover**: Z1 → honest no-speech (no fabrication, next press works), Z2 → pre-death speech preserved, Z3 → self-heals in-session. It does **not** rebuild a fully-dead warm engine mid-session or tell the user — which is exactly what the #1317 fix adds.

Part of #1317.

author: ben-zene
body:
Surfaced by an adopter driving the on-device image tier hard (a text→image feature on `StableDiffusionBackend`). Two parts, one origin.

## Part 2 — byte-level Android download progress (implemented + device-verified)

`ai.ensureModel` reports one aggregate `bytesDone / totalBytes` bar. On Apple/desktop the per-file download has a byte callback, so it's smooth; on Android the download routes through the Kotlin `net.downloadFile` RPC (Swift's `URLSession` has no injectable CA store there), which was **request/response only** — so `ensureModel` could `yield` progress just once per file. For the ~2 GB LCM weights (5 files, a **1.7 GB UNet = 83%**) that froze the bar on the UNet — reads as a hang.

**Fix:** `net.downloadFile` gained an optional host-event `channel`; when set, the Kotlin read loop (already streaming bytes for the incremental SHA-256) pushes throttled ~1 MiB `{ bytesDone, totalBytes }` frames, and a new shared **`AndroidFileDownload.download(…)`** helper forwards them to the `ensureModel` stream — parity with the Apple/desktop byte callback. The three model backends (`StableDiffusionBackend`, `LaMaBackend`, `MobileSAMBackend`) now share that one helper instead of each hand-rolling the RPC. Reuses the host-event side-channel `GeminiNanoBackend` streaming already relies on; an absent `channel` keeps the old behavior (**backward compatible**).

**Verification**
- Swift Android cross-compile + Kotlin/Gradle `assembleDebug` clean.
- **Device-verified on a Galaxy Tab S10+:** a fresh ~2 GB LCM download emitted **1978 progress events** (1973 distinct byte counts) sweeping smoothly `0 → 2.07 GB` with **no per-file freeze** — vs the pre-fix **5 events** (one per file). Confirms the one new-risk aspect: `nativeHostEvent` firing from the `backgroundExecutor` thread delivers promptly mid-download.

## Part 1 — model/backend selector (proposal only, not implemented here)

Refines the proposal doc: the switcher is framed around **local + remote** backend switching (a remote API is just another `AIBackend`, routed by `request.model`); `AIImageModelInfo` becomes a modality-agnostic **`AIModelInfo`** whose `imageGeneration`/`imageEditing` bools become a **`Set<AIModelCapability>`** covering the standard multimodal spread (text / image / vision / audio); availability is an enum (`ready` / `downloadable` / `needsSetup`) rather than a `downloaded` bool; and `MultiModelImageBackend` is promoted from optional to recommended. No code in this PR — design for a follow-up.

## Docs
CHANGELOG (`[Unreleased]`), `docs/android-setup.md` (byte-level progress + shared helper), and the proposal doc (`Part 2 ✅ implemented`).

author: guuse
body:
## The bug you hit
Hosting on your PC: the timer was **instantly at 0** and you **couldn't click** answers, while everyone else was fine.

## Cause — clock skew
The question and countdown timers computed remaining time as `endsAt (server epoch ms) − Date.now() (your PC's clock)`, with **no offset**. If a client's clock runs a few minutes fast, every question looks *already expired* → the countdown shows 0 **and** the answer tiles are `disabled` (locked while "expired"). Players with correctly-synced clocks never saw it. This was the "no clock-sync channel" gap flagged during the build.

## The fix
- **Server** stamps every snapshot with `serverNow` (epoch ms).
- **RoomContext** derives `clockOffsetMs = serverNow − Date.now()` from each snapshot and exposes it.
- **Question** and **Countdown** pass it to the timer, so remaining time is computed against **server time** regardless of the local clock. (`useCountdown` already accepted `clockOffsetMs` — it just wasn't wired up.)

`shared`: `RoomSnapshot.serverNow`.

## Verification
A Playwright reproduction runs the host in a browser context with `Date.now()` forced **+5 minutes**:
- **Before:** would show 0 enabled tiles / instant timeout.
- **After:** 4 enabled answer tiles, and the host answers successfully (reveal shows **"Correct!"**, not "Too slow!").

Full build + socket smoke test green.

author: ginowine
body:
## Context

  Earlier during consultation testing we hit a white-screen crash when the citizen UI rendered a
  `LONG_TEXT` question whose `options` column came back as JSON `null`. The immediate fix was a client-side
   `q.options ?? []` normalization in `useConsultationQuestions`. This PR closes the actual gap and removes
   the workaround.

  ## What I found

  The write path was **already correct**. `service.normalizeOptions()` returns `[]string{}` (never nil) for
   every question created since the helper was added, so every write since that landing produces JSON `[]`
  in the jsonb column. I confirmed by scanning prod-shaped data locally:

  ```
       type      | total | null_rows
  ---------------+-------+-----------
   LONG_TEXT     |     3 |         1   ← the one culprit, from before normalizeOptions()
   YES_NO        |    17 |         0
   SINGLE_CHOICE |    17 |         0
   MULTI_CHOICE  |     1 |         0
   SHORT_TEXT    |    50 |         0
  ```

  The bug was **historical data + a soft schema contract**, not a live write path.

  ## What this PR does

  1. **`services/organization-service/internal/domain/models.go`** — strengthens the `Options` gorm tag
  from `type:jsonb;serializer:json` to `type:jsonb;serializer:json;not null;default:'[]'`. Comment explains
   the invariant: `normalizeOptions` is the single source of truth on write, and the schema tag reinforces
  it at the DB layer.
  2. **`services/organization-service/internal/consultations/consultations_test.go`** — new 
  `TestAddQuestion_OptionsAlwaysEmptySlice`. Table-driven, verifies SHORT_TEXT / LONG_TEXT / YES_NO all 
  round-trip with `Options == []string{}` (not nil). Locks the contract so a future refactor can't silently
   regress it.
  3. **`apps/web/src/hooks/useConsultations.ts`** — drops the `q.options ?? []` defense. API contract is 
  honest now; the defense would just hide any future regression.

  **+60 / −9** across 3 files.

  ## Deploy checklist ⚠️ 

  The gorm tag change makes AutoMigrate try to add `NOT NULL` + `DEFAULT '[]'` to an existing column. 
  **This fails on boot if the target DB has any lingering NULL rows** — Postgres refuses with:

  ```
  ERROR: column "options" of relation "consultation_questions" contains null values
  ```

  **Before deploying, run against prod:**

  ```sql
  UPDATE consultation_questions SET options = '[]'::jsonb WHERE options IS NULL;
  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM consultation_questions WHERE options IS NULL;  -- must return 0
  ```


  ## Deploy checklist ⚠️ 

  The gorm tag change makes AutoMigrate try to add `NOT NULL` + `DEFAULT '[]'` to an existing column.
  **This fails on boot if the target DB has any lingering NULL rows** — Postgres refuses with:

  ```
  ERROR: column "options" of relation "consultation_questions" contains null values
  ```

author: eswan18
body:
## Summary

Two OAuth2/OIDC correctness fixes at the token endpoint, both in `pkg/httpserver/oauth.go`:

### 1. Refresh-token rotation TOCTOU (security)

`handleRefreshTokenGrant` read the token via `GetTokenByRefreshToken`, validated it, minted new tokens, and only *then* revoked the old refresh token — via `RevokeTokenByRefreshToken`, which was a `:exec` query with no rows-affected check. Two concurrent requests presenting the **same** refresh token could both pass validation and both mint token pairs (a replay window), because nothing observed whether the revoke actually "won."

The authorization-code path already had the right pattern: `ConsumeAuthorizationCode` is `:execrows`, its `WHERE ... AND consumed_at IS NULL` clause makes the UPDATE atomic, and the caller checks the row count before issuing tokens (RFC 6749 §10.5).

`RevokeTokenByRefreshToken`'s query already had `AND revoked_at IS NULL` in its WHERE clause — it just needed to be observed. Fix:

- `db/queries/auth.sql`: changed `RevokeTokenByRefreshToken` from `:exec` to `:execrows`, with a comment documenting that callers must check the row count.
- Regenerated `pkg/db/auth.sql.go` (via `sqlc generate`, v1.30.0 to match the version already used in this repo) so the method now returns `(int64, error)`.
- `handleRefreshTokenGrant`: reordered so the atomic revoke happens **before** token issuance, gated on the row count. `rowsAffected == 0` means a concurrent request already consumed the token — return `invalid_grant` ("Refresh token has already been used") without minting tokens. A DB error still returns `server_error`. All prior validations (client match, expiry, deactivated user) are unchanged and still run before the revoke.

### 2. `invalid_client` returned 400 instead of 401 (spec)

RFC 6749 §5.2 requires HTTP 401 (with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge) when client authentication fails at the token endpoint. `/oauth/introspect` and `/oauth/revoke` already do this correctly for the same error code; `/oauth/token` and `/oauth/refresh` did not.

- Added `writeInvalidClientError`, which sets `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="oauth"` (matching the exact string already used by introspect/revoke) and returns 401.
- Updated both call sites (`HandleOauthToken` and `HandleOauthRefresh`) to use it in place of `writeTokenError(w, "invalid_client", ...)`.
- All other token-endpoint errors (`invalid_grant`, `invalid_request`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_scope`, `unauthorized_client`) are unchanged at 400.
- Updated the affected `@Failure` swagger annotations to split out the new 401 case.

### The two `RevokeTokenByRefreshToken` call sites

- `handleRefreshTokenGrant` (oauth.go): now checks the row count as described above.
- `revokeRefreshTokenIfOwnedByClient` (oauth.go, used by `/oauth/revoke`): updated for the new `(int64, error)` signature but intentionally ignores the count — per RFC 7009, the revocation endpoint always returns 200 regardless of whether the token was found/already revoked. No behavior change there.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go vet -tags integration ./...` all pass.
- `go test ./...` (non-integration) passes.
- Updated `TestClientCredentialsGrant_BasicAuth_WrongSecret` (`pkg/httpserver/client_credentials_test.go`) to expect 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="oauth"` instead of 400, since it exercises exactly the invalid_client-at-the-token-endpoint case.
- Added hermetic unit tests (`pkg/httpserver/token_error_test.go`) for `writeTokenError` (still 400, no `WWW-Authenticate`) and `writeInvalidClientError` (401 + header).
- Ran the full integration suite (`TestOAuthFlowSuite`, 90 subtests, real Postgres via testcontainers) — all pass, including `TestFullOAuthFlow`, `TestAuthorizationCodeCannotBeReused`, the full introspection/revocation suite, and the updated client-credentials test.

## Caveats

- `db/schema.sql` (gitignored, generated locally via `pg_dump` against a throwaway Postgres to regenerate sqlc output) is not part of this PR.
- No behavioral change to `/oauth/revoke`'s 200-regardless semantics.

body:
# Add local Qwen 3.5 9B agent and fine-tuning infrastructure

## Summary

This PR adds a standalone `qwen-spacetime-agent` project for running Qwen 3.5 9B locally through llama.cpp, recording tool-using trajectories in SpacetimeDB, and preparing reviewed trajectories for QLoRA fine-tuning and GGUF export.

## What changed

- Added a streaming TypeScript agent that calls an OpenAI-compatible llama.cpp endpoint.
- Added a calculator tool and a bounded tool-use loop with completion and failure handling.
- Added a SpacetimeDB module for jobs and ordered conversation messages, with reducer-based writes.
- Added lossless trajectory capture to JSONL for later review and training.
- Added a CRAFT/GitHub agent policy that requires read-only, schema-grounded tool use, concise decision summaries, and excludes hidden chain-of-thought.
- Added scripts to build and validate reviewed CRAFT training trajectories.
- Added a QLoRA training pipeline for `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, with 4-bit NF4 loading and LoRA adapters restricted to language-model projections.
- Added adapter merge, llama.cpp GGUF conversion/quantization, and local serving scripts.
- Added setup, usage, review, training, evaluation, and security guidance.

## Safety and data handling

- Training export is intended for reviewed completed trajectories only.
- Dataset validation rejects duplicate IDs, incomplete trajectories, malformed tool calls, unmatched tool results, unsupported roles, and hidden-reasoning markers.
- The checked-in configuration uses read-only CRAFT/GitHub behavior and requires final answers to be grounded in returned tool results.
- No credentials or generated training data are committed; local environment and output paths are ignored.
- SpacetimeDB tables are public for local development only and must be secured before remote deployment.

## Validation

- [x] `npm run check`
- [x] `python -m py_compile training/*.py`
- [x] `bash -n scripts/*.sh`
- [x] `git diff --check main...HEAD`
- [ ] Live llama.cpp inference and tool-call flow (requires a local model server)
- [ ] Live SpacetimeDB publish and persistence flow (requires the SpacetimeDB CLI/server)
- [ ] `npm run dataset:craft` (the reviewed raw five-run input is not included in this branch)
- [ ] QLoRA training and GGUF export (requires a suitable CUDA environment and llama.cpp checkout)

## Reviewer notes

- All branch changes are additive and contained under `qwen-spacetime-agent/`.
- The default model remains exactly `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`; the workflow does not silently substitute another model.
- Generated trajectories should be reviewed for correctness, sensitivity, duplication, and quality before training.
- Training and evaluation job IDs should remain disjoint.

author: new-usemame
body:
## What users see

With OpenID Connect login configured, the **classic** login page shows the admin-set **"Button label"** (e.g. *"Continue with Acme Identity"*), but the **new (SPA) login page showed the internal provider name** — `generic` — on the SSO button instead. This makes the two login surfaces disagree and shows users a meaningless internal name. Addresses #807 (reported by @thelastblt, on v4.1.9).

## Root cause

`cps/api/auth.py::_oauth_providers()` (which feeds the SPA login buttons via the public `/api/v1/auth/config` endpoint) built each button's `name` from `oauth_check[cid]`. But `oauth_bb.register_oauth_blueprint(cid, provider_name)` populates `oauth_check` with the **internal** provider name (`"github"`/`"google"`/`"generic"`) — not the display label. So the SPA rendered `generic` while the classic Jinja template (`login.html`) rendered the real label from `generic_login_button` (sourced from `OAuthProvider.login_button`). The React side (`Login.tsx`) already renders `{p.name}` faithfully — the wrong value was supplied by the backend, so no frontend change was needed.

Independently root-caused from scratch by two GPT-5.6 analyzers (Sol + Terra), both landing on the same cause with file:line evidence.

## Fix

- New single-source-of-truth helper `oauth_bb.generic_oauth_login_button()` resolves the admin-configured `OAuthProvider.login_button` (fallback `"OpenID Connect"`), used by **both** the SPA (`_oauth_providers`) and the classic page (`web.render_login`) — so the two surfaces can never diverge again. The classic path also becomes more robust: it now finds the generic descriptor by `provider_name == 'generic'` instead of assuming list index `[2]`.
- GitHub/Google buttons use a static label map (`"Login with GitHub"`/`"Login with Google"`) mirroring the classic template exactly.

## Security (unauthenticated endpoint)

`_oauth_providers()` feeds the **public** `/api/v1/auth/config`. The payload is built **explicitly** as `{id, name, url}` only — no ORM-row serialization, no dict spread/merge. `client_secret`, `client_id`, token/authorize/userinfo/metadata URLs, and every other OIDC field are structurally unable to flow into the response.

- Two new negative regression tests assert no secret material appears in the provider payload **or** the route body.
- **Live leak-scan** against the running endpoint (configured with `oauth_client_secret=acme-super-secret-807`) — no secret present; provider keys are exactly `["id","name","url"]`.

## Tests (red/green)

`tests/unit/test_api_v1_auth.py` — 4 new tests **fail on `main`, pass on this branch**:
- `test_oauth_providers_generic_uses_configured_button_label` — SPA generic button = configured label (was `"generic"`).
- `test_oauth_providers_generic_falls_back_to_openid_connect` — neutral fallback when unset.
- `test_oauth_providers_payload_never_leaks_secrets` — payload is `{id,name,url}` only.
- `test_auth_config_endpoint_never_leaks_oauth_secrets` — route body carries the label, never a secret.
- Updated `test_oauth_providers_maps_ids_to_urls_when_oauth` to assert the human labels.

On `main`, the route emitted `{"id":3,"name":"generic",...}` (the reported symptom). All 25 tests in the file pass on the branch.

## Live end-to-end verification

Built the image **from this branch** (`calibre-web-nextgen:807`) and ran an isolated container (`cwn-807`, port 8091) with a generic OIDC provider configured (label *"Continue with Acme Identity"*, a distinct secret):

- **SPA login (real built image), desktop + mobile (390×844)** — button renders **"Continue with Acme Identity"** (accessibility tree: `link "Continue with Acme Identity" → /link/generic`). Screenshots captured. Pre-fix this read `generic`.
- **Classic login** — same label, parity preserved, no secret in HTML.
- **`curl /api/v1/auth/config`** — `name` = configured label; leak-scan clean.
- **Reverse-proxy subpath** — `X-Script-Name: /books` → button url `/books/link/generic` (`url_for` honors the prefix).
- **Container logs** — no new ERROR/WARN/Traceback; fix held across a cold restart.

## Adversarial verification (CWNG_verify)

An independent fresh-context refuter (GPT-5.6 Sol) was tasked to **break** the fix against the live container across 4 lenses — secret-leak (incl. method/query-param fuzzing + `/ajax/oauth2/`), wrong-label, default-off/crash, classic-parity — and found **no break** on any. Combined with the two independent root-cause+security reviews, that's three independent adversarial passes plus the machine gates, all clean.

## `/security-review` note

The `/security-review` CLI could not execute in this run: it requires a git-repo working directory, but the change lives in a git **worktree** (`repo-wt-807`) while the harness cwd is the non-git parent dir. In its place, the auth/OIDC + secret-exposure surface received **two independent GPT-5.6 security reviews (Sol + Terra)** scoped explicitly to secret leakage, an **independent fresh-context refuter**, a **live leak-scan** of the real endpoint, and **two negative regression tests** — collectively stronger than a single automated pass. All found the payload structurally limited to `{id,name,url}`. Re-running the CLI from the worktree cwd before merge is welcome.

## Notes / deliberately left out

- The classic template's unreachable `else` fallback string (`"Log in with SSO"`) is now consolidated to the shared helper's `"OpenID Connect"`. This branch is dead code in practice (the generic button only renders when the provider is registered, at which point the real label/`"OpenID Connect"` is always returned), so this is a consistency improvement, not a behavior change users can hit.
- `"OpenID Connect"` fallback stays hardcoded English, exactly as the prior Python fallback was (not a regression; out of scope).

author: vxfemboy
body:
Closes #31.

The "bake" step after the eval topic-balance gate (#30): opt-in, `kirby build` flattens a skewed training set by **capping over-represented topics** — dropping each over-full topic's farthest-from-centroid rows using the existing `data/clusters.json` centroids. `eval`'s `max_topic_share` metric measures the imbalance; this reduces it.

## What's here
- **Layering refactor:** `assign_topics` + `load_clusters` moved from `eval.rs` to `cluster.rs` (their natural home), so `build` reuses them without depending on `eval`. Neutral warning copy; `eval` now reads `[cluster].out` instead of a hardcoded path. Pure move — no behavior change.
- **`src/rebalance.rs`:**
  - `topic_cap_drops` — pure core: for each topic over `cap`, drop the `(count − cap)` lowest-cosine (farthest-from-centroid) rows; sim-desc/index-asc tie-break; deterministic.
  - `rebalance_drops` — async, **Approach A**: loads the existing `clusters.json`, embeds the full written-train answers via the shared cache, assigns to nearest centroid, `cap = max(1, floor(max_topic_share × n_train))`, returns drop indices. Fail-soft on every path (rebalance off / no clusters.json / no embed backend / model or dimension mismatch / embed error → zero drops).
- **`[cluster]` config:** `rebalance = false` (opt-in — it deletes data) + `max_topic_share = 0.35` (the build cap, distinct from the `[eval.thresholds].max_topic_share` 0.60 gate; cap below gate so rebalancing makes the gate pass).
- **`build` integration:** rebalances train-only between curate and write, over the **full written train**. `clean` and `raw` are disjoint partitions concatenated by `write_split` (clean `clean_text`-ed first, then raw verbatim); the combined answer list is built in that exact order and text, and drop indices are split at `n_clean` to remove from each partition independently. Records `dropped_topic_rebalanced` in `stats.json`/`BuildStats`/the CLI summary. The end-of-build cluster auto-run then re-clusters the rebalanced train.

## Correctness (index alignment)
The 0..n index space stays coherent end-to-end: `train_answers` order = `write_split` order; `get_or_embed` preserves input order; `assign_topics`/`sims`/`topic_cap_drops` index 1:1; `retain` counters walk each partition and test the same combined-index drop set (clean `< n_clean`, raw `>= n_clean`). Embed text matches on-disk text (clean rows `clean_text`-ed, raw verbatim), so the cache hits and vectors share the centroids' space.

## Constraints honored
- **No new crate dependency** (`Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` unchanged) — reuses `cluster`, `vectors`, `embed`, `serde_json`.
- **Deterministic**, **train-only**, **fail-soft** (never aborts the build), **off by default**. First build is a no-op (needs a prior `clusters.json`; convergent over builds — Approach A; inline/hybrid deferred to #32).
- 272 tests pass; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; tests offline (pure core + fail-soft + relocation coverage).

## Process
Subagent-driven-development: 6 TDD tasks, per-task spec+quality review, whole-branch opus review (merge-ready, no findings). A design review before implementation caught two real integration bugs (clean/raw are disjoint partitions, not parallel; embed must use `clean_text`-ed answers) — both fixed in the spec before coding. Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-11-kirby-build-rebalance-design.md`; plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-11-kirby-build-rebalance.md`.

Follow-up: inline/hybrid centroids for first-build rebalancing (#32).

author: gardenbaum
body:
## Summary

Boosts coverage on `src/components/titlebar/WindowControlIcons.tsx` from **60% stmt / 50% fn** to **100 / 100 / 100 / 100** by adding a dedicated vitest file that exercises the four previously-uncovered `MacOSIcons` SVG wrappers (`close`, `minimize`, `fullscreen`, `maximize`).

## What this PR adds

A new file: `src/components/titlebar/WindowControlIcons.test.tsx` (170 lines, 8 tests). The tests follow the established `select.test.tsx` / `dropdown-menu.test.tsx` style — `render` / `container.querySelector` for SVG nodes, focused wrapper API assertions, no user-event. Each test renders one icon entry standalone with `aria-label`, `data-testid`, and `className` props, then asserts that the returned tree contains an `<svg>` and that the caller props were forwarded onto the SVG via the `...props` spread. The hard-coded `viewBox` is also re-asserted to confirm the icon's specific geometry is still rendered.

Coverage shape (each test matches one MacOSIcons entry):

| Icon | Covered in test |
| --- | --- |
| `MacOSIcons.close` | renders `<svg viewBox="0 0 16 18">` and forwards `aria-label`, `data-testid`, `className` |
| `MacOSIcons.minimize` | renders `<svg viewBox="0 0 17 6">` and forwards the same three props |
| `MacOSIcons.fullscreen` | renders `<svg viewBox="0 0 15 15">` and forwards the same three props |
| `MacOSIcons.maximize` | renders `<svg viewBox="0 0 17 16">` and forwards the same three props |
| `WindowsIcons.minimize` / `maximize` / `restore` / `close` | optional sanity coverage; SVG renders with forwarded props |

## Why the existing suite missed this

`MacOSWindowControls` only mounts `MacOSIcons.{close,minimize,fullscreen,maximize}` inside `isHovering` branches, and the integration tests query the buttons by role rather than triggering hover. So the icon wrapper functions never executed in the prior suite — that's why the row sat at 60% stmt / 50% fn despite having integration coverage for the buttons around them.

## Verification

```
$ bun run test:run -- src/components/titlebar/WindowControlIcons.test.tsx
  ✓ 8 passed

$ bun run test:coverage
  Test Files  108 passed (108)
  Tests       1229 passed (1229)
  WindowControlIcons.tsx |     100 |      100 |     100 |     100 |

$ bun run typecheck && bun run lint && bun run ast:lint && bun run format:check
  (all clean)
```

## Notes / pitfalls

- Test-only coverage boost. `src/components/titlebar/WindowControlIcons.tsx` is untouched.
- The icon entries are plain functions, not React components named with `PascalCase` — they're called as `MacOSIcons.close({...})` rather than `<MacOSIcons.close />` because they're stored as values on an object literal. TypeScript still infers the props from the `SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>` signature on each entry, so the call typechecks fine.
- Caller props are spread *after* the hard-coded SVG attributes, so forwarded props win on collisions — we don't assert the hard-coded `width` / `height` because the test props don't collide with them, but `viewBox` is verified because no test prop overrides it.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Erdős **#1038** concerns the extremal Lebesgue measure of the sublevel set `{x : |f(x)| < 1}` over monic real polynomials with all roots in `[-1, 1]`. The research file already proved the lower bound `2√2 ≤ sublevelSup'` (via the quadratic `x²-1`); the matching **sharp** upper bound `sublevelSup' = 2√2` is Tao's 2025 theorem and needs logarithmic potential theory absent from Mathlib.

This PR adds a **non-tight but fully elementary, machine-checked** upper bound `sublevelSup' ≤ 4`, confining the open extremal constant to a concrete finite interval `sublevelSup' ∈ [2√2, 4]` (`sublevelSup'_mem_Icc`) — so the faithful supremum is now provably finite with no potential theory.

## Mechanism

For a faithfully admissible `f` (monic, split, all roots real in `[-1,1]`), `f = ∏_{r ∈ roots}(X - r)`. For `|x| ≥ 2` each factor satisfies `|x - r| ≥ |x| - |r| ≥ 2 - 1 = 1`, so the product has `|f(x)| ≥ 1`:

- `one_le_abs_eval_of_ge_two` — `|x| ≥ 2 ⟹ 1 ≤ |f(x)|` (roots-product + `Multiset.one_le_prod`).
- `sublevelSet_subset_Ioo` — hence `sublevelSet f ⊆ (-2, 2)`.
- `sublevelMeasure_le_four` — `sublevelMeasure f ≤ vol(-2,2) = 4`, uniformly in `f`.
- `sublevelSup'_le_four` / `sublevelSup'_mem_Icc` — the supremum bound and the `[2√2, 4]` sandwich.

Helper `abs_multiset_prod` (`|∏ s| = ∏ |s|`) proved by multiset induction.

## Verification

```
$ ./bin/lake env lean Proofs/Erdos1038WIP01.lean     # EXIT 0, 0 sorries
#print axioms sublevelSup'_mem_Icc / sublevelSup'_le_four / one_le_abs_eval_of_ge_two
  -> [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]          # axiom-free
```

## Summary
Implements T1 from `pipeline/roamly-activities-mvp/product-tasks.md`: a new `activities-service` gRPC service that owns the activity catalog and answers scope+filter queries (`home` / `nearby` / `outside_country`), backed by Postgres+PostGIS. Adds the GO_STANDARDS-mandated `backend/shared/` scaffolding (errors, db, logging, config, models) since this is the first real service to need it.

## Acceptance criteria (product-tasks.md T1)
- [x] New service under `backend/`, follows GO_STANDARDS.md, registered in root `docker-compose.yaml`
- [x] Activity fields: title, description, category, location, country, price_tier, rating, image_refs, tags
- [x] Seeded catalog: ≥5 activities per scope, ≥4/6 categories
- [x] Single scoped query operation (home/nearby radius via `ST_DWithin`, outside_country via country mismatch)
- [x] Filters AND'd (category OR'd internally), unfiltered request returns all in-scope

author: daoyuanli2816
body:
## Summary

The 240s `stream_chunk_timeout` default added for #3189 (in #3195) is scoped to a class-path allowlist of `langchain_openai:ChatOpenAI` and `deerflow.models.patched_openai:PatchedChatOpenAI` only. Every *other* OpenAI-compatible provider in the repo subclasses langchain-openai's `BaseChatOpenAI` and inherits the very same `stream_chunk_timeout` mechanism, but is excluded by that string allowlist:

- `VllmChatModel`
- `MindIEChatModel`
- `PatchedChatDeepSeek`
- `PatchedChatMiMo`
- `PatchedChatStepFun`
- `PatchedChatMiniMax`

For these providers `_apply_stream_chunk_timeout_default` takes the "non-OpenAI" branch, which:

1. **never injects the 240s default** — they silently fall back to langchain-openai's aggressive built-in **120s** chunk-gap timeout (the exact value in the #3189 traceback), and
2. **`pop`s a user's explicit `stream_chunk_timeout` from `config.yaml`** with no warning — so a self-hosted user who sets `stream_chunk_timeout: 300` to survive long reasoning pauses has that override silently discarded.

Notably, #3189 was reported against **`mimo-v2.5`** (`model=mimo-v2.5` in the traceback), which maps to `PatchedChatMiMo` — one of the excluded subclasses. So the original fix did not actually cover the model the issue was filed against.

## What changed

`backend/packages/harness/deerflow/models/factory.py`:

- `_apply_stream_chunk_timeout_default` now gates on `issubclass(model_class, BaseChatOpenAI)` instead of the `_OPENAI_COMPAT_USE_PATHS` string allowlist, and receives the already-resolved `model_class` (rather than the config `use` string).
- Any genuine `BaseChatOpenAI` subclass now gets the 240s default when unset **and** preserves an explicit override.
- Genuinely non-OpenAI clients (e.g. `ChatAnthropic`, which is **not** a `BaseChatOpenAI` subclass) stay on the drop path: they don't declare the field and would divert it into `model_kwargs` and fail at request time, so the kwarg is still popped before construction.

`_normalize_openai_base_url`, `_enable_stream_usage_by_default`, and `_warn_unknown_model_settings` are intentionally left on their existing scoping — this PR only touches the `stream_chunk_timeout` heuristic. (`stream_usage` is already applied to all subclasses via the separate `model_fields`-based block further down in `create_chat_model`.)

`ChatDeepSeek` extends `BaseChatOpenAI` directly (not `ChatOpenAI`), which is why the gate targets `BaseChatOpenAI` rather than `ChatOpenAI`.

## Verification

Effective `stream_chunk_timeout` the constructed model ends up with, from the real `create_chat_model()`:

| Provider | before (unset) | before (config: 300) | after (unset) | after (config: 300) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ChatOpenAI` / `PatchedChatOpenAI` | 240 | 300 | 240 | 300 |
| `VllmChatModel` | 120 (langchain default) | 120 (override dropped) | **240** | **300** |
| `MindIEChatModel` | 120 (langchain default) | 120 (override dropped) | **240** | **300** |
| `PatchedChatDeepSeek` | 120 (langchain default) | 120 (override dropped) | **240** | **300** |
| `PatchedChatMiMo` | 120 (langchain default) | 120 (override dropped) | **240** | **300** |
| `PatchedChatStepFun` | 120 (langchain default) | 120 (override dropped) | **240** | **300** |
| `PatchedChatMiniMax` | 120 (langchain default) | 120 (override dropped) | **240** | **300** |
| `ChatAnthropic` (non-OpenAI) | not injected | dropped (correct) | not injected | dropped (correct) |

Tests (`backend/tests/test_model_factory.py`):

- New parametrized regression over all six subclasses asserting the 240s default when unset **and** that an explicit `stream_chunk_timeout: 300` survives.
- New end-to-end anchor that builds the real `PatchedChatMiMo` (issue #3189's model) and asserts the constructed instance's `stream_chunk_timeout == 240.0` — i.e. accepted as a real field, not diverted into `model_kwargs`.
- Reverting the factory change makes the 13 new subclass assertions fail (`PatchedChatMiMo` resolves to `120.0` instead of `240.0`); re-applying it makes them pass. The existing `ChatOpenAI` / `ChatAnthropic` cases were updated to resolve the real provider classes so the `issubclass` gate is genuinely exercised.
- `test_model_factory.py` + the provider suites (`test_vllm_provider`, `test_mindie_provider`, `test_patched_{deepseek,mimo,minimax,stepfun}`, `test_codex_provider`, `test_claude_provider_*`, `test_model_config`, `test_tracing_factory`, `test_lead_agent_model_resolution`, `test_scheduled_task_models`, `test_token_usage_by_model`): **245 passed**.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both changed files.

author: ibrahim-newaeon
body:
## TRUST-007 · per-tenant trust thresholds collected but never enforced

Onboarding collects per-tenant trust thresholds (`trust_threshold_autopilot`, `trust_threshold_alert`) and writes them to `tenant.settings` — but the trust gate **ignored them**. Every `TrustGate()` used the global defaults (`pass=70`, `hold=40`), so a tenant who set stricter or looser autopilot thresholds during onboarding had those values only echoed back on the dashboard, never actually enforced.

## Fix

- **`TrustGateConfig.from_tenant_settings(settings)`** — maps `trust_threshold_autopilot` → `pass_threshold`, `trust_threshold_alert` → `hold_threshold`; clamps to `[0,100]`, keeps `hold <= pass`, ignores non-numeric/bool values, and falls back to defaults for absent keys.
- **`trust_layer` `/trust-gate` endpoints** now build the gate via `_trust_gate_for_tenant(db, tenant_id)` (loads `tenant.settings`) instead of a bare `TrustGate()`, so `get_allowed_actions` / `evaluate` use the **tenant's own** thresholds.

## Verified against real Postgres (Docker)
- Factory unit tests: defaults, overrides, clamp to [0,100], `hold<=pass`, non-numeric/bool ignored, partial settings.
- `trust_layer` integration suite passes (15 total). mypy / black / ruff clean.

> **Follow-up (ML-06):** EMQ driver weights (`emq_calculation.py:110,169,…`) are still hardcoded per-driver — next step is a per-tenant weights map on `calculate_emq_score`.

body:
## Summary

- add one bounded, default-off pnpm content-addressable-store cache experiment to both Assurance Gate composite action entry points
- isolate cached content under the downloaded action checkout and key it exactly by OS, architecture, declared pnpm version, and lockfile SHA-256
- add a manual 5 cache-disabled + 5 exact-cache-hit GitHub-hosted comparison workflow, machine contract, semantic aggregator, Markdown decision surface, tests, and operator docs

Refs #3641
Parent: #3637
Follow-up to #3645

The cache remains `dependency-cache: "false"` by default in this PR. After merge, the manual workflow will collect the actual comparison. A final evidence PR will either make it default-on if all keep conditions pass or retain/restore default-off and record rollback/follow-up.

## Acceptance

- [x] Exactly one optimization is implemented: pnpm store caching.
- [x] Root and compatibility-subdirectory action inputs/outputs and cache behavior remain in parity.
- [x] Existing default-off consumer install behavior remains available; cache enablement does not change gate pass/block semantics.
- [x] Cache key has no moving branch component or restore prefix and includes OS/architecture/pnpm version/lockfile digest.
- [x] Cached path is action-local and excludes the shared global pnpm store, consumer/private dependencies, `node_modules`, core build output, evidence, decisions, and review surfaces.
- [x] Explicit restore/save completes before action-local store cleanup; frozen-lockfile validation remains enforced.
- [x] Manual report-only comparison uses fresh GitHub-hosted jobs, unique empty stores for five cache-disabled samples, and five exact-key-hit samples after an explicit seed job.
- [x] Action elapsed time includes setup, restore when enabled, install, build, gate, and review rendering; checkout/setup-node remains outside both modes.
- [x] Aggregation preserves functional/cache-miss diagnostics and recommends keep only for 10 passing samples, 5/5 exact hits, consistent runner/tool class, and >=20% median improvement.
- [ ] Hosted comparison and final keep/rollback decision: follow-up after this workflow exists on `main`.

## Verification

- targeted Vitest (`cache comparison`, `startup benchmark`, action runner, publish docs): 36 passed
- cache-comparison end-to-end synthetic artifact aggregation/schema/report test: passed
- targeted ESLint: passed
- `pnpm -s run types:check`: passed
- actionlint 1.7.12: passed
- schema ID policy: 96/96 compliant
- `pnpm -s run check:schemas`: passed
- `pnpm -s run check:doc-consistency`: passed
- `pnpm -s run verify:lite`: passed; 1365 pre-existing warn-only lint findings, 0 errors
- local cache metadata + isolated-store frozen install + core build smoke: passed; generated key `ae-framework-core-pnpm-v1-Linux-X64-10.0.0-<64-hex-lock-hash>`
- `git diff --check`: passed

## Benchmark method

`Assurance Gate Cache Comparison` is `workflow_dispatch` only and not a normal PR check. A seed job enables the exact action-owned key and explicitly saves the isolated store. Five cache-disabled matrix jobs set unique empty runner-temp stores. Five enabled matrix jobs depend on the seed and must report exact hits for the same key. Every measured job uses the same ref, Ubuntu runner image class, Node 20, pnpm declared by that ref, and `external-minimal-pass` fixture.

The timer starts immediately before `uses: ./.benchmark-action` and ends immediately after it. Therefore action package-manager preparation, cache restore, frozen install, core build, gate execution, review rendering, store save where applicable, and cleanup are inside the action boundary. Checkout, Node setup, fixture creation, and sample upload are outside it. The comparison report records per-sample environment/result/cache state and min/median/max/p90 totals.

## Rollback

Before the final decision, rollback is already the default: omit `dependency-cache` or set it to `"false"`. Reverting this PR removes the opt-in action surface, manual workflow, schema, and aggregator without changing current default action behavior. If the hosted result misses functional, exact-hit, or 20% criteria, the final PR will preserve default-off and remove or explicitly retire the experiment.

## Context Pack conflict

None. The optimization caches only dependency-store content and keeps action-ref/profile/schema/policy/core alignment, frozen lockfile enforcement, consumer evidence ownership, publication state, and claim boundaries unchanged.

author: weaversmask
body:
## Task

Item 2 of 3 of OPS-04 ([#15](https://github.com/WeaversMask/argus-oss/issues/15)) — second of the three-PR slice (maintainer decision 2026-07-08). OPS-04a = [#17](https://github.com/WeaversMask/argus-oss/pull/17); OPS-04c (mutation testing) follows.

## Summary

The package contracts upheld so far only by convention and review become mechanical: a new **`Architecture boundaries (dependency-cruiser)`** CI job cruises `packages/` against [.dependency-cruiser.cjs](../blob/ops-04b-boundary-enforcement/.dependency-cruiser.cjs). `packages/core/src` importing anything but `neverthrow` (Node builtins included), any deep import bypassing a package's public `exports` entries, or any violation of the one-way type-only-in-src `testing → core` edge now fails the build. This covers the year until Argus can scan itself — Phase-2 dogfooding reinforces, not replaces, it.

## Approach

Six forbidden rules:

- **`core-no-node-builtins`** + **`core-only-neverthrow`** — the zero-infrastructure guarantee. The neverthrow exemption is anchored (`node_modules/neverthrow/`) so lookalike names can't slip through.
- **`core-public-entry-only`** / **`testing-public-entry-only`** — per-package rules mirroring each package's `exports` map **exactly** (core: `.` → `src/index.ts`; testing: `.`, `./config`, `./setup`). A package's exports map and its rule change together; every new package gets its own rule (→ new-package checklist).
- **`no-cross-package-deep-imports`** — explicitly-commented coarse backstop for packages added without their own rule; dormant today.
- **`core-never-imports-testing`** — one-way edge, scoped `src|tests` so core's `vitest.config.ts → @argus/testing/config` dev edge stays sanctioned.
- **`testing-src-core-type-only`** — fakes import core types only (P1-02 convention); `tests/` may runtime-import core freely.

Key config choices: `tsPreCompilationDeps: true` (type-only edges are real boundary edges — tsc erases them; also what tags them for the type-only rule); excludes anchored to workspace paths (an unanchored `"dist"` silently dropped `node_modules/*/dist` edges — found by negative test); `exportsFields`/`conditionNames` tuned for the buildless `exports → src/` layout. Workspace symlinks realpath to `packages/...` natively in v18.

**Dependency (ADR-0003 dance):** `dependency-cruiser@18.0.0`, exact-pinned root devDependency. MIT (allowlist ✓), published 2026-06-25 (≥3-day age gate ✓), canonical maintainer `sverweij` ✓, pure JS — no `allowBuilds` prompts. `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` regenerated (379 pkgs); license gate green.

## Acceptance Criteria (issue #15, item 2)

- [x] Boundary rules run in CI (`boundaries` job; required-check wiring = same pending admin bucket)
- [x] `packages/core` imports nothing but `neverthrow` — mechanically enforced, negative-tested
- [x] No deep imports across package boundaries — per-package exports-map rules + backstop
- [x] `testing ↔ core` only via the documented peer edge — one-way + type-only-in-src enforced
- [x] Deliberate violation fails the build — **negative tests documented below**
- [x] New devDependency: full ADR-0003 dance done

## Testing

Negative tests (violation injected → `pnpm boundaries` → reverted; clean tree = 84 modules / 279 deps / 0 violations before and after):

| # | Violation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| NEG-1 | `import "node:fs"` in core/src | exit 2 — both core rules fire |
| NEG-2 | `import "vitest"` in core/src | exit 1 — `core-only-neverthrow` (initially **passed** through an unanchored `"dist"` exclude that dropped `node_modules/*/dist` edges — fixed, lesson recorded in config comment) |
| NEG-3 | relative deep import of a core port file from testing/src | exit 2 — deep-import + type-only rules |
| NEG-4 | `import "@argus/testing"` in a core test | exit 1 — `core-never-imports-testing` |
| NEG-5 | bare runtime `import "@argus/core"` in a fake | exit 1 — `testing-src-core-type-only` |
| PROBE-A (reviewer) | fake `neverthrow-extra` package imported from core/src | **0 violations before fix** → caught after anchoring |
| PROBE-B (reviewer) | type-only deep import of a non-exported `core/src/config.ts` | **0 violations before fix** → caught by `core-public-entry-only` |

- [x] Root gates green: format / lint / typecheck / build / test (159 tests, 100% coverage — no product code touched)
- [x] Reviewer verified mixed/split import-statement edge semantics safe (`dependencyTypesNot` never masked by a merged edge)

## Documentation

- [ ] `IMPLEMENTATION.md` — **deliberately untouched**: [#17](https://github.com/WeaversMask/argus-oss/pull/17) owns current tracker state (first-to-merge rule); OPS-04b entry lands on rebase after #17 merges
- [x] `HANDOVER.md` untouched (orthogonal to the P1 lane)
- [x] Docs delta: `docs/architecture.md` boundary-enforcement paragraph; `packages/core/README.md` boundary rule now cites CI enforcement
- [x] No ADR — enforces existing contracts (P1-02 decision, ADR-0004); no new architectural decision

## Notes for Reviewer

- Independent review pass (fresh-context **Sonnet**, cross-family): **approve-with-nits** with two live-demonstrated majors — the reviewer built probe packages/files and showed both holes empirically before any fix. Both fixed in `fix(boundaries)` commit, probes re-run and caught; re-review addendum in the packet comment below.
- `ci.yml` on this branch does not contain #17's `review-gate` job — the `boundaries` job is appended after `secret-scan` (file tail), a different region from #17's edits (trigger block + pre-`secret-scan` insert), so the two PRs merge cleanly in either order.
- When `@argus/ast` lands (P1-03), it needs its own `ast-public-entry-only` rule — flagged in the config comment, architecture.md, and the tracker's P1-03 entry (on rebase).

author: recursive-ai-dev
body:
🎯 **What:** The `hashlib.sha1` cryptographic hash function was being used for generating IDs in various places across the project. It has been replaced with `hashlib.sha256`.
⚠️ **Risk:** SHA1 is considered a weak cryptographic hash algorithm. Its continued use for ID generation could expose the system to collision attacks, making it easier for an attacker to craft a payload that resolves to an existing ID or impersonate generated data.
🛡️ **Solution:** The `hashlib.sha1` algorithm has been swapped out for the secure `hashlib.sha256` function for ID generation. All places where `hashlib.sha1` was employed have been updated consistently to maintain functionality without introducing regressions. Truncation logic (e.g., `[:12]`, `[:16]`) remains identical, ensuring there are no breakages caused by altered ID string lengths.

Files affected:
- `os/core/aios_ipc.py`
- `os/core/aios_core.py`
- `os/core/aios_memory.py`
- `os/scheduler/aios_scheduler.py`

author: naomiaro
body:
Adds musical (tick/PPQN) positioning to annotations, per-track lane label modes, and label-less region support — follow-on to the annotation web components epic (#455 / PR #607).

## What's new

- **`start-tick` / `end-tick` on `<daw-annotation>`** — authoritative when both are set, mirroring the clip `startTick` pattern. The `start`/`end` seconds attributes become a derived cache the editor keeps fresh (on connect, on updates, and whenever the engine BPM changes) — so BPM changes keep annotations on their bars while the list's times update. Everything time-domain (list panel, `playActive`, click-to-seek) keeps reading seconds unchanged.
- **Tick-native boundary editing** — core `updateAnnotationBoundaries` gained a units options parameter (defaults unchanged, non-breaking; existing tests pass unmodified). Keyboard nudges and drags on tick annotations run on integer ticks (min duration = a 128th note, `ppqn/32` floored at 1). Mixed tracks work: seconds neighbors are converted into the dragged annotation's unit space for link/collision math and written back in their own unit.
- **Snap-to-grid drags** — in beats mode, tick-annotation boundary drags honor `editor.snapTo` via core `snapTickToGrid`, same feel as clip drags (only the dragged edge snaps; linked neighbors follow by delta, clip-drag parity).
- **Grid-exact beats rendering** — tick annotations position with clip-identical math (`Math.round(tick / ticksPerPixel)`), eliminating the documented lane-drift limitation for tick-based annotations (it now applies only to seconds-based ones under variable tempo).
- **`box-label` on `<daw-annotation-track>`** — `text` (default, unchanged) / `id` (sonnet-style: id attribute or 1-based position in the bars, full text in the list) / `none` (bare region bars).
- **`name` on `<daw-annotation-track>`** — lane label rendered in the editor's controls-column sidebar row (mirrors `<daw-track name>`; empty default, zero layout shift).
- **Contractual blank-text + list-less support** — empty-text bars and tracks without a `<daw-annotation-list>` are now tested behavior; empty list rows show a muted placeholder.

## Demos

- `examples/dawcore-native/beats-grid.html` — bar-aligned, label-less tick region track ("Sections") with snap dragging.
- `examples/dawcore-native/sonnet.html` (new) — recreates the classic React annotations example (Shakespeare's Sonnet 1, aeneas data copied verbatim): ids in the bars via `box-label="id"`, full lines in the list.

## Testing

- Core: parameterized-units tests (defaults proven non-breaking — pre-existing suite unmodified); tick-space link/collision/min-duration coverage. 390/390.
- dawcore: 894/894 — tick attribute validation, derive-sweep loop safety (write-only-on-change, settles in one pass), beats geometry, tick drags with proven-discriminating snap/cancel tests (RED verified against pre-implementation code), mixed-track conversion, box-label modes, name labels, blank/no-list contracts.
- Real browser (headless Chromium, real input): beats-grid — grid-aligned regions, snap-to-beat drags, BPM change leaves `startTick` untouched while seconds re-derive; sonnet — select/seek/Enter-play-and-stop/text round-trip/linked drags. One real browser-only bug found and fixed with a regression test (native focus-before-click order poisoned the list row's click guard).
- Full sweep: `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck` 18/18, `pnpm -w lint` 0 errors.
- Final whole-branch review: 0 Critical / 0 Important; all unit-coherence/rounding/mid-drag-BPM seams verified.

## Release

Two patch changesets: `@waveform-playlist/core` (additive options + constants + optional AnnotationData fields), `@dawcore/components`. The React annotations package is untouched by this branch.

## Notes

- Variable-tempo tempo-map segment edits (callbacks mode) don't fire the BPM-derive sweep — documented nuance; re-derivation happens on the next annotation update.
- Refs #455 (epic follow-on). #477 (`<daw-player>` hosting) remains open.

body:
Closes #5.

## Problem

`nodus_mcp_aindy/` — the entire AINDY adapter layer — was excluded from the built wheel, because `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` only discovers packages under `where = ["src"]` and the package lived at the repo root. `pip install nodus-mcp` gave you the MCP wire stack but not the adapters, blocking `aindy-runtime`'s client-side MCP plugin which depends on `nodus_mcp_aindy` as a pip dependency.

## Fix

Option A (src-layout consistency): moved `nodus_mcp_aindy/` under `src/` via `git mv` (history preserved). No `packages.find` config change needed — `where = ["src"]` now discovers both packages. The adapter's internal imports are all relative, so nothing else changed.

- Bumped version `0.1.0` → `0.1.1` (`pyproject.toml` + `nodus_mcp.__version__`).
- Added CHANGELOG `0.1.1` entry.
- Hardened `test_version_is_not_dev`, which hardcoded `== "0.1.0"` (would break on every future bump). It now enforces the real invariant: a clean `X.Y.Z` release string, no `dev` suffix, in sync with `pyproject.toml`.

## Verification

```
python -m build
# inspect wheel:
OK: nodus_mcp_aindy is in dist/nodus_mcp-0.1.1-py3-none-any.whl
   nodus_mcp_aindy/__init__.py

author: andhus
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #154. With the blocking-fan-out model, a restart of the Modal build function (preemption, timeout, retry) loses every in-flight `worker.remote.aio` await: the resumed build re-executes all tasks whose outputs aren't written yet — including long-running tasks that are still happily running in live worker containers. This PR makes task executions independent of the orchestrator's lifetime.

## What changes

### Detached execution (SDK, generic)

- New optional executor surface on `TaskExecutorABC`: `supports_detached()`, `submit_detached()`, `reattach()` + a `DetachedHandle(executor, ref, wait)`; `RoutedTaskExecutor` forwards all three to the routed child.
- `build_aio` records each detached execution's `(executor, ref)` with the TASK_STARTED event *before* awaiting the result, and — on any build that (re)discovers a task reported RUNNING with a ref — asks the executor to **re-attach** instead of re-executing. A dead/expired ref degrades to normal execution.

### Modal implementation

- `ModalTaskExecutor` spawns workers as detached Modal function calls by default (`detached=False` / `Builder(detached=False)` restores blocking `remote` calls). Re-attach uses `FunctionCall.from_id` + `get(timeout=0)` to discriminate running (attach and await) / finished (resolve immediately) / failed-or-expired (re-execute).
- **Real cancellation**: in-flight function calls are tracked and `cancel()` now actually cancels them on Modal — FAIL_FAST and user cancellation previously left workers of a dead build running to completion.

### Registry API

- `POST .../tasks/{id}/start` accepts optional `executor` / `executor_ref` (event metadata + new denormalised `tasks.latest_executor`, `latest_executor_ref` columns; additive Alembic migration). A start without a ref clears a stale one.
- The slim bulk-register response (`?id_only=true`) now carries `latest_status` / `latest_executor` / `latest_executor_ref` per task, so a resumed build learns about re-attachable executions with **zero extra roundtrips**.

Liveness for re-attach comes from Modal itself rather than TTL leases — the lease machinery remains exclusively in the (opt-in) global concurrency lock.

## Backwards compatibility

- Custom `RegistryABC` implementations with the pre-existing `task_start` / bulk-register signatures keep working — refs are dropped gracefully (TypeError fallback, covered by a test).
- Old SDKs against the new API: unaffected (new params optional, new response fields ignored, columns additive). New SDK against an old API: response fields absent → no re-attach, behavior as before.
- Cross-build side effect (intentional): a build whose task is already RUNNING in another build now attaches to that execution instead of duplicating it.

## Testing

- `tests/test_build/test_detached.py` — engine mechanics with a fake detached executor: spawn+ref recording, re-attach, dead-ref fallback, status gating, spawn-failure, old-registry-signature compat (8 tests).
- `tests/test_integration/test_modal/test_detached_executor.py` — ModalTaskExecutor with faked Modal primitives: handle lifecycle, error wrapping, re-attach state discrimination, cancel (12 tests).
- **Live e2e** (`modal_live` tier, `test_live_detached_e2e.py`): a subprocess orchestrator spawns a 40s task, records the function call id, and is SIGKILLed; a resumed build re-attaches and the task's saved call id equals the pre-crash ref — the task was not restarted.
- Full suites green: SDK 653 passed, stardag-api 263 passed, live Modal tier 27 passed, migration upgrade/downgrade cycled, pre-commit clean.

## Resumo

Implementa o marco **M2 — API REST v1 de leitura** (SPEC 003 `api-rest-v1-leitura`): camada **FastAPI read-only** sobre o acervo do UFC já no Postgres, com 8 endpoints GET sob `/api/v1` e documentação OpenAPI automática (`/docs`, `/openapi.json`). Serve de contrato estável para a SPA (M3).

Pipeline `/implementar-spec` completa, **zero débitos**: 6 sprints em 4 ondas de paralelismo, cada uma auditada até `aprovado`; revisão consolidada final `aprovado`.

## Endpoints (todos GET, read-only)

| Rota | Descrição |
|------|-----------|
| `GET /api/v1/fighters` | Lista paginada, filtro `?name=` case-insensitive |
| `GET /api/v1/fighters/{id}` | Detalhe (404 se inexistente) |
| `GET /api/v1/fighters/{id}/bouts` | Histórico cronológico com stats granulares por luta |
| `GET /api/v1/fighters/{id}/stats` | Agregação **on demand** (nunca pré-agregada) |
| `GET /api/v1/events` | Lista paginada (mais recentes primeiro) |
| `GET /api/v1/events/{id}` | Detalhe com card de bouts (404) |
| `GET /api/v1/bouts/{id}` | Stats granulares dos dois cantos, de `bout_fighters` (404) |
| `GET /api/v1/head-to-head?a=&b=` | Confrontos diretos (422 `a==b`, 404 inexistente, 200 vazio) |

## Decisões load-bearing

- **Esqueleto reusável** (`mma_analytics/`): app factory, agregador `/api/v1`, `get_session` síncrona sem commit (read-only), envelope `Page[T]` com teto.
- **Granularidade inegociável**: estatísticas por luta via schema long `bout_fighters` (sem `OR` nos cantos); médias/contagens calculadas **on demand**, blindadas por teste-guarda (recálculo ao vivo + ausência de escrita + ausência de tabela/coluna de agregado).
- `source` propagado nos schemas de item. Exceção documentada: o agregado `FighterStatsOut` omite `source` (mistura origens kaggle/cito; não é registro de item).
- **FastAPI** adicionado ao stack (`uv add fastapi`, autorizado; `make security` limpo).

## CAs e qualidade

- CA-01 a CA-09 cumpridos (9/9). Contrato de 8 rotas GET coexistindo confirmado via dump do OpenAPI; API 100% read-only.
- **`make ci` verde**: ruff + mypy --strict limpos, **186 testes** (Selector + API contra Postgres real transacional, factories polyfactory), determinístico.
- Nenhuma migration (leitura pura sobre o schema M0).

author: vincentkoc
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`bin/ocm` supports callers that override `HOME`, but only inferred `RUSTUP_HOME` when Cargo lived under `~/.cargo/bin`. Homebrew installs Cargo as an external `cargo -> rustup-init` proxy, so an overridden `HOME` made rustup lose the installed toolchain and caused the wrapper and full test suite to fail.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Detect external Cargo symlinks whose target is a rustup proxy.
- Resolve the account home through `getent` on Linux or `dscl` on macOS.
- Keep account lookup best-effort so discovery failures fall through to Cargo instead of aborting the wrapper.
- Force the regression test through an external `cargo -> rustup` shim on every supported CI host.

This is intentionally separate from the OCM network/release performance work in https://github.com/shakkernerd/ocm/pull/4.

## User Impact

The development wrapper now works when tools isolate `HOME` on Homebrew rustup installations, while preserving the existing standard `~/.cargo/bin/cargo` path and explicit `RUSTUP_HOME` behavior.

## Evidence

- `bash -n bin/ocm`
- `cargo fmt -- --check`
- `cargo test --test bin_wrapper_tests`
- `cargo test` (full suite passed)
- Fresh branch autoreview: no actionable findings, correctness confidence 0.88

author: adamsned
body:
## What

WordPress named-encodes accented Latin letters, but `HTMLSanitizer`'s named-entity table (the DUT-550 recipe set) omitted them, so they passed through raw into blurb/article text. **Confirmed on live dutchovendaddy.com pages:**
- `garlic-butter-skillet-corn`: "sweet corn **sautéed** in butter" → app showed `sautéed`
- `dutch-oven-7-can-soup`: "Dutch Oven **Jalapeño** Poppers" → app showed `Jalapeño`

Accented words are everywhere in recipes (sauté, purée, jalapeño, crème, flambé…), so this was a broad, high-visibility defect — same rationale as DUT-550 (named fractions / degree signs).

## Fix

Add the common Latin-1 accented named entities (lower + uppercase for titles) plus the guillemet/prime marks seen on the same pages (`«` `»` `′` `″`). Numeric forms (`é`) already decode via `decodeNumeric`; this adds only the **named** forms — pure additive map entries, zero over-decode risk.

## Verification

Reproduced empirically first (scratch probe: `sautéed`, `Jalapeño`, `Éclairs` all leaked the literal entity), then fixed. **4 regression tests** added (live-page cases, common accented recipe words, uppercase titles, guillemet/prime). Full **DODSupport suite green (811)**; swift-format + swiftlint clean.

Found via the model-batch loop (B-iOS21), confirmed against live HTML. Closes DUT-961.

author: manojmallick
body:
Closes #480 (found during the full benchmark sweep).

## Root cause
The retrieval harness generates each cached repo's context with per-repo `CONFIG_OVERRIDES` (write config → generate → restore). The grounding benchmark regenerated the **same shared repos with a plain default config** and left the result behind — so any later suite reading contexts as-is saw degraded indexes: the callgraph A/B measured **32.2%** hit@5 (true ~87.8%), and the first retrieval regen after pollution came out one task low (86.7%) before stabilizing.

## Fix
- **`measureGroundingHermetic(dir)`** — snapshots every context artifact (all adapter outputs + `gen-context.config.json`) before its regen and restores them **byte-exactly** after measuring; artifacts that didn't exist before are removed. The benchmark's own measurement is unchanged (aggregate still 14.4%).
- The callgraph A/B now prints that it reads contexts **as-is** and points at the retrieval benchmark for canonical state.

## Verified (the issue's acceptance criteria)
- grounding → A/B back-to-back: **87.8% / 87.8%** — identical to A/B alone (was 32.2%) ✔
- grounding → retrieval first run: **87.8%**, no one-task transient ✔
- 3 regression tests (`test/integration/benchmark-isolation.test.js`): byte-exact restore of a sentinel context+config, cleanup of leftovers on repos that had none, artifact-list coverage ✔

Scripts-only change — the published package is untouched. Full suite **116/116 green** + unit pass; tests meta 122.

Supply-chain gate: local audit PASS (no shell spawns · no install scripts · main exports API · no fingerprinting · tarball 542KB/158 files).

author: jarbasal
body:
**dev is red** — two PRs landed in an order that collided.

The clade model (#280) forbids a spec from authoring a `family` string; it is derived from the parent chain. But the language stubs added in #272 still carried one **and had no parent**, so there was nothing to derive from. `test_family_is_not_authored_in_json` fails on dev.

## Fix

Give them the parent they were missing:
- **17 Austronesian stubs** → Malayo-Polynesian (`x-clade-mala1545`), the branch containing every Austronesian language outside Formosa.
- **6 Bantu stubs** → Bantu (`x-clade-narr1281`), within Atlantic-Congo.
- `gl-x-reintegrado` authored a family it can read straight off its parent (`gl`).

Their `family` now derives like everything else — e.g. `haw` → *Austronesian > Malayo-Polynesian*, `sn` → *Atlantic-Congo > Bantu*.

## Creoles keep an authored label — deliberately

A creole **does not descend from a single parent** — that is what makes it a creole. The family tree genuinely cannot classify one, so `ht`, `tpi`, `srn`, `bi` keep "French Creole"/"English Creole" and the test allowlists them **with that reason written down**. Deriving a descent for a creole would be inventing a line that does not exist.

## Test

`pytest tests/` → **22082 passed** (dev was red).

author: jojoneku
body:
## Problem

The automated `dev → main` promotion PR ([#465](https://github.com/jojoneku/nudgr-fasting-habit-app/pull/465)) was opened by CI but never merged, and sat open with all checks green.

**Root cause — a race in the promotion wait loop.** `promote_to_main` (and the two `promote_hotfix` steps) opened the PR, then polled `statusCheckRollup` for checks with a `null` conclusion, merging as soon as that count hit zero:

```bash
status=$(gh pr view "$existing" --json statusCheckRollup \
  --jq '.statusCheckRollup[] | select(.conclusion == null) | .name' | wc -l)
if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
  gh pr merge "$existing" --auto --merge ... || true
```

Immediately after the PR is created, its own `pull_request`-triggered checks haven't registered yet, so the rollup shows only the already-finished push checks. The loop reads "all done" and fires an immediate merge while the required checks are still **queued**. GitHub rejects it:

```
GraphQL: Repository rule violations found
2 of 2 required status checks are queued.
(mergePullRequest)
```

The `|| true` swallowed the failure, and because the `mergePullRequest` mutation failed, no auto-merge was armed to retry — so the PR was left open indefinitely.

## Fix

Poll `mergeStateStatus` instead of counting null-conclusion checks:

- `BLOCKED` while required checks are pending, `CLEAN` once they pass.
- An initial `sleep 20` lets the PR's own checks register, so the state isn't transiently `CLEAN` before they appear.
- Merge on `CLEAN`/`UNSTABLE`/`HAS_HOOKS`; bail out with an error on `DIRTY` (conflicts).
- Dropped `|| true` so a genuine merge failure surfaces instead of going green.

Applied identically to all three promotion steps (`dev→main`, `hotfix→main`, `hotfix→dev`).
