author: ishiland
body:
First tranche of fixes for the 2026-07-11 editing audit (#458).

## Changes

- **E-01 — geometry writes on projected-SRID datasets** (`features/service.py`): `ST_GeomFromGeoJSON` emits SRID 4326, but file-ingested layers keep their source CRS in `geom` (file-path ogr2ogr runs without `-t_srs`), so every geometry POST/PUT/PATCH on a non-WGS84 upload violated the column typmod and 500'd. The `geom` write is now wrapped in `ST_Transform(..., dataset.srid)`; `geom_4326` keeps the raw 4326 expression. `dataset.srid` mirrors `Find_SRID` on the live column via `refresh_dataset_metadata`, so it is the column's actual SRID.
- **E-03 — attribute-table inline edits** (`AttributeTable.tsx`, new `lib/attribute-values.ts`): the inline cell editor sent every value as a string, so edits to integer/numeric/boolean/date columns always failed with a generic toast. The drawing `AttributeForm`'s type mapping is extracted into a shared lib; cell values are coerced to the column's wire type, unrepresentable input is rejected with a type-specific message (new `editInvalidValue` key, all four locales), and the editor stays open on rejection.
- **E-05 — column DDL tile purge** (`layers/router.py`): add/rename/type-change/drop now call `tile_cache.invalidate_table` post-commit, mirroring the feature-edit path and the reupload swap. Previously stale MVT tiles served the old column set until TTL.
- **E-12 — column drop→re-add 500** (`layers/service.py`): `attribute_metadata` is unique on `(dataset_id, field_name)`, so re-adding a previously dropped column name hit `UniqueViolation` when `add_column` inserted a fresh row alongside the `is_current=False` history row. The historical row is now revived and refreshed (the audit had predicted a `MultipleResultsFound` at drop time; the regression test surfaced the actual failure at re-add).

## Impact

No schema, API-contract, or config changes. `openapi.json` unaffected (internal signatures only). One new i18n key in all four locales.

## Verification

```
cd backend && set -a && source ../.env.test && set +a && \
  uv run pytest tests/test_features_crud.py tests/test_features_geojson_z.py \
    tests/test_feature_geometry_limits.py tests/test_layer_column_ops.py \
    tests/test_attribute_metadata.py -q        # 96 passed
cd frontend && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test:i18n && \
  npx vitest run src/components/drawing src/components/dataset src/lib   # 212 passed
```

New regression coverage: EPSG:2263 POST/PUT/PATCH round-trips asserting `ST_SRID(geom)=2263` + `geom_4326=4326`; coercion unit tests; DDL tile-purge assertion across all four ops; drop→re-add→drop.

Remaining P1s (E-02 geometry validity, E-04 clear-to-null, E-06 saved-map dependency warning, E-07 e2e round-trips) tracked in #458.

author: n-ichimura
body:
## Summary

The lightweight Java hook for the predicate the built-in expression whitelist cannot express — a checksum, a code-format rule, a business-calendar check — without reaching for a full runtime extension. One SPI serves both asks: validation `rule:` expressions and every other place the expression language runs (2-way SQL `/*%if*/` directives, `requiredWhen`, notify `when:` guards, workflow guards).

- **`ExpressionFunction` SPI** (`tesseraql-core`, JDK-only so core stays dependency-free): `name()` / `arity()` / `apply(List<Object>)`, with a documented purity contract (side-effect-free, total, fast) — guardrail ch. 20.6 stays intact.
- **`ExpressionFunctions` registry**: an explicit `install(ClassLoader)` snapshot, deliberately not per-thread TCCL discovery, so hot-reload and worker threads always see one deterministic function set. Installation fails fast with **`TQL-SQL-2110`** on an illegal name, a built-in shadow, or a duplicate contribution — a broken function jar can never silently change what an existing expression means.
- **Parser**: unknown names and wrong arities stay parse/lint errors; an unknown call site now gets a dedicated diagnostic naming the modules channel. `Expr.Call` dispatches non-built-in names to the registry (all arities supported, nulls pass through) and fails loudly if the registry changed since parse.
- **Wiring**: `serve` installs from its composed modules TCCL; `lint`/`test`/`coverage` gain `--modules` and install via `CliModules.installAppExtensions` (a broken app still lints — modules just stay uninstalled); `mcp` installs from the app's declared modules; the lint/test/coverage Maven mojos install from the plugin classpath.
- **Security stance**: functions load from the reviewed, lock-pinned `tesseraql.modules` classpath only — deliberately **not** from signed `plugins/` (functions change lint/compile semantics, so they belong on the reproducible channel). `tesseraql admission` keeps lint-rejecting custom-function call sites: custom Java stays out of the declarative-only marketplace bar by design.

## Docs (site-covered)

- `declarative-validation.md` — new **Custom functions** section (SPI example, modules distribution, the three safety rules).
- `two-way-sql.md` — the `/*%if*/` expression paragraph points at custom functions.
- `admission.md` — the declarative-only stance now covers the expression language explicitly.
- `app-developer-distribution.md` (site-excluded, maintainer view) — `ExpressionFunction` joins the SPI list.
- `reference-error-codes.md` regenerated (TQL-SQL-2110). Docs-site builds clean locally (sync, completeness guard, links).

## Testing

- Core: registry validation (identifier/shadow/duplicate/negative-arity fail-fast, failed install leaves built-ins), parse+eval of 1/2/3-arity customs composing with built-ins, null passthrough, unknown-function diagnostics, stale-tree eval failure after reset.
- `ValidationRulesTest`: a custom predicate drives a `validate: rule:` end to end.
- `AppLinterTest`: the same app lints as unknown-function error without installation and clean with it.
- Full `mvn verify` green locally (Java 21). One unrelated flake observed and cleared on rerun: `InboxDeliveryIntegrationTest.anAddressedNotificationLandsRenderedAndReadStateWorks` (read-state count off by one under full-suite load; passes in isolation and on resume — candidate for a separate issue).

author: laolex
body:
## The bug

The event log's writer guarded the hash chain with a `threading.Lock` and an in-process cache of the tip hash. Both are per-process — and this system has always run more than one process on the log (the MCP server and a batch run are two). Two writers each read the same tip and each chained onto it.

**The result is not corruption.** Every event is present, nothing is lost, and each branch hash-verifies internally. The log simply contains *two valid chains*, and a linear walk misreports that as **tampering** — pointing an operator at an attacker who does not exist. Anchor it and you attest to one branch while the other sits in the log looking legitimate.

Reproduced 3/3. (It needs a barrier: without one, `spawn`'s slow import serialises the writers and the bug hides behind a false negative.)

## The fix

An advisory `flock` would prevent this only while every writer agrees to take it. The next one to forget forks the log again. So the tip constraint moved into the store:

```sql
prev_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
```

A second event claiming the same predecessor is **refused by the index**; the loser of the race retries against the new tip. `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` serialises writers so the race is rare, and the UNIQUE index is the airtight backstop for when it isn't.

This is not a new idea — it is the `UNIQUE(world_id, parent_hash)` that `@civ/history` already runs in production, ported.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| two processes × 25 events | **forks at event 1**, `verified: False` | 50 events, **one chain**, `verified: True` |
| a fork is… | detected after the fact | **impossible** — refused by a UNIQUE index |
| `explain(payout)` | full parse of the log | **0.7 ms** against a 3,000-event log |
| `fold_state()` | replay every event in Python | 4.4 ms, aggregated in SQL |
| a retried `emit()` | **records the event twice** | `idempotency_key` → returns the original |
| durability | `flush()` — page cache only | `fsync` per commit |
| diagnosis | `broken_at` only | tells a **fork** from an **orphan** from a **tamper** |

Verified by bypassing `emit()` entirely with a raw `INSERT` reusing a `prev_hash`: `UNIQUE constraint failed: events.prev_hash`.

**JSONL remains the archive and evidence format.** `export_jsonl()` writes it byte-compatible with every run in `runs/`, so replay, the console, and evidence export are unchanged. The database is the writer; the file is what an auditor reads. All 22 archived runs still verify (the 2 pre-hash runs remain unverified, as they should — nothing was retro-hashed).

## Also: the ablation numbers

The ablation table put a typical-run balance ($25,540) beside a ten-run mean stranded figure ($8,500), which reads as a discrepancy. Per run they reconcile as an **identity** — `gated balance = society balance + stranded`, every row. The full per-run table is now published so it can be checked.

And the strongest attack on the thesis is in our own data, so it is now stated rather than left to be found: run `20260711-181100` is the monolith's *worst* judgment run (72.2%) and the one the gate rescues *perfectly* — $0 stranded, level with the society. It approved almost everything, so it never wrongly rejected anything, and its 10 bad approvals were all mechanically forbidden. **On this benchmark, "rubber-stamp everything and let the gate sort it out" is optimal** — because our ground truth *is* the executable policy the gate enforces. That's a limit of the benchmark, not a virtue of the rubber stamp, and the judgment claim is bounded by it.

## Cost, stated plainly

`synchronous=FULL` fsyncs on every commit, capping writes at **~90/s**. Deliberate — a payout ledger that loses acknowledged events on power loss is worthless — and irrelevant at ~220 events per run. It would matter at thousands of payouts a second, and the fix there is batching commits per tick, not weakening the flush.

Still not claimed: multi-*host* writers (the store is single-node SQLite; the schema and the constraint port to Postgres unchanged).

## Testing

87 pass, 2 skipped. New regression tests:
- `test_two_processes_cannot_fork_the_chain` — two contending writers, asserts one verified chain **and that both writers exited 0** (a writer that dies mid-append loses events *and the chain still verifies*, which is the worst failure mode; my first cut of the fix did exactly that when `ROLLBACK` was called after `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` itself failed on a busy lock).
- `test_a_retried_emit_does_not_record_the_event_twice`
- `test_export_jsonl_roundtrips_the_chain`

Note: the suite only collects with `PYTHONPATH=src`.

## Summary

Reviewed error handling for spots where errors were discarded with `_ =` and either lost silently or could cause wrong-but-quiet behavior. Fixed the cases where discarding the error actually matters; left the intentional best-effort patterns alone (scraper `continue`-on-parse-error loops, and the `router_responses.go` JSON shapers that AGENTS.md documents as deliberately lenient).

Changes:

- **`store.LoadJobChapters`** — a corrupt `job.ChapterIDs` JSON blob was swallowed (`_ = json.Unmarshal(...)`), leaving `ids` empty so the job silently selected **zero** chapters instead of erroring. Now propagates:
  ```go
  if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(job.ChapterIDs), &ids); err != nil {
      return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("parse job chapter ids: %w", err)
  }
  ```
- **`UpdateNovelCheckResult` / `UpdateChaptersStatusFast`** — three `_ = s.Store.Update...()` call sites (`runtime_worker.go` check job, `router_import.go` update-preview + batch-check, batch-translate) discarded DB write errors even though the surrounding code logs every other update failure with `slog`. Now each logs a `slog.Warn` on error (kept non-fatal: these are secondary/cached side effects, so the primary response still succeeds).
- **epub cover read** (`router_epub_export.go`) — `coverBytes, _ = epubexport.ReadCloserToBytes(reader)` swallowed the read error and then ran `DetectImageMime` on possibly-empty bytes. Now only sets bytes/mime on success and logs a warning otherwise.

No behavior change on the happy path; failures that were previously invisible now either propagate (job chapter parse) or get logged.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -short ./...` pass.

## Summary

Fixes #243 — the bookmark target picker (`BookmarkTargetPickerSheet`) had no row representing the bookmarks root (`parentID == nil`), so in a wiki with zero folders the user was forced to create a folder before they could confirm "Add", even though the data model already supports root-level bookmarks.

## Changes

- **Added a pinned "Bookmarks" root row** at the top of the folder list in `BookmarkTargetPickerSheet`, selectable like any folder row. Selecting it means "bookmark to the top level" (`parentID = nil`).
- **Pre-selected root on appear** so the "Add" button is enabled immediately in an empty wiki — no forced folder creation.
- **Sentinel-based selection**: used a constant `__bookmarks_root__` to distinguish "root selected" from "nothing selected" (both were `nil` before), converted back to `nil` in `onConfirm` via a testable static method `parentID(forSelection:)`.
- **Added `BookmarkTargetPickerSelectionTests`** covering the sentinel-to-nil conversion (root sentinel → nil, real folder ID → passthrough, nil → nil, empty string → passthrough).

## Before / After

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Empty wiki, open picker | "No folders yet — create one below." Add disabled | "Bookmarks" root row pre-selected, Add enabled |
| Wiki with folders | Root not offered as destination | Root row pinned above folder list |
| Selecting root then confirming | N/A (impossible) | `onConfirm(nil)` → bookmark created at top level |

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build` passes
- [x] `swift test --filter BookmarkTargetPickerSelectionTests` — 4 new tests pass
- [x] `swift test` (fast tier, 2191 tests) — all pass
- [ ] CI green

Closes #243.

author: byrongamatos
body:
> Stacked on #901. `lib/demo_mode.py` (342). **`server.py` 1,870 → 1,649.**

The read-only request guard (its 96-entry blocked-route table + the middleware) and the hourly session janitor (registry, hook runner, thread). Bodies **verbatim**.

## The middleware needs `app`, so the module takes it

`_demo_mode_guard` is an `@app.middleware("http")` and cannot exist without an app object. Rather than have a module under `lib/` reach for a global, it exposes `install(app)` and **server.py — which owns the app — hands it over.**

The janitor is symmetrical: `start_janitor()` / `stop_janitor()`, called from server.py's startup and shutdown hooks, where the process lifecycle actually lives.

## `register_demo_janitor_hook` is part of the plugin contract

It's a key in `plugin_context`, so plugins hold it as a **live reference** from `setup()`. server.py imports this exact object and puts it in the dict unchanged — identity preserved, and `tests/test_plugin_context_contract.py` (#898) fails if that ever stops being true.

**This is the first carve that guard has actually protected.**

## `stop_janitor()`'s order is load-bearing

The obvious way to write it — clear the "started" flag, then join — is **wrong**, and I wrote it that way first. server.py's original deliberately returns *early*, leaving `_DEMO_JANITOR_STARTED` True **and the thread handle intact**, when the thread outlives the join:

```python
# Leave _DEMO_JANITOR_STARTED True so a new janitor is not
# spawned by a subsequent startup while the old one is alive.
```

Clearing the flag first quietly reintroduces exactly the double-janitor leak the flag exists to prevent. Preserved byte-for-byte, and the reason is now written down *at the function* rather than only at its single call site.

## A bug moved verbatim, on purpose

```python
if getenv_compat("FEEDBACK_DEMO_MODE") or getenv_compat("FEEDBACK_DEMO_MODE") == "1" \
        and not _DEMO_JANITOR_STARTED:
```

`and` binds tighter than `or`, so this is `A or (B and C)` — **the not-already-started re-entry guard is dead** whenever the env var is truthy, which is the only case that runs. A second startup leaks a janitor thread (the handle is overwritten, so shutdown joins only the last).

Verified, preserved exactly, and filed as **#902**. A carve whose whole value is being provably behaviour-neutral is not the place to change behaviour.

## pyflakes

Three more missing imports caught on the way in (`uuid`, `warnings`). Five carves, **ten missing imports**, every one a `NameError` on a live path.

pytest **2399** · pyflakes **0** · Codex **0**.

## Summary

Adds four committed PROCESS skills under `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, capturing recurring engineering workflows mined from the repo's issue/PR history so the knowledge is durable and versioned rather than living only in closed issues. Each skill is a YAML-frontmatter (`name` + when-to-use `description`) doc whose body encodes the procedure, with the source issue/PR numbers cited as evidence.

Step 9 of 11 of Epic #620.

## Related

- Closes #629
- Part of #620

## Changes

- `bug-audit-epic` — running a codebase/subsystem bug audit: orthogonal parallel investigators, adversarial verification of every Medium+ finding, standard bug-issue body, severity-grouped `[Epic]` with an "Areas verified clean" section and linked sub-issues (sources: #493, #543, #570; body template #545).
- `bug-fix-pr` — executing one filed bug as a PR: reproduce from the Failure-scenario section, fix at the cited site, regression-test at every layer the three-layer rule names, run the gates, Verification section with real output (sources: fix-PR waves #363–#408, #494–#517, #571–#613; #417/#606/#607; #231/#619).
- `feature-epic-breakdown` — planning a multi-PR feature: design-complete epic body, layer-ordered standalone sub-issues with DELETE/ADD/MODIFY tasks and dependencies, integration branch when needed, verbatim context-isolated-review clause (sources: #451/#452–457, #419, #410).
- `docs-audit` — keeping docs in sync: sweep tables/env-vars/paths vs implementation, current-state-only reference bodies, identical terminology across CLI/README/GUI, README aqua section tracked against the external aqua-registry (sources: #448/#442, #544, #245/#461/#614, #409/#412).

Skill bodies are written in current-state-only prose; every cited number was re-verified with `gh issue view` / `gh pr view` (no transposed numbers). The AWS e2e gate is referenced as `mise e2e-aws` per the #629 spec (its post-rename name from Step 3 / #623).

## Verification

```
$ ls .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/bug-audit-epic/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/bug-fix-pr/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/docs-audit/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/feature-epic-breakdown/SKILL.md
```

- All four frontmatter blocks are valid single-line-scalar YAML with `name` + when-to-use `description`.
- These are Markdown skills (not Go-linted); they load as available project skills in a fresh Claude Code session.
- A context-isolated review subagent verified spec fidelity, all cited numbers, and the current-state-only rule — no defects found.

body:
## 개요

M2(모노레포) 최종 whole-branch 리뷰가 비차단으로 분류한 follow-up을 정리한 **M2.1 하드닝**입니다. 기능 추가가 아니라 견고성·정합성·테스트 커버리지·문서 보강입니다.

## 변경

- **H1 — manifest 게이트 정렬 + validate 규칙**
  - `changed-packages.py`의 배포 조건을 `repo.kind == "monorepo"` → `repo.monorepoStrategy == "independent"`로 정렬(모노레포 변형 스킬과 동일 조건). 결과: **fixed** 모노레포에서 불필요하게 복사되던 dead file 제거.
  - `render.py`의 `validate_config`에 규칙 추가 — `monorepoStrategy`가 설정됐는데 `kind`가 monorepo가 아니면 exit 1. `{kind:"app", monorepoStrategy:"independent"}` 같은 손편집 config가 만드는 broken toolkit 경로를 차단.
- **H2 — `changed-packages.py` 회귀 테스트 3건**(소스 무변경): `tag.enabled=false`→`anchor.value` 분기, sibling-prefix 비충돌(`packages/a` vs `packages/ab`), git 명령 실패→exit 2.
- **H3 — scan glob 시맨틱**: `_node_packages`에 `/**`·`/*`·리터럴 경로 처리 주석 추가 + `/**`·리터럴 경로 분기 테스트 2건.
- **H4 — 문서**: `references/monorepo.md`에 "노트 설정은 전 scope 공통(M2)" 가정을 명시.

## 검증

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → **98개 통과** (M2 90 + 신규 8)
- `claude plugin validate . --strict` → 통과

author: syamaner
body:
## Summary

Refs #499. Codex posted three P2 inline threads on the merged #503 (the
joint-drop-window teaching + DTR window context field). All three verified
against the actual code first — all three confirmed REAL, none were false
positives — and fixed. This PR lands before the promotion slice so the
default prompt stack ships internally coherent.

## The three findings

**1. "DIFFERENT numbers" claim was false in a common case.** Verified:
`RoastControlPolicy._bitter_ceiling_temp_c()` caps the told bitter ceiling to
`profile.target_drop_temp_c` whenever that target is at/below the hard
ceiling (`min(196, 195) == 195`), so the advisor's context can legitimately
carry an identical target and ceiling. Fixed: the section now teaches the
MEANING differs regardless of whether the values coincide, and anchors the
always-numerically-distinct claim to `emergency_drop_temp_c` instead (never
capped by the profile; a validator pins it strictly above the bitter
ceiling).

**2. c2's "NEVER overshoot the drop target... LATEST acceptable drop"
directly contradicted the joint objective in the fully assembled c3/c6
prompt.** Verified via string-index comparison on the actual assembled text:
c2 splices onto c1 at the same anchor point as #499's new section, and its
contradicting text lands textually AFTER the joint-objective section — a
later-spliced section reading as an override of an earlier one. Fixed:
reworded c2's guard to target the BITTER CEILING specifically (still
genuinely law, unaffected by #499) rather than the drop-TEMPERATURE target
(which #499 now teaches may be modestly overshot). Audited c3/c4/c5/c6's own
added sections for the same class of bug — no other contradictions found;
their convergence language ("arrive together") already agreed with the new
teaching.

**3. Swapped DTR-window judgment-space examples.** Verified the clauses were
backward (under-DTR ⇒ development is what's still closing; over-DTR-while-
temp-short ⇒ temperature is what's still closing) — cross-checked against
the section's own already-correct earlier paragraph. Fixed: flipped both
clauses.

## A fourth finding — my own follow-up fix introduced a new false claim

**Safety-reviewer LOW on the first follow-up commit (9801588):** fixing
finding 1's false "always different" claim introduced a new false
relational claim — "(never below the target)" — which is itself false
whenever `target_drop_temp_c` is ABOVE the hard bitter ceiling (an unbounded
profile field; this repo's own `test_advisor.py` `PROFILE` fixture is
`target_drop_temp_c=205.0`, above the 196.0 default, so the resolved ceiling
is 196.0 — BELOW the target). Fixed per the reviewer's instruction: dropped
the relational claim entirely, keeping only the meaning-distinction and the
provably-always-true emergency-anchor sentence.

## Pre-open review

**Pre-open review: 1 low found and folded.** Everything else confirmed by
the safety reviewer: c2's rewording is consistent with the deterministic
layer and non-weakening; the new assembled-text tests are non-vacuous
(verified to fail on `origin/main`); zero digits holds in the section; no
new control authority introduced anywhere.

## Test class added

Per the reviewer's requirement, two new tests assert on the FULLY ASSEMBLED
`c3`/`c6` prompt text (not just the `c1` fragment) — the class of bug that
made finding 2 possible in the first place: fragment-level tests are
structurally blind to a contradiction introduced by a LATER splice. A third
new test renders the REAL resolved control box
(`RoastControlPolicy(SafetyLimits(), PROFILE).limits_for(DEVELOPMENT)`) for
a target-above-ceiling profile and confirms the prompt makes no ordering
claim that profile would falsify. A `docs/recent-fixes.md` entry records
this test-class gap as a reusable lesson for future prompt-splice changes.

## Deterministic paths — unchanged

No production logic touched anywhere in either follow-up commit —
`models.py` / `controller.py` are untouched; this is prompt-text-only plus
tests plus the docs entry.

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` — clean
- [x] `pyright` (strict) — 0 errors
- [x] `pytest` — full suite green
- [x] `pytest --cov=roastpilot_agent --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing`
      — every changed line/branch covered
- [x] Two pre-existing tests updated to match corrected wording (one had
      been asserting the exact buggy phrase existed — updating it removes
      the defect, not a regression)
- [x] Five new tests for the three Codex findings (swapped-example fix +
      two assembled-text consistency tests, parametrized over `c3`/`c6`)
- [x] Two new tests for the safety-reviewer LOW (the strengthened
      distinguishing test + the real-profile ordering-claim regression)

`src/roastpilot_agent/advisor.py`, `tests/test_advisor.py`).

author: lifestyle3nergy-web
body:
# Pull Request

## Summary

Implements the first concrete slice of the KAI-OS handover: the **Cognitive Cycle engine** modelling the OUR operational loop `Observe → Understand → Respond` as a DI-registered platform service.

The engine is a thin orchestrator over three replaceable collaborators, so reasoning strategies can evolve without rewriting control flow:

```ts
interface Observer<TSignal>      { observe(input): Observation }
interface Interpreter<TSignal,I> { understand(obs): Understanding }
interface Responder<I,TAction>   { respond(u): CycleResponse }

new CognitiveCycleService({ observer, interpreter, responder, logger? })
  .run({ signals, metadata }) // -> CycleResult (with timings + full evidence)
```

Error handling is first-class (aligns with the broader error-propagation work): any phase failure is wrapped in a `CognitiveCycleError` that records the failing `phase` and preserves the original `cause`, is logged (not swallowed), and re-thrown — callers never receive a partial/misleading result.

Ships baseline collaborators (`PassthroughObserver`, `EchoInterpreter`, `NoopResponder`) so a working default `CognitiveCycleService` is registered in `Bootstrap` out of the box and is ready to be swapped for richer strategies.

New files under `src/services/cognitive/`:
- `types.ts` — phase enum, cycle contracts, structural `CycleLogger`
- `CognitiveCycleService.ts` — orchestrator
- `CognitiveCycleError.ts` — phase-aware error wrapper
- `defaults.ts` — baseline phase collaborators
- `index.ts` — barrel

## Related Issue

Closes #

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project standards.
- [x] I have tested my changes.
- [ ] I have updated documentation where necessary.
- [x] I have verified there are no unnecessary files included.
- [x] I have reviewed my own changes.

## Additional Notes

- 8 new tests in `tests/services/CognitiveCycleService.test.ts` (vitest); full suite passes (60 tests) and `npm run lint` is clean.
- This PR is intentionally scoped to the Cognitive Cycle slice. The full KAI-OS monorepo architecture (packages/*, agent packages, frontend, Docker/K8s, Python knowledge scripts) is a separate, larger effort.
- Local note: vitest's `rolldown` native binding (`@rolldown/binding-linux-x64-gnu`) was not installed by `npm ci` due to a known npm optional-deps bug; installing it manually made the suite run. Not committed — flagging for the environment/blueprint.

author: sudo-kaneki
body:
## Summary

Replaces the al-folio academic template with an owned "retro-modern" design system, and rebuilds the site around the four assets that were actually mine. The rest of al-folio's content turned out to be demo boilerplate.

**Four routes** — `home`, `cv`, `projects`, `blog` — down from eleven.

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSS | ~500 KB (Bootstrap + MDB) | 14 KB |
| Published site | ~36 MB | ~210 KB |
| Jekyll plugins | 19 | 7 |
| Layouts / SCSS partials | 13 / 13 | 4 / 5 |
| Frameworks | Bootstrap, jQuery, MDB | none |

`_site` was shipping 26 MB of al-folio's demo **videos**.

## `cv.yml` is now the single source of truth

One file drives **three** outputs — the `/cv/` page, the homepage timeline, and the RenderCV PDF. Career history can no longer drift between them. `_pages/cv.md` iterates the sections rather than hardcoding them, so adding a section to `cv.yml` appears everywhere with no template change.

## Bugs fixed along the way (all pre-existing)

- **The build has been broken since `9419b99`.** `website:` was added to `_data/socials.yml`; `jekyll-socials` didn't recognise the key and crashed every build. **GitHub Pages has been serving a stale site ever since.** This PR is what unbreaks the deploy.
- **The CV silently lost data.** Entry types were identified by guessing which fields were present, so a publication with no `authors` rendered with an *empty title*. Publication authors were never printed at all. Now branches on an explicit `kind`.
- **`design.yaml` was never applied** — not locally, not in CI. `settings.yaml` declares `render_command.design`, but RenderCV ignores it (a bogus key raises no error). The phone rendered as `054 521 5572`, dropping the country code. `render-cv.yml` now passes `--design`/`--locale-catalog` explicitly.
- **The download button served a stale, hand-uploaded PDF**, not the one RenderCV generates from `cv.yml`.
- **The RSS feed was titled "blank"** (al-folio's placeholder `site.title`, read only by `jekyll-feed`).
- **The email shipped as scrapeable plaintext** despite `jekyll-email-protect` being installed and unused.
- **`purgecss` would have broken production**: it strips classes it can't find in the HTML, and the theme-toggle and blog-filter classes exist only in JS. Removed.

## Accessibility

Blog filter re-done as `role="group"` + `aria-pressed` (it claimed `role="tablist"` with no tabpanel, no `aria-controls`, and no arrow-key handling). Skip link now actually moves focus. All colours checked against WCAG AA in **both** themes. Motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Design contract

`_sass/_tokens.scss` is the **only** file permitted to hold a literal colour, size, or font. Everything else uses `var(--token)`.

Retro cues: `--radius: 0`, visible 1px borders, hard offset shadows (never blurred), hover states that translate 2px so buttons depress like keys. Dark by default, light fully supported.

## Deliberately deferred

- **Pixel font.** `--font-display` / `--font-body` are the swap point. `AGENTS.md` records that a bitmap font also needs `--fw-display: 400` (pixel fonts have one weight; faux-bold smears the grid) and a type scale re-pitched to multiples of 8px.
- `_data/projects.yml` is empty and the blog has no posts. Both homepage blocks hide themselves until filled.

## Verification

Build green. Prettier clean. All four routes render. 25 CV entries, 5 timeline entries. No horizontal overflow at 375 px. Both themes checked. `Gemfile.lock` is now committed and its `PLATFORMS` includes `x86_64-linux`, so CI resolves.

> ⚠️ On merge, `render-cv.yml` fires (it triggers on `_data/cv.yml`) and will commit a regenerated PDF back to `main`. Expected — it should be byte-identical to the one committed here.
